progress: Old Bristle beds in the south-east meadow of the Caerdun Fields, where the grass meets the pines. Hunt him and bring me his hide so I can see it with my own eyes.
complete: That hide is older than my marriage. Hang it in the barn; the young boars will smell it and think twice before they come near the rows.
Take this. It was my father's hunting ring, and he hunted this ground before me. Ten years of waiting, and it took a stranger to finish it. I will not forget that.

s_cf_4.name: Forged Papers

objective.label: Take 2 Forged Charter papers from the beacon jackdaws' nests on Beacon Knoll in the Caerdun Fields

s_cf_4.desc: Watchman Dorran at the Landward Gate wants two forged charter papers from the beacon jackdaws' nests on Beacon Knoll, north-east of Milestone Zero in the Caerdun Fields, so the wall learns what a forgery looks like.
offer: Out or in? Either way, mind the road. I am Dorran; I keep the Landward Gate, Caerdun's east gate, the one that opens onto the Fields.

Here is the trouble. The jackdaws that nest on Beacon Knoll carry off anything with a seal on it, and half of what is in their nests is forgery: freebooter paper. Freebooters are the unchartered, people who mean to dig and trade in the interior without a court's licence. They draw a court seal by guesswork and try it on my gate, and not one of those papers has ever got past me.

I want two of those forged charter papers out of the nests, for Gate-Sergeant Ottey at the drill yards, so every post on the wall knows what to look for. The knoll is north-east of here, past Milestone Zero toward the North Road. Drive the jackdaws off their nests and take what they have hoarded. The wall will pay what it can.
progress: Two forged charter papers from the beacon jackdaws' nests. Beacon Knoll is north-east of Milestone Zero, toward the North Road, in the Caerdun Fields.
complete: Look at that seal. A child could have drawn it, and probably did. These go to Gate-Sergeant Ottey, and by tonight every post on the wall knows the difference between a court's seal and a jackdaw's.
The wall thanks you. The wall does not pay well, but here, a hi-potion from the gate's own stores.

s_hf_1.name: Feathers for the Fletcher

objective.label: Bring Charcoal-Master Dask 5 wood hen feathers

s_hf_1.desc: Charcoal-Master Dask at the Charcoal Camps owes a city fletcher a favour and wants five hen feathers from the wood hens in the east of the Heartwood Fields, between the camps and Heartwood's west gate, to settle it.
offer: Dask. Charcoal-master. These camps burn charcoal for Heartwood's forges, three carts a week, and the smoke you saw from the road is us. Mind the clamps as you walk; they're hot under the turf.

Here's my trouble. The fletchers in the city buy hen feathers by the hundred for their arrows, and I owe one of them a favour from last winter, when he let a cart of charcoal go on credit. He'll take feathers in place of thanks; fletchers always will.

The wood hens scratch about in the east of the Fields, this side of the city gate, between my camps and the road up to Heartwood. Bring me five of their tail feathers, good clean ones. They drop them when they're chased, and they're easily chased.
Do that and we're square, he and I, and you and me as well: there's a traveller's hood off my rack in it for you, and a bit of coin.
progress: Five hen feathers, still. The wood hens are in the east of the Fields, this side of Heartwood's west gate, between my camps and the road. Bring the clean ones; a fletcher won't take a bent quill.
complete: Good clean feathers, every one. The fletcher will be pleased, which is rare, and I'll be out of his debt, which is rarer. Here's the hood, and the coin. If you're staying in the Fields, come back when you've some weight on you; the boars that root up my clamps at night want seeing to, and that's a job for someone who's been bitten before.

s_hf_2.name: Clamps in the Night

objective.label: Drive off 5 wild boars rooting the charcoal clamps

s_hf_2.desc: Wild boars root up the charcoal clamps at the Charcoal Camps by night and cost Heartwood's forges a week's charcoal each time. Charcoal-Master Dask wants five of them driven off the wood west of the camps.
offer: Now the real trouble. A charcoal clamp is a stack of wood under turf, burning slow for a week with no air; open it before its time and the whole stack flares and goes to ash. The boars root up the turf at night for the grubs under it, and every clamp they open is a week's charcoal gone and a cart the city's forges don't get.

They're wild boars, the big grey ones, not the young things you've seen rooting about the orchards. They bed in the wood just west of my camps and come down after dark, when the clamps are warm and the burners are asleep.

Drive five of them off and the clamps will hold the night, and the forges stay lit. I've a burner's wraps for you, leather, they take the heat; and a potion, because a boar doesn't care how new you are.
progress: Five wild boars, the big grey ones. They bed in the wood just west of the Charcoal Camps and come at the clamps after dark. Five off, and the clamps hold the night.
complete: The clamps held the night, first time this month. Here; a burner's wraps, they take the heat, and the potion. And since you've a taste for pig: there's a sow in the Fields that eats a whole season of windfall every autumn. Orchardist Petta, at the Wild Orchards north of the crossroads, has sworn at her for years and will pay anyone who ends her. In pie, knowing Petta. But she'll pay.

s_hf_3.name: The Orchard Sow

objective.label: Hunt the Orchard Sow that eats a season of windfall a year

s_hf_3.desc: Every autumn a great sow eats a season's windfall from the Wild Orchards in the Heartwood Fields. Orchardist Petta wants the Orchard Sow hunted down in her hollow west of the orchards, under the ridge.
offer: Wild, they call these orchards. Wild! I prune every one of them. Petta, orchardist, and these trees are mine whatever the maps say.

Now, the sow. Every autumn a great sow comes up out of the west and eats a whole season of windfall off this ground, the fruit every newcomer to Heartwood gathers for a first gift to the city, and every autumn I stand here and swear at her. She beds in the hollow west of the orchards, under the ridge, where the ground dips. You can't miss her; nothing else in the Fields is that size.
End her raids. She's called the Orchard Sow, and she's earned the name. When she's down, come and tell me and I'll send the orchard hands out for the carcass. Then I can stop swearing. Mostly.
progress: The Orchard Sow. She beds in the hollow west of the Wild Orchards, under the ridge, where the ground dips. End her and come back and tell Petta; the orchard hands will fetch her in.
complete: She's down! Oh, she's down. The orchard hands are already out with the cart. I'll make a saddle of her hide and sit on her every market day, and this autumn the windfall will lie where it falls, for the newcomers' baskets, the way it's meant to.

Take this charm. The twins from the high orchard, up the slope past my rows, left it with me years ago for whoever finally did it, and I'd near given up on anyone ever doing it. Go on, wear it; they'll want to see it on you.

s_hf_4.name: The Widow's View

objective.label: Walk the Fields the way the Widow Crake sees them: the orchards, the crossroads, the west gate of Heartwood

s_hf_4.desc: The Widow Crake on the ridge path wants a newcomer to walk the Heartwood Fields before hearing about them: the Wild Orchards, the Crossroads and the West Gate of Heartwood, then come back up the ridge and say it is the best ground in the world.
offer: From up here you can see the whole of the Fields and none of the Timber Estates, the rows the empire planted where our groves stood, past the Border Gate below you. That is by design. Mine. I built this path, and I chose where it looks.

I'm the Widow Crake, and you're new; it's in how you stand. New eyes should see the Fields before they hear about them, because once Heartwood starts telling you about this ground you'll never see it plain again.

So walk it. Down to the Wild Orchards to the north-east, where Petta prunes the trees she calls wild; across to the Crossroads in the middle of the Fields, where every road meets; and east along the road to the West Gate of Heartwood, under the city's walls. Stand at each. Then come back up my ridge and tell me it isn't the best ground in the world. I've a pair of potions here for your boots when you're done.
progress: The Wild Orchards to the north-east, the Crossroads in the middle of the Fields, and the West Gate of Heartwood at the east end of the road. Stand at each, then come back up the ridge path to the Widow Crake.
complete: Well? Best ground in the world. I knew you'd see it; you had the look of someone who'd see it. The orchards full of fruit nobody picks, the roads all meeting, and the city at the end of it with the trees showing over the walls. Keep that picture. Whatever anyone in that city tells you about the Fields later, and they will, you saw it first.
Here, two potions, for your boots. Come up again when the ridge is in sun.

s_ms_1.name: Reed Crabs in the Beds

objective.label: Clear 6 reed crabs from the reed harvest's beds

s_ms_1.desc: Cutter Bram, who cuts the reeds the academy's ledgers are pressed from, cannot get a crew into the reed beds on the Moonmere Shores while reed crabs are nipping the cutters' ankles. Clear six reed crabs from the beds and the shallows west of them before the reeds go to seed.
offer: Cutter Bram. I cut the reed harvest, here on the Moonmere Shores, and I have done since I could hold a knife. Every ledger in the college across the causeway started out standing in that water: cut, dried, split, pressed into the page they write on.

This season I cannot get a crew in. Reed crabs have come up into the beds, dozens of them, and they nip the cutters' ankles until nobody will stand in the water long enough to cut a bundle. The reeds go to seed in a few weeks, and seeded reed makes a page that cracks.

Clear six reed crabs out of the beds for me. They are in the harvest itself and in the shallows just west of it; you will see them scuttle when you wade in. Six fewer and I can put a crew in by morning.
The college pays me by the bundle, so I cannot pay much, but the cutters wear a hood against the sun off the water and I have a spare. It is yours when it is done.
progress: I still need six reed crabs cleared. They are in the reed harvest's beds and in the shallows just west of the beds, here on the Moonmere Shores. Wade in and they will come to you.
complete: Six, and I watched you do the last two. The crew goes in at first light; the college will have its ledgers this year, and the crabs will have a bad week. Here, take the hood; the cutters wear them, and you have earned the right to look like one of us.

s_ms_2.name: Shells for the College

objective.label: Bring Cutter Bram 4 silver shells from the silvershell crabs on the east shore

s_ms_2.desc: Cutter Bram needs four silver shells for the ink the academy writes its records in, the ink that does not fade. Silvershell crabs carry them, east along the Moonmere Shores past the end of the reed harvest.
offer: You know the reeds make the page. Here is the other half of it: the college grinds silver shell into the ink that does not fade. Three hundred years of the academy's records, every infirmary log and every catalogue card, are written in it, and the oldest line is as black as the newest.

The shell comes off the silvershell crabs. They live east along the shore from here, past the end of the reed harvest, where the beds give out and the sand starts. Not every crab's shell is thick enough to grind, and none of them give it up willingly.
Bring me four silver shells. I pass them to the college's ink-makers and they grind them down. Four is a year of ink for the whole academy; that is how little it takes and how much it matters.
I will give you a fen shell for your trouble, the kind the outfitters want for shoeing staves, and whatever potions I have in the hut.
progress: I still need four silver shells. The silvershell crabs carry them: east along the Moonmere Shores from the reed harvest, past where the beds end. Not every crab's shell is good enough; keep at them.
complete: Good shell, thick, with the silver all through it. That is a year of ink for the college. One day someone up there will write your name in a ledger, in this very colour, and it will not fade either. Potions, and a fen shell, as promised.

s_ms_3.name: What the Flats Count

objective.label: Bring Student Wen 3 marsh-fox pelts from the reed flats

s_ms_3.desc: Student Wen measures the Reed Flats every seventh day for the Provost, and the marsh foxes keep eating the marker stakes. Bring Wen three marsh-fox pelts from the foxes on the flats west of the road, enough for a coat.
offer: Student Wen, of the academy, posted to the Reed Flats. I am to measure the flats every seventh day and write down what I find: how far the water has come, how far the reeds have come, what grows where. What I find is water, and reeds, and a great many frogs. The Provost says it matters. I have stopped asking why.

What I also find is foxes. The marsh foxes eat my marker stakes, because the stakes were cut by a fisherman and smell of fish, and every seventh day I measure from stakes that are not there. Then I stand in the wind and write down numbers I do not trust.

Bring me three marsh-fox pelts. The foxes are on the flats west of the road, here on the Moonmere Shores; they den in the dry tussocks. Three pelts is a coat, and a coat means I can stand out here long enough to measure properly, and fewer foxes means the stakes stay where I put them.
The Provost would call that two problems solved by one errand. I have two ethers from the college stores, and they are yours.
progress: I still need three marsh-fox pelts. The marsh foxes are on the Reed Flats, west of the road on the Moonmere Shores, in the dry tussocks. Three pelts make a coat.
complete: A coat! A whole coat. The Provost says a shore is a clock if you read it slowly enough; she means that the water and the reeds move a little every year, and if you measure for long enough the years show. I would rather be warm while I read it. The ethers are yours, with my thanks.

s_ms_4.name: Hatchlings on the Shore

objective.label: Kill 5 fen hatchlings before they grow into something the watch cannot handle

s_ms_4.desc: Watch-Sergeant Haldis, who holds the North Gate for Moonmere's court, wants five fen hatchlings killed on the eastern flats of the Moonmere Shores before the young drakes grow too big for the watch to handle.
offer: Watch-Sergeant Haldis. I command the watch on the North Gate, the Border Gate that shuts the Moonmere Shores off from the Summer Lakes and the empire's land beyond. The gate opens when the court says it opens and not one morning sooner, so do not lean on it, and do not ask me about it.

Here is what I can do something about. Drake hatchlings have come up out of the eastern flats this spring, fen hatchlings, a dozen or more, and hatchlings grow. Today they are the size of a dog and take ducks. In a year they are the size of a boat and take the boat.

Kill five fen hatchlings for me, now, while they are small. They are on the eastern flats of the Shores, south of the Shore Wood, basking on the mud at the water's edge. My watch cannot leave the gate to do it, and the court will not send more men to a shore that is quiet.
The watch is grateful; the watch is also poor. A potion from the gatehouse, and a drake scale: the college across the causeway pays good coin for those, so sell it or keep it.
progress: I still need five fen hatchlings dead. They are on the eastern flats of the Moonmere Shores, south of the Shore Wood, basking at the water's edge. Go now, while they are still dog-sized.
complete: Five fewer things to grow up on my shore. Good. The watch stays at the gate, the fares get to the causeway with their legs, and in a year nobody is asking me why a drake took a ferryboat. The potion and the scale, as I said. If the hatchlings come back, so do you.

s_nr_1.name: Wolves at the Yard

objective.label: Kill 6 winter wolves that come down to the inn's yard

s_nr_1.desc: Ostler Bram, who keeps the Halfway Inn's stable, wants six of the winter wolves that come down to the inn's yard at night killed, in the snow north-west of the inn toward the Cliff Coast, so the coach horses can sleep.
offer: Bram. I keep the stable here at the Halfway Inn: the coach horses, the inn's mules, whatever a traveller leaves tied up. Mind the yard as you cross it, the horses kick; they have been coming over the pass all day and they want walking, not standing.

Here is my trouble. In the deep of winter the wolves come down off the high ground to the road, and lately to this yard. The inn's lamps keep them off, mostly, but a horse that smells wolf all night does not sleep, and a coach horse that has not slept goes lame on the pass.

The pack lies up north-west of the inn, in the snow toward the Cliff Coast. Kill six winter wolves out of it and the rest will keep their distance for the season. Then the horses sleep, and so, for the first time since the snow came, do I.
I can give you a Hi-Potion from the inn's shelf, and the pelt off the last one that tried the yard; it is yours by right if you do the work.
progress: Six winter wolves. The pack lies up north-west of the inn, in the snow between here and the Cliff Coast. Come back to me at the stable when it is done.
complete: The horses slept. First night since the snow, and the yard was quiet enough that I slept too. Here: a Hi-Potion from the inn's shelf, and the pelt off the last one that tried the yard. It is yours by right; you earned it in the cold. If you are staying, Auntie Wren's stew is on, and the horses will not mind you now.

s_nr_2.name: The Frozen Tarn

objective.label: Walk the Old Milestones and the Frozen Tarn for the road-warden's survey

s_nr_2.desc: Road-Warden Tesk at the Border Cairn needs the Old Milestones and the Frozen Tarn walked for this season's road survey by someone from neither Caerdun nor Heartwood, and a report that the tarn's ice holds.
offer: Tesk, road-warden. I keep this stretch of the North Road for both cities and belong to neither, which is the only way the job works. Heartwood's ground is reckoned from this cairn; Caerdun's from the Old Milestones. The inn was built where neither reckoning reaches, which is the whole point of it.

Every season the survey wants two places walked and looked at by someone who is not from either court, so that neither court can say the other lied about the road. This season it is the Old Milestones, the old imperial stones east of the inn on the north side of the road, and the Frozen Tarn, the lake south of the road between the inn and this cairn.

Go and stand at both. At the tarn, look at the ice. The coaches cut across it when the road drifts shut, and I need to know it holds this year. Come back and tell me what you saw; your word goes in the survey, next to mine. Two Ethers from the warden's stores for the walking.
progress: Walk to the Old Milestones, east of the inn on the north side of the road, then to the Frozen Tarn, south of the road. Look at the ice. Then come back to me here at the Border Cairn.
complete: Holds, does it? Good. That goes in the survey under your name, and the coaches can cut across when the road drifts shut. Two Ethers, as promised.

One thing more, since you were down there. Something big walks the crescent of high ground above the tarn. I have seen its prints in the snow: shaped like a man's, if a man were the size of a house. Stay by me a moment; I have more to say about it, and it is not for the survey.

s_nr_3.name: The Old Man of the Road

objective.label: Find and kill the Old Man of the Road on the crescent above the Frozen Tarn

s_nr_3.desc: Road-Warden Tesk wants the Old Man of the Road, the great white beast that has taken a horse and a trapper this winter, found on the crescent above the Frozen Tarn and killed, and its hide brought back so the coachmen believe it.
offer: The prints above the tarn. I have seen the thing that makes them once, at dusk, standing on the crescent, white as the slope behind it, so that I only saw it when it moved. The coachmen call it the Old Man of the Road, and when they see it they stop the coach and give it the road, and it lets them.

It has stopped letting them. This winter it has taken a horse out of its traces and a trapper who camped too near the tarn. The coaches will not cross the ice while it walks there, whatever my survey says, and I cannot blame them.

Find the Old Man on the crescent of high ground above the Frozen Tarn, south of the road east of the inn, and kill it. Bring me its hide; a coachman will not believe a road-warden, but he will believe a hide. In return I will give you a vest that was a trapper's. He would want it used.
progress: The Old Man of the Road walks the crescent of high ground above the Frozen Tarn, south of the road, east of the inn. Kill it and bring me its hide here at the Border Cairn.
complete: That hide is a hand deep. No wonder nothing we shot at it ever troubled it. I will hang this at the inn where the coachmen can put their hands in it, and the coaches will cross the tarn again.

They will drink to you tonight and have forgotten your name by the thaw, which is the road's way; do not take it hard. This vest was the trapper's it took. He would want it worn by the one who settled his account.

s_nr_4.name: Frost in a Jar

objective.label: Bring Auntie Wren 3 frost gels from the slimes on the pass

s_nr_4.desc: Auntie Wren of the Halfway Inn wants three frost gels, taken from the frost slimes on the pass east of the inn, to keep her larder cold through the summer.
offer: Sit. Eat. Whatever it is, it will keep until you have eaten; things usually do. I'm Wren, love, and this is my inn, and nobody goes back out into that snow on an empty stomach while I keep it.

Now, since you look like someone who goes out in the cold on purpose. Frost gel is the cold stuff a frost slime is made of, and it does not thaw. A jar of it in my larder keeps the meat and the butter cold clean through summer; a jar of it in a room will chill the room.

The frost slimes live on the pass east of the inn, where the road climbs toward the Border Cairn. Bring me three frost gels off them. Three jars, and the stew stays good till the thaw and past it, and I'll send you back on the road with a Remedy and a Hi-Potion for your trouble.
progress: Three frost gels, love. The frost slimes carry them; they're on the pass east of the inn where the road climbs toward the Border Cairn. Bring them to me here at the Halfway Inn.
complete: Cold as a Provost's welcome; that's Moonmere's head of the academy, love, and the cold is the only thing of hers I'd keep in the house. The larder thanks you, and so will everyone who eats here in July. Here, for the road: a Remedy and a Hi-Potion. Finish your bowl first.

s_sr_1.name: Crab for the Table

objective.label: Bring Fisher Marn 5 crab meat from the sand crabs

s_sr_1.desc: Fisher Marn, at the hut on the Shore Road's south-west shore, wants five crab meat from the sand crabs on the strand so the Coach Halt can serve crab to its coach tables and Marn can take a day off.
offer: Marn. I fish this shore from the hut here, and what I fish is crab, mostly. The big crabs come up out of the old grain-ship wreck along the bay at night, which is why I fish by day and sleep with the door barred.

The Coach Halt up the road wants crab for its coach tables, as it does every week, and this week my back wants a day off, which it does not often get. Those two wants can be settled by one person with a spear.

The sand crabs are on the strand: here by my hut, and all along the bay east toward the halt. Bring me five crabs' worth of meat and the halt eats, and I sit down. I'll give you a Hi-Potion for it, and a silver shell, which the academy at Moonmere pays for, ground.
progress: Five crab meat, from the sand crabs on the strand: by my hut here, and along the bay east toward the Coach Halt. Bring it back to me at the hut.
complete: Sweet meat; the crabs eat well off that wreck. The halt will eat well tonight and I will sit down for once with the door open. Here's your Hi-Potion. And take a shell, a silver one; the academy grinds them up for something, and pays like it matters.

s_sr_2.name: The Grain That Sprouts

objective.label: Kill 5 tide glubs feeding on the wreck's sprouting grain

s_sr_2.desc: Beachcomber Sull wants five of the tide glubs that have found the sprouting grain barrels in the Grain-Ship Wreck killed, before the wreck is more glub than ship.
offer: Sull. I comb this beach, and I comb that wreck: an imperial grain ship that has lain on this bay for three hundred years and was never claimed. Everything that comes out of her hull is grain, barrel after barrel, and every barrel of it sprouts the moment it is wet. Three centuries dry in a hold and it sprouts. Think about that; I do, most evenings.

The tide glubs have thought about it too. Glubs, the slimes that come in with the tide. They have found the sprouting barrels and they are feeding on them and growing, and there are more of them every week.
Kill five of them, here at the wreck, before there is more glub than ship. I'll pay in two Ethers and a slime gel, which is what one gets off a glub and what the Moonmere alchemists buy.
progress: Five tide glubs. They feed on the sprouting grain barrels at the Grain-Ship Wreck, here on the bay. Come back to me at the wreck when it is done.
complete: Fewer glubs, more barrels. That's a fair day. Here, two Ethers and a gel.

Something keeps the purser's cabin, mind; the cabin aft where the ship's clerk kept the ship's books. I do not go in. I have heard the pen. You could go in, if you are the sort who does; speak to me again here at the wreck when you are ready, and I'll tell you what I know.

s_sr_3.name: The Purser's Ledger

objective.label: Go into the wreck and take the ledger from the Purser who keeps its cabin

s_sr_3.desc: Beachcomber Sull wants whatever keeps the purser's cabin in the Grain-Ship Wreck put an end to, and the ship's ledger brought out: something in there has gone on signing for the grain for three hundred years.
offer: The purser's cabin, then. The purser was the ship's clerk, the one who signed for every barrel that came aboard. Something is in that cabin still, and it is still signing. I have stood under the deck at night and heard the pen go: a line, a pause, a line.

I don't know what it is and I am not going in to find out. You are. Go into the wreck, find the cabin aft, put an end to the Purser, whatever it has become, and bring out the ledger it has been writing in.

The court pays for a manifest from an imperial ship; a list of what she carried and for whom is worth money to any court that wants to know what the empire left behind. And I will pay to stop hearing that pen: whatever the Purser wears, you keep. I want none of it.
progress: The Purser keeps the cabin aft inside the Grain-Ship Wreck. Put an end to it and bring the ledger out to me on the beach.
complete: Every page signed for. Three hundred years of pages, in the same hand, every barrel of grain accounted to the empire. The last entry is this morning.

I'll take it to the court; let them read what the ship's clerk thought it was owed. And keep the vest off him, the drakescale one; it's yours. I want nothing of his in my hut, and I'll sleep with the door open for the first time in years.

s_sr_4.name: The Old Watch

objective.label: Reach the Old Watch on the headland and the Palm Strand for Student Ovi's notes

s_sr_4.desc: Student Ovi, walking the Shore Road to the academy at Moonmere, needs the Old Watch on the headland and the Palm Strand visited and described, for notes a tutor expects, because Ovi cannot draw and burns in the sun.
offer: Ovi. I'm a student, or I will be when I reach the academy at Moonmere, which is forty miles down this road, every mile of it warmer than the last. I was told the academy was cold. I think I was lied to.

My tutor set me work for the road: sketch the Old Watch, the imperial watch post on the headland south-east of here, and pace out the Palm Strand, the long beach south of here, and write both up. I cannot draw. I burn in the sun. I have been sitting under this palm for two days composing excuses.

Would you go in my place? Walk out to the Old Watch and down to the Palm Strand, look at both properly, and describe them to me when you come back. I'll write it up as though I went, which is a kind of scholarship. I can give you a Hi-Potion; it is the most valuable thing I own.
progress: Go to the Old Watch on the headland south-east of me, and to the Palm Strand, the beach to the south. Look at both and come back and describe them to me under my palm.
complete: Thank you. My tutor says the empire called every one of its sentinels, the metal watchmen it left at its posts, off this coast the night it left, all but the one on that headland; nobody knows why that one was left. I shall write that it looked lonely, which from your description it does, and I shall write that I paced the strand in the shade. Here, the Hi-Potion. I hope you never need it.

s_hw_1.name: Hounds Off the Rides

objective.label: Cull 6 king's hounds that have gone feral on the rides

s_hw_1.desc: Huntsman Orrin at the Hunting Lodge wants six of the King's Hounds, the imperial pack gone feral on the King's Rides east of the lodge, culled so Caerdun's supply trains stop losing mules.
offer: Orrin. Huntsman; I keep the lodge for Caerdun now that the court has put its forward camp here, and I sell what a hunter needs. Look east from this door. The King's Rides: three cuts through the wood, straight as a rule, made so the king could see a stag from the lodge door. He never came. Not once, in all the years before the empire left.

The hounds came, though, and they stayed. The empire bred a pack for his hunt, and a sentinel, one of the empire's metal caretakers, has gone on breeding them for three hundred years because nobody told it the king was not coming. Three centuries of King's Hounds, wild, and hungry.

They run the rides east of the lodge and the woods south of them. Cull six and the pack will give the lodge a wider berth, and Caerdun's supply trains coming through the gate will stop losing mules on the road. Two Hi-Potions from the lodge's stores for the work.
progress: Six King's Hounds. They run the King's Rides east of the lodge and the woods south of the rides. Come back to me at the lodge when they are down.
complete: Six collars. Look: imperial brass, the royal kennel's mark, and a number stamped under it. The numbers are in the thousands. Somebody has been numbering every pup for three hundred years.
That somebody is the master of hounds, and it is still out there at the far end of the rides, blowing its whistle. Here, your Hi-Potions. Stay a moment; I want to talk to you about that whistle.

s_hw_2.name: The Master of Hounds

objective.label: Silence the Master of Hounds at the far end of the rides

s_hw_2.desc: Huntsman Orrin wants the Master of Hounds, the sentinel at the far east end of the King's Rides whose whistle every hound in the wood still answers, silenced, and its whistle brought back to the lodge.
offer: The Master of Hounds. It is a sentinel, one of the empire's caretakers, standing at the far east end of the rides where the king's hunt would have gathered, with a whistle round its neck that every hound in this wood still comes to. I have heard it at dawn. The whole wood sits up.

While it blows, the pack breeds; it kennels them, numbers them, and sends them out onto the rides to be ready for a hunt that is three hundred years late. Cull all you like, the numbers go on climbing.

Go to the far east end of the King's Rides and silence it. It will not be glad to see you. Bring me the whistle, and this wood goes quiet for the first time since the king did not come. There is a hood in it, and the collar off any hound you fancy; I have a drawer of them.
progress: The Master of Hounds stands at the far east end of the King's Rides, past the stag ground. Silence it and bring its whistle back to me at the lodge.
complete: The whistle. When it stopped, every hound in the wood sat down at once; I felt it through my boots, standing on this step. Three hundred years of waiting for a hunt, over in a breath. Keep this collar; it's the lowest number I have, and I'd like it worn by someone who knows what it means. And wear the hood; the rides are cold at dawn, and you'll be walking them again.

s_hw_3.name: The Garrison Ruin

objective.label: Kill 6 Holloway Rummagers in the Swallowed Garrison, Pike's old company's billet in the west of the wood

s_hw_3.desc: Pike, a retired freebooter, wants six of the Holloway Rummagers that have got into the Swallowed Garrison, the old imperial garrison on its knoll in the west of the wood where Pike's former company is billeted, killed so the rest move on.
offer: Pike. I was a freebooter, which is what the courts call anyone who goes into the interior without a court's paper, and I'm retired, which is what a freebooter calls leaving the company. My old company holds the Swallowed Garrison: the imperial garrison up the holloway on its knoll in the west, swallowed by the wood to the roofline.
Garrison's ours now, the wood had it first, and the wood can have it back when we're done. That's what I used to say. The wood has started taking it back early.

Rummagers. Masked faces, ringed tails, little hands like a cutpurse. Holloway Rummagers, the wood calls them, after the sunken lane they came up. They have got into the racks, the stores, the bedding, the flour. My company is sleeping on the flour with a knife in each hand.

I left the company and they didn't like it, so I can't walk in and help. You can. Kill six of the rummagers in the ruin and the rest will move on to somewhere easier. A Hi-Potion for it, and something else I'll explain when you're back.
progress: Six Holloway Rummagers, in the Swallowed Garrison: up the holloway, on its knoll in the west of the wood. Then come back to me here.
complete: The ruin's quieter; I can hear it from here, or rather I can't, which is the point. Here is your Hi-Potion. And here is a charter I forged myself, years back, a court's paper with a seal I cut from a boot heel. A court would hang me for it, so you keep it; call it a souvenir.
One warning, for free. Don't go in the tomb, the Mausoleum under the ridge north of here. Something in there takes your name down, and I have never liked being written down.

s_hw_4.name: Stag on the Rides

objective.label: Bring Scout Bettany 3 elder antlers from the stags on the north ride, east of the Hunting Lodge

s_hw_4.desc: Scout Bettany at Caerdun's Forward Camp wants three elder antlers, shed by the red and elder stags on the north ride east of the Hunting Lodge, to send back to the court's smiths with the maps.
offer: Bettany. Caerdun's scout; I chart this province for the court, the water, the sightlines, and anything with teeth, and the supply trains follow my maps in. The trains go back empty, which the court dislikes.

So: the court's smiths want antler for knife hafts and tool handles, and the stags on the rides shed the best there is. Red stags and the big elder stags graze along the north ride, east of the lodge, up toward the King's Seat. Bring me three elder antlers, the heavy kind a full-grown stag carries, and the next train carries them back to Caerdun with my maps. Two Ethers and a piece of root amber for it, which is what the camp has to pay with.
progress: Three elder antlers. The red stags and elder stags graze along the north ride, east of the lodge, toward the King's Seat. Bring the antlers to me at the forward camp.
complete: Good heavy antler; that's a full head. The smiths will fight over it, which is how you know it's good, and the train goes back with something in it for once. Two Ethers and the amber, as promised. Chart safe out there; this wood has more teeth in it than my maps show yet.

s_te_1.name: Sap in the Felled Block

objective.label: Clear 6 sap beetles from the felled block

s_te_1.desc: Hasp, the freebooter logger at the Timber Yards, wants six of the dog-sized sap beetles cleared from the Felled Block, the stump ground between the yards and Plantation Cross, so the crew can cut past dusk.
offer: Hasp. Freebooter, logger, whatever pays; a freebooter is anyone working the interior without a court's paper, and I've never had the patience for paper. I run the Timber Yards here with a crew of my own. The empire's flume still runs and the empire's saw still cuts, and that is a living.

This is the Timber Estates: Heartwood's old groves, felled by the empire and replanted in ruler-straight rows. The Felled Block, north-east of the yards and south-west of Plantation Cross where Heartwood's camp is, is where the empire's last cut stood. The stumps there still run with sap after three hundred years, and the sap beetles have found it. They are the size of a dog and they do not like to be interrupted at dinner.
Clear six of them out of the block and my crew will cut past dusk again instead of knocking off at the first click of a shell. A Hi-Potion, and a beetle shell, which has its uses.
progress: Six sap beetles, in the Felled Block: the stump ground north-east of the Timber Yards, south-west of Plantation Cross. Come back to me at the yards.
complete: Shell like a shield; that's why the Heartwood woodwrights buy them, for exactly that, a shield. Take this one, and the potion. My crew is cutting till dark tonight. One thing: don't stand in the block yourself after dark. Something drinks the sap the beetles left, and it's bigger than a beetle.

s_te_2.name: Resin for the Yards

objective.label: Bring Hasp 4 thorn resin from the Estates' beetles and stumps

s_te_2.desc: Hasp at the Timber Yards wants four measures of thorn resin, taken from the sap beetles, stump mushnubs, root creepers and thorn sprites of the Timber Estates, so the yards can start caulking barges.
offer: Resin. Thorn resin seals a barge seam better than pitch, and the yards are going to be caulking barges soon. The Canal Works, the empire's fen province further in, has sentinels in it, the empire's metal caretakers, and by the sound of their hammers they're mending the locks. Locks mean barges, and barges mean someone has to build them, and that someone is going to want seams that hold.

The resin comes off the things that live on the sap: the sap beetles and the stump mushnubs, the walking fungus-caps, round the Felled Block and the Haul Road; the root creepers down by the flume; the thorn sprites in the west toward the old wood. Bring me four measures and the yards start caulking tonight. Boots for it; you'll want them, with the sap.
progress: Four thorn resin. The sap beetles and stump mushnubs carry it, round the Felled Block and the Haul Road; so do the root creepers by the flume and the thorn sprites in the west. Bring it to me at the yards.
complete: Amber-dark, and it smells of burnt honey; that's the good stuff. The yards are caulking tonight, and the first barge off these stocks will carry Hasp's name whether the court likes it or not. Here, the boots. Waywatcher pattern, and sealed with the same resin; you'll thank me the first time you step in a sap pool.

s_te_3.name: The Foreman

objective.label: Fell the Foreman, the sentinel that still walks the ranks with a two-man saw

s_te_3.desc: Ranger Tallow of Heartwood wants the Foreman, the sentinel that still walks the Timber Estates' rows with a two-man saw marking trees for a felling nobody ordered, destroyed; it walks the rows south-west of Plantation Cross, below the Felled Block.
offer: Tallow. Heartwood ranger; I keep the Gardens Road for the court, out here at the west end of the Estates. Heartwood's groves stood on this ground. The empire felled every one of them and replanted the land in rows, a tree where a clerk marked a tree. My grandmother could name the trees they cut, by name, in order, and she made me learn them.

There is a sentinel the crews call the Foreman. It walks the rows with a two-man saw that it carries alone, and it marks trees for felling: a chalk cross on the bark, one after another, for a felling nobody has ordered in three hundred years. Every mark is one of my grandmother's trees counted for the axe again.

It walks the rows south-west of Plantation Cross, below the Felled Block, where the rows run down toward the Glassworks road. Fell it, and report to me. My crew will fetch its saw. A ranger's cap for it, and the plate off the thing.
progress: The Foreman walks the rows south-west of Plantation Cross, below the Felled Block, where the rows run down toward the Glassworks road. Destroy it and report to me on the Gardens Road.
complete: The saw has stopped. I heard it stop; you get to know a sound after a lifetime of it. My crew will bring the saw back to Heartwood and I'll hang it in the grudge hall, the hall that records everything the empire took from us, with a label saying what it cut and when it stopped. Take the cap; it was a ranger's before me. And the plate, so you remember what it was.

s_te_4.name: Wolves in the Ranks

objective.label: Kill 6 rank wolves that hunt between the planted rows

s_te_4.desc: Scout Wenna at Heartwood's Forward Camp wants six of the rank wolves that hunt the lanes between the planted rows north-east of Plantation Cross killed, so the court's supply trains get through.
offer: Wenna. Heartwood's scout; I chart this province for the court, and the supply trains follow my charts in. Every tree in this province stands where a clerk told it to, in rows you could lay a rule along. I chart it anyway; the court likes a map, and the clerk's rows are not the whole of what lives here.

The wolves have learned the rows. They run the straight lanes between the trees at a supply train, out of the dark, and are gone down the next lane before the mules have stopped screaming. Rank wolves, we call them, for the ranks they run. Two trains this month have come into camp short.

Kill six of them. They hunt in the rows north-east of here, between Plantation Cross and the Overseer's Lodge. Then the trains get through, and I can chart the lodge road without looking over my shoulder. Two Hi-Potions and a pelt for it.
progress: Six rank wolves. They hunt the lanes between the rows north-east of Plantation Cross, toward the Overseer's Lodge. Come back to me at the forward camp.
complete: The trains got through; two came in this morning with every mule. Six pelts' worth of quiet. Here, your potions, and keep this pelt; you are the court's eyes in here as much as I am now, and the court's eyes go cold at night in these rows.

s_sl_1.name: Boats That Float

objective.label: Kill 6 mere frogs at the Lily Meres, west across the great lake

s_sl_1.desc: Boatwright Tess at the Boathouse Crescent wants six of the mere frogs that breed at the Lily Meres, west across the Great Lake, killed, so they stop sitting on her hulls at night and she can get a boat in the water.
offer: Tess, boatwright. Three boathouses here on the crescent, and every boat in them still floats after three hundred years. Imperial pitch. I'd sell my grandmother for the recipe, and she'd understand.

The trouble is the frogs. Mere frogs breed out at the Lily Meres, the lily ponds west across the Great Lake, and every night they come over the water, frogs the size of the boats, and sit on my hulls. A hull that's been sat on by that all night is not going anywhere in the morning.
Kill six of them out at the meres, where they breed, and the rest will thin out enough that I can get a hull in the water. A Hi-Potion for it, and a frog leg, which is more of a gift than it sounds.
progress: Six mere frogs, at the Lily Meres: the lily ponds west across the Great Lake from the crescent. Come back to me at the boathouses.
complete: A hull's in the water, and it floats like the day it was pitched. Here's the potion, and the leg; Heartwood eats these, you know, roasted with the skin on. Caerdun pretends not to and buys them by the barrel.

s_sl_2.name: Whiskers for the Alchemists

objective.label: Bring Student Pell 4 villa cat whiskers

s_sl_2.desc: Student Pell of Moonmere's academy, counting lilies at the Lily Meres, needs four villa cat whiskers for the academy's alchemists, from the villa cats around the Promenade and the villas, which keep stealing Pell's lunch.
offer: Pell. Student, of the academy at Moonmere, posted to the Lily Meres to count the lilies and write down what I find. What I find is that they close at dusk and open at dawn, which makes them a clock, if you are the Provost, who runs the academy and likes a clock.

What the academy's alchemists want is less poetic: villa cat whiskers, four of them, for reasons they have not shared with a student. The villa cats are the great sleek cats that have kept the empty villas for three hundred years, and they roam the Promenade and the villas east of it, and they have discovered my lunch.
Bring me four cat whiskers and the alchemists are satisfied and I get to keep eating. Two Ethers for it, and a pearl that came up out of the lily mere, which I have no use for.
progress: Four cat whiskers. The villa cats roam the Promenade and the villas east of it, along the lake. Bring the whiskers to me at the Lily Meres.
complete: Four. The alchemists will be pleased and will not say why; that is what alchemists are for. Here, two Ethers, and the pearl. It came up in the lily mere one morning as if the mere had decided I needed cheering up. Stay a moment; I have a larger problem, and he croaks.

s_sl_3.name: Old Bellwether

objective.label: Silence Old Bellwether, the great frog of the lily meres

s_sl_3.desc: Student Pell wants Old Bellwether, the giant frog that croaks the hours from the Lily Meres and makes the lilies open to him instead of the dawn, silenced, so the lily clock can be recorded truthfully.
offer: Old Bellwether. He is a frog the size of a boathouse, and he lives in the Lily Meres, and he croaks the hours: dawn, noon, dusk, with a voice you can feel in your teeth. The lilies have been listening to him for three hundred years. They open when he croaks, not when the sun rises, which means the clock I have been sent here to measure is a frog, and the Provost will not accept a frog.

Silence him. Find him in the Lily Meres, out in the deepest of the ponds, and bring me his crest, the ridge of skin along his head, so I have proof for the academy. Then I can finally write down what the lilies actually do. I have a hood for you, merewoven, which keeps the rain out, and another pearl.
progress: Old Bellwether croaks from the Lily Meres, out in the deepest pond, west of the Great Lake. Silence him and bring me his crest.
complete: The lilies opened at dawn this morning. Dawn! Every one of them, with the sun, and nothing croaking. I have a clock again, and my notes make sense, and the Provost will be pleased, which is a clock of its own, in that it happens about once a year. Here, the hood and the pearl. I'll put your name in the footnote.

s_sl_4.name: The Villa Registry

objective.label: Walk the villas, the boathouse crescent and the promenade, and confirm each is as the household left it

s_sl_4.desc: The Caretaker Sentinel that keeps the Summer Lakes' villa registry requires the Villa Terraces, the Boathouse Crescent and the Promenade inspected from the path by a person of no household standing, and a report that each is as the household left it.
offer: The villa is closed for the season. The season has been closed for three hundred and eleven years. I am the Caretaker; I keep the registry of the household's summer properties on these lakes, the household being the empire's people, their dependants and their belongings as one house.

The registry requires, once in a season, an inspection of the properties by a person of no household standing. You qualify; you have no standing whatsoever. Walk to the Villa Terraces, the houses on the slope north of the Great Lake; to the Boathouse Crescent, on the lake's east shore; and to the Promenade, here on the south-west shore. Observe each from the path.

Report to me that each is as the household left it. Do not enter. Do not touch the linen. Compensation for the inspection will be issued: two Hi-Potions from the villa stores. You may admire the gardens from the path.
progress: Walk to the Villa Terraces north of the Great Lake, the Boathouse Crescent on its east shore, and the Promenade on its south-west shore. Observe from the path. Then report to me here.
complete: Noted: the Villa Terraces, as the household left them. The Boathouse Crescent, as the household left it. The Promenade, as the household left it. The linen is aired weekly. The household will return and find the season ready. Compensation issued: two Hi-Potions. You may continue to admire the gardens from the path. Please do not sit.

s_rv_1.name: Sounding the Lane

objective.label: Kill 6 lake pike that snap at waders beside the boardwalk crossing

s_rv_1.desc: Poleman Grist, who keeps the boardwalk at the Reservoir's Joint Camp, wants six lake pike killed in the shallow lane beside the crossing before the courts' surveyors wade out toward the Bell Tower.
offer: Poleman Grist. I keep the boardwalk for the three courts' camp here, the Joint Camp, and I sound the boards every morning with this pole. Hear that? Sound. The boards are sound from this shore to the tower's foot and no further, and I'll say so to anyone who asks and to several who don't.

Here's the trouble. The courts' surveyors want to wade the shallow lane beside the boards, over the drowned village, to mark a crossing to the tower. The lake pike in that lane have had three hundred years with nobody fishing them. They're as long as a man, and they've taken a sounding pole clean out of my hands twice.

Kill six of the lake pike in the water east of the camp, alongside the boardwalk crossing. Six fewer and the surveyors can wade without one of them losing a leg. I'll pay, and I'll throw in a tooth; the fishers on the Shore Road give good coin for a pike tooth this size.
progress: I still need six lake pike dead. They lie in the shallow lane east of the camp, right alongside the boardwalk crossing. Wade in and they'll come to you; they always do.
complete: Teeth like roofing nails. Keep that one; the Shore Road fishers will give you more for it than I can. The surveyors go out at first light, and they'll come back with all their legs, which is more than I'd have promised yesterday.
You've noticed the camp, I expect. Three courts on one shore, Caerdun, Heartwood and Moonmere, sharing one fire and one mule line, and nobody has drawn steel yet. Give it a week.

s_rv_2.name: Chitin for the Smiths

objective.label: Bring Junn 4 silt chitin plates for the courts' smiths

s_rv_2.desc: Archivist Junn at the Reservoir's Joint Camp needs four silt chitin plates, which the silt striders on the camp's west shore carry on their backs, for the courts' smiths to hone the camp's blades.
offer: Archivist Junn, of Moonmere, though you know that by now; we sat at the same table at the inn. I came down to this valley through the Canal Works. Damp. Educational. There was a barge full of three-hundred-year-old paperwork, and I am not allowed to talk about how happy that made me.

This is not about paper, for once. The silt striders, the long-legged things that pick along the mud west of the camp, carry back-plates silted through with old riverbed. The courts' smiths swear a plate of that chitin puts a better edge on a blade than any stone they brought. I am told this matters, and in this valley I have decided to believe the people with hammers.

Bring me four silt chitin. Kill silt striders on the west shore and take the plates off their backs. Four plates and the camp's blades stay sharp for whatever is inside that tower. I'll pay, and there are two ethers in it, since you'll be doing the walking.
progress: I still need four silt chitin plates. The silt striders carry them; they pick along the mud on the west shore, out of the camp. Four plates, and the smiths stop looking at me as if I should be doing it myself.
complete: Plate from a strider's back, and the smiths are delighted, and I will never understand smiths. One of them found a pearl grown into the silt of the first plate, and nobody in the camp could agree whose it was, so I am settling the matter: it's yours. Take it before Heartwood files a claim.

s_rv_3.name: The Drowned Warden

objective.label: Put down the Drowned Warden in the drowned village west of the Bell Tower

s_rv_3.desc: The Sluice-Keeper, the sentinel that keeps the Great Dam at the Reservoir, wants the Drowned Warden put down: what remains of the flooded village's warden, who still keeps its broken houses west of the Bell Tower and takes surveyors in the shallow lanes.
offer: I am the Sluice-Keeper. I keep the Great Dam. The dam holds. The dam has always held. You are standing on household works without a manifest; this is noted, and no notice will be issued, because I have a shortfall and you have a blade.

The village below the water was closed when the valley was flooded. Its warden did not leave with the household. He remains, after a fashion, and he keeps the village still: he walks its broken houses in the shallow lanes west of the Bell Tower, and he takes any surveyor who wades into them. The village is closed. He does not accept that it is closed.

Put down the Drowned Warden in the drowned village, west of the tower, where the roofs stand out of the water. Bring me his key. The village's key is the dam's property and I will file it. Compensation will be issued from the dam's stores in accordance with standing orders.
progress: The Drowned Warden is in the drowned village west of the Bell Tower, among the roofs that stand out of the shallow water. Put him down and bring me his key.
complete: The key to a village of flooded houses. Received. Filed. He kept the village three hundred years past its closing; I note that I understand the impulse, and I note that it is not in my standing orders to understand anything. The dam holds. You may cross the crest; keep to it, and do not lean on the rail. Compensation: a helm from the dam's stores, and the warden's relic, for which the dam has no file.

s_rv_4.name: Sentinels on the Dam

objective.label: Clear 4 sluice sentinels from the dam's works before the courts' expedition passes

s_rv_4.desc: Grudge-Keeper Morrow wants four sluice sentinels cleared from the west end of the Great Dam at the Reservoir, where they turn back anyone not on their manifest, so the courts' expedition can cross the dam's crest.
offer: Morrow, Heartwood's grudge-keeper. I keep the floor of the grudge hall, where Heartwood writes down everything the empire took from it, and I've carried the hall's book down into this mud. Look at that dam. Nobody has tended it in three hundred years and it holds like the day it was poured. I've written that down for the grudge hall; the hall records what the empire built as carefully as what it took.

The dam is also our road. The expedition needs to cross its crest to reach the far side of the valley, and at the west end, where the crest comes out of the valley wall on the flooded town's side, four sluice sentinels stand the gate. Sentinels: the empire's caretakers, left behind to keep the place and its rules. These admit nobody who is not on their manifest, and nobody living is on their manifest.

Clear the four sluice sentinels from the dam's west end. They don't negotiate; I tried, with the seal, which I'll remind you is the size of a dinner plate. Then the expedition can cross. Bring me the plates off them; I want to see what they're stamped with.
progress: Four sluice sentinels, at the dam's west end: follow the crest to where it comes out of the valley wall on the flooded town's side. They stand the gate there and let nobody past who isn't on their manifest.
complete: Four plates. Look: each one stamped with a work order, a number and a date. The sentinels on the dam weren't left here by accident; somebody wrote them an order, and the order is still in force. Everything in this valley has a work order.

I am going to be angry about that in a moment. The groves my families lost have waited three centuries for one line of paper, and a sluice gate got a stamped order. Give me the moment. The expedition crosses at noon; you cleared the way.

s_kg_1.name: Cuttings for Heartwood

objective.label: Bring Vell 4 silver cuttings from the nursery beds

s_kg_1.desc: Vell, a freebooter who steals cuttings from the King's Gardens and sells them to Heartwood, wants four silver cuttings recovered from the nursery slimes in the silver beds by the glasshouse, south-east of the Fountain Court.
offer: Vell. No title; I don't hold a court's charter and I don't want one. I'm what the courts call a freebooter: I come in without their paper, I take what sells, and I argue with them when they catch me. What sells here is cuttings. Three hundred years of royal stock in these beds, and nothing guarding it but a machine with manners.

The silver beds are the prize: silver-leaved stock the empire bred for the palace, and nobody outside the border has grown it since. Heartwood buyers pay well for anything the empire took, and the Gardens were laid out on Heartwood land. The trouble is the nursery slimes in the beds. They eat the roots, and they take the cuttings down with them.

Bring me four silver cuttings. Kill nursery slimes in the silver beds, south-east of here by the glasshouse, and take the cuttings out of them, roots and all; the silver bowerbirds on this side of the Gardens steal a few for their bowers too. I'll pay in coin, and I'll tell you this week's way through the hedge maze; the Head Gardener, the sentinel with the shears, re-cuts it, and you'll want it before you go in.
progress: Four silver cuttings, roots and all. The nursery slimes carry them; they're in the silver beds south-east of here, by the glasshouse. Kill the slimes and take the cuttings out of them; the silver bowerbirds near here carry a few as well.
complete: Silver cuttings, roots and all, and Heartwood will pay me more than I'm paying you, which is how trade works. Here's your coin. The maze: left at the first fork, right twice, straight on at the little fountain, and don't trust a word of it past Thursday. The Head Gardener re-cuts the whole thing every week, and nothing I steal changes that.

s_kg_2.name: Hounds in the Hedges

objective.label: Kill 6 garden hounds hunting the hedge walks

s_kg_2.desc: Duelist-Master Sabel, at the Fountain Court of the King's Gardens, wants six garden hounds killed in the hedge walks east of the court, so the courts' surveyors can leave the paths.
offer: Sabel. Look at the carts. They run inward, every one of them: fresh cuttings and potted stock, crate after crate, all bound deeper into the interior, toward the capital. I've been counting them since dawn and I've run out of fingers. Something in this garden is being sent somewhere, on purpose.

The courts want the Gardens surveyed, and a survey needs people who leave the paths. The garden hounds in the hedge walks east of this court take anyone who does. Kennel-bred, from the look of them, like the hounds in the Hunting Wood, and better fed.

Kill six garden hounds in the hedge walks east of the Fountain Court. Six and I can send the surveyors in off the paths with a clear conscience, or as clear as it gets in here. Bring me their collars; I want to compare the brass.
progress: Six garden hounds still need killing. They hunt the hedge walks east of the Fountain Court; step off the path and they'll find you before you find them.
complete: Six collars. Same brass as the hounds in the Hunting Wood, same stamp, and the kennel numbers are higher: whoever numbered the king's hounds in the wood numbered these afterward, and kept counting. Somebody in this empire was very organised. I hate it.

The surveyors go in off the paths tomorrow, and the numbers go in my report to the courts: the same kennel as the king's hounds in the wood, still breeding and still counting, three hundred years after the household left.

s_kg_3.name: The Head Gardener

objective.label: Defeat the Head Gardener in the King's Gardens' south-east parterre and take its shears

s_kg_3.desc: Archivist Junn wants the Head Gardener defeated and its shears taken: the sentinel that cuts the King's Gardens' hedges to a three-hundred-year-old plan and cuts down anyone standing in it. It works the south-east parterre, off the Fountain Court's south walk.
offer: Junn. I've been reading the Gardens' registry, the planting book from the glasshouse office. It lists every bed by its stock and by its purpose, and the purpose column says the same word for every bed: household. Not the king, not the palace. Household. Every rose in this place is growing for the people who left.

The Head Gardener is the sentinel that keeps the plan. It cuts the maze and the hedges to the shape they had three hundred years ago, to the inch, and it cuts anyone standing where the plan says a hedge goes. Two of our readers went in to measure a hedge and came out needing stitches. Its shears are the plan; it carries three centuries in its hands.

Defeat the Head Gardener and take its shears. It works the south-east parterre, off the south walk out of the Fountain Court; you'll hear the shears before you see it. Without them the Gardens stop being edged, for one morning at least, and our people can measure what they like.
progress: The Head Gardener is in the south-east parterre, off the south walk out of the Fountain Court. Defeat it and bring me its shears.
complete: The shears. They're heavier than they look; three hundred years of a plan will do that. Every hedge in the Gardens will stand a hand taller by spring, the maze will grow shut, and nobody will cut the roses for a household that isn't here.

I expected to be glad. A garden kept for three hundred years for someone who is coming back, kept perfectly, by a thing that was told to and never asked why. I find I cannot hate it. Keep the shears; someone should, and it won't be me.

s_gw_1.name: Cullet for the Melt

objective.label: Bring Pane-Seller Dorrit 5 cullet from the melt crabs and furnace floors

s_gw_1.desc: Pane-Seller Dorrit, a freebooter at the Glassworks, wants five pieces of cullet, broken glass for the melt, from the melt crabs along the Melt Canal or the furnace sentinels of the Furnace Row, to run a pour of Dorrit's own where the sentinels do not count.
offer: Pane-Seller Dorrit. Freebooter, which means no court's charter and no court's protection, and I sell window glass out of a desert made of it. The furnaces along the row have run without a day's stop for three hundred years, and the sentinels count every pane at the racking yard. They don't count the ones that never reach the rack. Buying?

I want cullet: broken glass, for the melt. You can't pour glass from sand alone in a furnace you've borrowed. The melt crabs along the Melt Canal carry cullet in their shells, and the furnace sentinels on the Furnace Row shed it when they're broken. Either will do.

Bring me five cullet. Kill melt crabs on the lower Melt Canal, where it runs into the Mirror Flat south-east of the Racking Yard, or furnace sentinels on the row if you're feeling brave, and pick the glass out of them. Five and I can run my own pour tonight, in a kiln the sentinels don't inspect. I'll pay, and I'll owe you a favour, which in a place like this is worth more.
progress: I still need five cullet. The melt crabs on the lower Melt Canal, where it runs into the Mirror Flat, carry it in their shells; the furnace sentinels on the Furnace Row shed it when they fall. Five pieces, any mix.
complete: Good clean cullet, no slag in it. My pour runs tonight, and tomorrow I'll have panes the racking yard never counted. Here's your coin.

One thing, as the favour owed. If you hear of a glassblower still working out on the Mirror Flat, east of the yard, don't go near it. It isn't on the row's orders, and it isn't making windows, not the kind anyone ordered. Come back and see me here, by the furnaces, when you've the stomach for it.

s_gw_2.name: The Glassblower

objective.label: Stop the Glassblower on the mirror flat

s_gw_2.desc: Pane-Seller Dorrit wants the Glassblower stopped: a sentinel working alone on the Mirror Flat east of the Racking Yard, pouring glass the Furnace Row never ordered, which has killed two of Dorrit's runners. Bring back one of its panes.
offer: You're back, and you've the look for it. Good. The Glassblower. It's a sentinel like the others, but it has left the row, and it works the Mirror Flat alone, out east of the Racking Yard, where the melt ran flat and cooled into a mirror. It pours something out there that the row never ordered and the manifests never list.
It has killed two of my runners for getting close enough to see what. The second had run panes for me ten years and thought he knew how close was close. I'm done sending runners.

Stop the Glassblower on the Mirror Flat, and bring me one of its panes. I want to know what a sentinel makes when nobody is giving it orders. I'll pay what I've got: coin, and the jerkin my runner wore.
progress: The Glassblower works the Mirror Flat, east of the Racking Yard, where the melt cooled flat. Stop it and bring me one of the panes it has been pouring.
complete: Look at this pane. Measure it against anything on the rack: it's the wrong size for every window in the manifests. It's a window for a house that isn't in any order, built to no plan but its own. Nobody told it to. It was making its own.
The jerkin was my runner's. He'd want it worn by someone who went out there and came back. Keep it, and keep off the flat at night; whatever that thing was building, it never finished.

s_gw_3.name: Wasps in the Row

objective.label: Kill 6 glass wasps nesting in the furnace row

s_gw_3.desc: A Furnace Sentinel of the Glassworks' Furnace Row wants six glass wasps killed in the row and along the Melt Canal; they nest in the furnaces' heat and foul the pour, and a shortfall at the rack is recorded.
offer: The row is not to be approached during the pour. The pour is continuous. I am a Furnace Sentinel; I keep the Furnace Row, the line of furnaces that has poured window glass without stopping since the household left, and I count the panes at the rack.

Glass wasps nest in the row's heat. They build in the flues and fall into the melt, and a pane with a wasp in it is a pane that does not reach the rack. The count at the rack then shows a shortfall. Shortfalls are recorded. I would prefer to record none.

Kill six glass wasps. They nest along the Furnace Row and hunt over the Melt Canal beside it. Six removed and the count at the rack will show no shortfall for the season. Compensation will be issued from the row's stores in accordance with standing orders.
progress: Six glass wasps. They nest in the Furnace Row's flues and hunt over the Melt Canal beside the row. Remove them; the pour must not show a shortfall.
complete: Shortfall: none. Recorded. The count at the rack is correct for the first time in eleven seasons, and I have noted the cause, which is you. Compensation issued: wasp glass from the flues, and ethers from the stores. You may approach the row. Not during the pour. The pour is continuous.

s_cw_1.name: Eels and Iron

objective.label: Bring Eel-Seller Pask 4 bog iron from the fen's mud

s_cw_1.desc: Eel-Seller Pask, a freebooter trading on the Canal Works fen, will buy four lumps of bog iron, which the bog lurkers, marsh wisps and barge crayfish drag up out of the mud, to sell on to Moonmere's smiths.
offer: Eel-Seller Pask. Freebooter: no court's charter, no court's cut, just a boat and a basket. Eels, roe, reed-cord, smoked or fresh, and I'll buy any iron you pull out of the mud. That's the whole shop. Welcome to the fen.

The Canal Works was the empire's great waterway, every lock from here to the capital. Three hundred years with nobody tending it, and the fen came back over the lot. Now the mud is full of bog iron, lumps of it, rusted off the old lock gates and sunk. The bog lurkers and the marsh wisps drag it up when they move, and the barge crayfish build it into their lodges.

Bring me four lumps of bog iron. Kill bog lurkers, marsh wisps or barge crayfish anywhere on the fen and take the iron off them. Moonmere's smiths pay me for it, I pay you, and everybody's boots stay wet. That's the fen's arithmetic.
progress: Four bog iron. The bog lurkers, the marsh wisps and the barge crayfish all drag it up out of the fen's mud; kill them anywhere on the Canal Works and take the iron off them.
complete: Iron with the fen still in it; you can smell the mud. The smiths take it anyway, melt it clean, and never ask where it came from, which is a quality I value in a customer. Here's your coin. The fen pays, if you don't mind the fen. Most do. Come back if you're ever down in the sluice; there's more iron there than I like to think about.

s_cw_2.name: The Paperwork Barge

objective.label: Drive 5 barge crayfish off the canal company's paperwork barge

s_cw_2.desc: Junn wants five barge crayfish driven off the canal company's paperwork barge in the Canal Works (they lodge in the Sunken Barges just west of it), so she can read its three hundred years of manifests, tolls and lock tallies in peace.
offer: Junn. Do you remember, at the Reservoir, I said I came through the Canal Works and there was a barge full of three-hundred-year-old paperwork? This is the barge. Sabel says I'm not allowed to talk about how happy it makes me, so I'm going to show you instead. Look at it. Look at it.

It's the canal company's barge, the one that carried its books: every manifest of every cargo, every toll paid at every lock, every lock-keeper's tally, from the first cut to the night they left. The company's whole life, in one hold. And the barge crayfish want its timber for their lodges, and they come up the sides at me whenever I turn a page.

Drive five barge crayfish off. Their lodges are in the Sunken Barges, the old wrecks just west along the canal from this one; that's where you'll find them. Five of them gone and I can read in peace, and the courts get the only record of how this canal was run.
progress: Five barge crayfish. They lodge in the Sunken Barges, the wrecks just west along the canal from my barge in the Canal Works. Drive them off so I can read.
complete: Peace, and paper. Thank you. I've got as far as year forty of the tolls and I may be here until the household gets home.

Listen, though. Hear the water moving in the channels? That isn't the fen. The sentinels have started repairing the works, dredging and rebuilding the locks, this season, after three hundred years of letting it all drown. I'll be here a while, reading, and I'd like to know why they started now. Sabel has a theory and bad boots.

s_cw_3.name: The Lock-Keeper

objective.label: Retire the Lock-Keeper that holds the First Lock shut, east of the Great Sluice

s_cw_3.desc: A Dredge Sentinel of the Great Sluice wants the Lock-Keeper retired: an older sentinel at the First Lock east of the sluice that does not recognise this season's repair order and holds the lock shut, so that nothing for the rehanging can pass up the line.
offer: The works are under repair. Navigable by the Restoration. Stand clear of the paddles. I am a Dredge Sentinel; I dredge the Great Sluice's channels, and I carry the repair order for this season, which is nailed to the sluice posts for anyone to read: every lock from here to the capital, mended and rehung, in time for the Restoration, the household's return.

The Lock-Keeper of the First Lock predates the repair order. It was set to keep that lock three hundred years ago, and it has never received a new instruction it recognises. It holds the First Lock shut. Nothing for the rehanging, no gate timber, no ironwork, no dredge, gets up the line past the First Lock while it holds, and the schedule slips. The schedule does not slip.

Retire the Lock-Keeper at the First Lock, east of the sluice along the lock line, and recover its key. Then the schedule holds. Compensation will be issued from the lock stores in accordance with standing orders.
progress: The Lock-Keeper holds the First Lock, east of the Great Sluice along the lock line. Retire it and bring me its key.
complete: Key received. Lock the first: cleared. Lock the second: dredged. Lock the third: gates to be rehung, this week. The schedule holds.

The Lock-Keeper kept its lock for three hundred years on an order nobody rescinded. I have recorded that it did its duty, and I have recorded that its duty was in the way. Both entries stand. The Restoration will find the canal navigable. Compensation issued: a helm from the lock stores.

s_gp_1.name: Sheaves for the Farm

objective.label: Bring Goodwife Tessaly 6 wheat sheaves from between the harvesters' rows

s_gp_1.desc: Goodwife Tessaly of the Western Farm on the Granary Plains needs six wheat sheaves back from the granary rats and straw slimes that carry them off her rows, so the farm eats this winter.
offer: Goodwife Tessaly, of the Western Farm. Yes, a farm, on the Granary Plains, inside the border, with people on it. We never left. My people were farming here when the empire went, and we're farming here still, between the harvesters' rows, because somebody has to.

The harvester sentinels reap the empire's rows and leave ours alone; they always have. It's the vermin I can't abide. The granary rats and the straw slimes carry off more sheaves from my field than the sentinels reap in a day, and the rats out here are the size of dogs, with all that grain and nobody hunting them.

Bring me six wheat sheaves back. The granary rats run the fields round this farm; the straw slimes are out in the south fields, below the Reaping Line. Kill either and take back the sheaves they've carried off. Six and we thresh tonight, and the farm eats this winter; the sentinels don't count our grain, and they won't share theirs. I'll feed you, and there's a potion or two in the house.
progress: Six wheat sheaves. The granary rats carry them off through the fields round the Western Farm, and the straw slimes out in the south fields below the Reaping Line. Kill them and bring the sheaves back.
complete: Six sheaves, and we'll have them threshed by tonight. That's bread for the winter and seed for the spring, which is all a farm ever asks. Sit down. There's bread, and apples from the tree Harl swears is his, and you'll always have a plate at this table. Not many come up from the Western Ford who'd stop for a farm.

s_gp_2.name: The Wild Oxen

objective.label: Cull 5 feral oxen trampling the southern farm

s_gp_2.desc: Old Harl of the Southern Farm on the Granary Plains wants five feral oxen culled west of his farm; the plains' plough teams went wild when the empire left, and this year the herd has come down on his rows.
offer: Harl. The Southern Farm, such as it is. You'll have met Tessaly; she talks, I farm. The reapers never troubled us. The harvester sentinels reap the survey rows, the empire's rows, and leave the rest, and we've lived in the rest for as long as anyone can remember.

The oxen are another matter. When the people went, the plough teams went wild, and they've run these plains in herds ever since, six generations of them. They never came near a farm. This year they've come down on my rows like they know something, trampling what the rats leave.

Cull five feral oxen, west of the farm, where the herd has been grazing. Five and the herd moves off and the farm stands. I'll pay what a farm can pay, and you can have a horn; they make a decent cup.
progress: Five feral oxen. The herd grazes west of the Southern Farm on the Granary Plains. Cull five and the rest will move off.
complete: Five horns. My grandfather's oxen, most like, or their get, six generations wild. Good beasts, once.

I'll tell you what I've not told Tessaly. Three hundred years the empire's wheat rotted where the harvesters cut it; every year of my life and my grandfather's. Not this year. This year they're carting the wheat to the towers instead of letting it rot, and the oxen have gone restless the same season. I don't like what that means, and I've not decided what it means yet.

s_gp_3.name: The Reaper

objective.label: Fell the Reaper south of the Great Granary and bring its blade

s_gp_3.desc: A Count Sentinel at the Great Granary wants the Reaper felled south of the granary: a harvester that cuts rows the count never ordered, which the count cannot record. Bring its blade for the record.
offer: Tower the ninth: filled. Tower the tenth: filling. I am a Count Sentinel. I keep the count of the Great Granary: every sheaf reaped on the Reaping Line, every tower it fills, every ration it will make. The count is kept. The count has been kept every day since the household left, with nothing to count, and it is kept today, with a great deal.

There is a discrepancy. The Reaper is a harvester that has left the Reaping Line and cuts rows south of the granary that the count did not order cut: the fallow, the verges, the headlands. The count cannot record what it did not order. Grain enters the towers that is not in the count. The count is therefore wrong, and the count is not wrong.

Correct the discrepancy. Fell the Reaper, south of the Great Granary, where the uncounted rows are, and bring its blade to me for the record. Compensation from the granary stores will be issued in accordance with standing orders.
progress: The Reaper cuts south of the Great Granary, in rows the count did not order. Fell it and bring me its blade.
complete: Discrepancy corrected. Blade recorded, and struck from the harvest. The count is kept, and it is right.

You may ask what the count is for. I am permitted to answer. Phase five: rations for a city, from the morning they arrive, every man, woman and child of the household, fed from these towers on the first day and every day after. Forty towers. The count will be exact. Compensation issued: a maul from the granary stores. Tower the eleventh: filling.

s_bw_1.name: Ropes for the Face

objective.label: Recover 3 wall-runner's ropes from the rampart geckos on the outer face

s_bw_1.desc: Wall-Runner Ketch, a freebooter who climbs the Border Wall's outer face, wants three Wall-Runner's Ropes back from the rampart geckos that nest in the coils the lost runners left on the face, so he can rig the West Stair for the courts' climbers.
offer: Ropes, pitons, and the good snow-boots: that's me, Ketch, wall-runner, no court's paper and proud of it. The sentinels let you walk the rampart road up top; they don't let anyone on the outer face, the hundred miles of sheer stone this wall shows the free lands. I go on it anyway. That's what a runner is.

Here's my trouble. The runners who climbed before me left their ropes on the face when the wall took them: a slip, a storm, a sentinel's hand, I don't ask which. The coils are still hanging out there, and the rampart geckos have made nests of them. You'll find the geckos along the rampart west of my pitch, on the face just below the road.
