Kill geckos until you've pulled three ropes out of their nests and bring them to me. With three good lengths spliced I can rig the West Stair properly, so the courts' climbers come up the wall on a line instead of on their fingernails. Potions in it for you, and the courts can owe me the rest.
progress: I still need three Wall-Runner's Ropes. The rampart geckos nest in the old coils on the outer face, west along the rampart from my pitch; the ropes come out of their nests once the geckos are dead.
complete: Three. Frayed where the wall took their owners, chewed where the geckos sat on them, and still better rope than anything the courts brought up here. I'll splice them tonight. By morning the West Stair is rigged, and every climber who comes up it on my line can tell the courts they owe Ketch. Here: potions, for the cold up here.

s_bw_2.name: Snow Cats on the Road

objective.label: Kill 6 snow cats that hunt the rampart road

s_bw_2.desc: A Wall Sentinel on the Rampart Road of the Border Wall wants six Snow Cats culled: they hunt the chartered travellers the wall admits, which is not permitted.
offer: The rampart road is closed to unchartered traffic. You are chartered. Proceed. Before you proceed, a notice. I am a Wall Sentinel. This wall is one hundred miles long. It is patrolled. It has always been patrolled.

The snow cats are a fault in the patrol. They hunt the road, and what walks the road since the gates opened is chartered traffic: explorers, mule trains, the courts' climbers. Chartered traffic is permitted. Hunting it is not. I have issued the cats no notices; they do not read.

Six snow cats removed from the Rampart Road would correct the fault. You will find them along the road in both directions from this post, lying in the drifts where they are white on white. Compensation will be issued from stores in accordance with standing orders. Proceed.
progress: Six Snow Cats are still hunting the Rampart Road of the Border Wall. They lie in the drifts along the road in both directions from my post. Remove them. Proceed.
complete: Six snow cats. Recorded in the register. The road is patrolled; it is now patrolled more effectively. Compensation from stores: a pelt, and restoratives. Note that Caerdun's furriers pay coin for snow cat pelts; the wall does not. The wall has paid nobody anything for three hundred years, and the patrol has continued. Proceed.

s_bw_3.name: The Wall Drake

objective.label: Kill the Wall Drake that roosts on the east ramparts

s_bw_3.desc: Wall-Runner Ketch wants the Wall Drake killed, the slate-coloured drake that roosts on the east ramparts of the Border Wall and snatches runners off the outer face, so he can at last rig the East Stair.
offer: Ketch again, wall-runner. The West Stair I can rig any day; here's the bigger ask. Walk the rampart road east and look up: the slate-coloured thing roosting on the east ramparts is the Wall Drake. It takes runners off the face the way a cat takes birds off a wall: one swoop, and the rope's swinging empty. Half the empty coils hanging on the outer face are its doing.

I've never rigged the East Stair because of it. No runner will work that face while it's up there, and the courts' climbers can't come up the east end at all, which means every load goes the long way round by the west.

Kill it. It roosts on the east ramparts, this side of the stair that comes up from the Glassworks. Take a party; it's bigger than anything on the road. Bring me one of its scales to prove it, and the helm off my rack is yours, and every runner on the wall will drink to your name.
progress: The Wall Drake still roosts on the east ramparts of the Border Wall, west of the stair that comes up from the Glassworks. Kill it, and take a party: it is bigger than anything else on the road.
complete: A scale the colour of the rampart it hunted from. So it's done. I'll rig the East Stair tomorrow, which I've never dared, and then the courts can come up the wall at both ends. You've made it a hundred miles shorter for everyone who has to climb it. The helm's yours; keep the scale too. The runners will be drinking to you tonight.

s_bl_1.name: Ash Flowers

objective.label: Bring the grave-keeper 4 ash flowers for Emmer's grave

s_bl_1.desc: The Grave-Keeper Sentinel at Emmer's Grave in the Burned Land needs four Ash Flowers to dress the grave of the farm's one resident; they grow only in the ash west along the fire line, and the Ash Wights trample them.
offer: Good day. I am the Grave-Keeper Sentinel. This farm had one resident, Emmer. He is buried here, in front of his house. Residents are entitled to upkeep. Upkeep of a grave is dressing it with flowers weekly. I have kept the practice since the burial; the instruction was never rescinded.

The flowers are ash flowers. They grow in the ash and nowhere else, west of here along the fire line, the ring where the fire stopped. The ash wights walk that ground and trample the beds, and this week the beds are bare. The wights carry what they tread on; the flowers come away from them.
Bring me four ash flowers and the practice continues. Compensation will be issued from stores in accordance with standing orders. I do not have plums. I regret that in advance.
progress: The grave still requires four Ash Flowers. They grow only in the ash west along the fire line of the Burned Land, where the Ash Wights trample them; the flowers come away from the wights.
complete: Four ash flowers. The grave is dressed again, as it is every week; the practice continues. You are the first to assist with the upkeep. He would have offered you plums. I do not have plums. I regret the shortfall. Compensation from stores, as instructed.

s_bl_2.name: The Courts' Camp

objective.label: Kill 4 scorch sentinels pressing the courts' camp before the gates

s_bl_2.desc: Quartermaster Veil of the Courts' Camp before the Capital's gates wants four Scorch Sentinels put down: they walk the fire line and have begun walking straight through the camp, with every banner in the world on its way here to be fed.
offer: Quartermaster Veil, the courts' camp, and don't ask me which court: all three pay me now, and the war-chests are open. That means every banner in the world, every company of explorers under every court's colours, is marching on the Capital's gates, and every one of them will arrive hungry and expect a tent. I'm the one who has to have it standing.

The scorch sentinels are the trouble. They walk the fire line, the ring where the fire stopped, as they have for three hundred years, and lately their round comes straight through my camp: through the tent lines, over the cook-fires, as if we weren't here. They don't stop for a quartermaster.

Put down four of them. You'll meet them on the fire line south-west of the gates, where it runs closest to the camp. Do that and the banners arrive to a camp that's still standing. Take what you need from the stores after; the courts are paying, for once, without arguing.
progress: Four Scorch Sentinels still walk through the camp. Their round follows the fire line south-west of the Capital's gates, where it runs closest to the camp; meet them there.
complete: Four. The tent lines are standing, and the fires are where I left them. Four plates off them, and under each plate a work order, every one signed by the Regent: walk the line, keep the ground. Three hundred years of walking the same round, and we went and pitched a camp on it. Take what you need: a plate for yourself, and the potions. The courts are paying.

s_bl_3.name: The Glassed Stag

objective.label: Fell the Glassed Stag that walks the glassed orchard

s_bl_3.desc: Junn wants the Glassed Stag felled: a stag the flash turned to glass mid-stride in the glassed orchard west of the fire line, still walking and attacking the survey teams. She wants its antler, to see which way it was facing.
offer: Look at the glassed orchard, west of here, on the fire line. Every trunk bent away from the city, every ripple in the melt running outward: one flash from the centre, in a single morning, the morning the household left. I've put that in my report three times over. I'd like to put in one more thing, and I need you for it.

Something still walks that orchard. A stag, caught mid-stride when the flash came, run to glass where it stood and still walking. It attacks the survey teams; the courts' surveyors won't go back in while it's there, and I don't blame them.

Fell it. It walks the glassed orchard to the west; it's a big beast and glass is heavier than hide, so take a party. Bring me its antler. The glass keeps the shape the flash gave it, and I want to know whether it remembers which way it was facing.
progress: The Glassed Stag still walks the glassed orchard, west along the fire line of the Burned Land. Fell it with a party and bring its antler to me at the fire line.
complete: Its glass faces outward. Even now. Every edge of it set running away from the city, mid-stride; it was fleeing the flash, and the flash kept it exactly so. That finishes the report: the trees, the ripples, and the stag. Everything in this land faces away from the centre except us. The helm is from the surveyors' trunk; they'd like you to have it.

s_caer_1.name: The Chandler's Round

objective.label: Call at the Harbour Terrace and the Lighthouse for Chandler Mott

s_caer_1.desc: Chandler Mott at the Market Crossroads has a salt order waiting on the Harbour Terrace and lamp-wicks at the Lighthouse, and no delivery boy. Call at both for him and learn Caerdun's sea front.
offer: Chandler Mott, at your service: potions, salves, lamp-oil, and a coat that keeps the fjord out. I had a delivery boy, too, until he went to sea, which I am told is a career.

So I have two orders standing and nobody to show their face for them. My salt is waiting on the Harbour Terrace, down on the quay by the south mole, and my lamp-wicks are at the Lighthouse, out at the far end of the sea front, with Lamp-Keeper Hilde Varn.

Call at both for me. They know the order; they only need to see someone from the shop. Go down to the Harbour Terrace first, then follow the sea front out to the Lighthouse. By the time you are back you will know the whole of Caerdun's sea front, which is the only thing in this city that comes free. I will pay in potions.
progress: The Harbour Terrace first, on the quay by the south mole, then the Lighthouse at the far end of the sea front. The fish carts yield for nobody down there; walk round them.
complete: Salt and wicks, both accounted for. You have now been to both ends of Caerdun's sea front, and everything else in this city is stairs between them.
Two potions, as promised. Come back when you are stronger; I will have a longer walk for you then, with slimes at the end of it.

s_caer_2.name: A Bowl for the Sergeants

objective.label: Bring Innkeeper Sayre 3 mushroom caps from the Caerdun Fields

s_caer_2.desc: Innkeeper Sayre of the Crown Inn needs three mushroom caps for the broth the sergeants eat when they come off the wall at dawn. The caps come from cap mushnubs in the meadows of the Caerdun Fields, out past the Landward Gate.
offer: Sayre, of the Crown Inn. The sergeants come off the wall at dawn, every one of them cold through, and they want broth. The broth wants mushroom caps, and the caps are out in the Fields walking about on their own legs.
Cap mushnubs, I mean: mushroom creatures, knee high, in the meadows west of the road out past the Landward Gate. Knock one down and take the cap off it.

Bring me three caps and there is a bowl of broth in it for you. Two bowls. My family has a standing bet with the wall about who really feeds Caerdun, the inn or the garrison, so I can afford to be generous with a newcomer.
progress: Three mushroom caps. The cap mushnubs keep to the meadows west of the road in the Caerdun Fields, out through the Landward Gate. Knock them down and take the caps.
complete: Into the pot they go. This fire has not gone out since the Sealing, the night the border shut and the garrison was locked outside, and strictly speaking neither has the broth.
Two bowls, as promised. Drink one now and keep one for the road; it travels better than you would think.

s_caer_3.name: The Fields' Seams

objective.label: Bring Guildmaster Torv 3 glimmer ore from the seams in the Caerdun Fields

s_caer_3.desc: Guildmaster Torv of the Smiths' Guild wants three glimmer ore from the two seams in the Caerdun Fields, the pale rock by the pine breaks and up toward the North Road Pass, before he teaches a newcomer the hammer.
offer: Torv. I keep the Smiths' Guild. The guild will teach you the making, but the making starts with the getting, and the getting is out in the Fields.

There are two seams of iron in the Caerdun Fields: one in the pale rock by the pine breaks, one up the slope toward the North Road Pass. The ore in them glimmers, and it rings true when you strike it. Strike the seams and take what comes loose.
Bring me three lumps of glimmer ore. In return I will put a coif on your head, a gate-warden's, forged here, so you know what the ore is for before you ever lift a hammer.
progress: Three glimmer ore. The seams are the pale rock by the pine breaks and up toward the North Road Pass, in the Caerdun Fields. Strike the rock and take what comes loose.
complete: Rings true. That is the Fields' iron. The empire's iron was better, and the empire's iron is three hundred years away on the far side of the border.
Wear this: a gate-warden's coif, our make. When you have worn it a while and grown into it, come back to me; the next thing you learn is the hammer.

s_caer_4.name: Ring True

objective.label: Forge a Glimmer Band at the guild and bring it to Guildmaster Torv

s_caer_4.desc: Guildmaster Torv wants to see a Glimmer Band forged by the player's own hands at the Smiths' Guild bench in Caerdun: three glimmer ore make one band. Bring him the finished ring.
offer: You have held the ore. Now hold the hammer.

Three glimmer ore makes one Glimmer Band; that is the first recipe every smith in Caerdun learns. The guild's bench here knows the recipe. Open your crafting list, press K, find the Glimmer Band, and make it at the bench.

Then bring me the one you made yourself, not one bought off a rack. I can tell the difference by the hammer marks, and I will know from them what your hands know. There is chain from the guild's own rack waiting for a smith who has started.
progress: Forge a Glimmer Band at the guild's bench: three glimmer ore, one ring. Press K for your crafting list and find the band. Bring me the one you made.
complete: Your work. It is honest; the marks are even and the join does not show. The first thing anyone makes in this guild is a ring. The second is usually a better ring.

Here, as promised: a thornguard coif, chain from the guild's own rack, for a smith who has started. The band stays with me, on the nail above the bench with every other first ring this guild has made. You will want to know where to find it.

s_caer_5.name: Hide for the Hauberks

objective.label: Bring Armourer Brann 4 boar hides for the chain's lining

s_caer_5.desc: Armourer Brann at the Market Crossroads lines every hauberk he sells the garrison with boar hide. Bring him four boar hides from the young boars south of the watch farms and the bramble shoats in the Caerdun Fields.
offer: Brann, armourer. Chain without a lining is a cheese grater with ambitions. Every hauberk I sell the garrison is lined in boar, and I am out of boar.

The young boars in the Caerdun Fields root the watch farms, south of the road, and the bramble shoats root everything else; you will find shoats wherever the brambles grow thick. Both carry a hide worth having.
Bring me four boar hides, whole, and the next hauberk off my bench is yours, lined. That is a gate-warden's hauberk, the pattern the gate watch wears.
progress: Four boar hides. Young boars south of the watch farms, bramble shoats in the brambles, both in the Caerdun Fields. Whole hides, no tusk-holes.
complete: Good hides, not a tusk-hole in them. These will line a season's worth of hauberks for the gate watch.
And this one is lined already: a gate-warden's hauberk, yours. Put it on. It is meant to be hit and to leave you upright afterwards, which is all armour has ever been for.

s_caer_6.name: The Ferry Account

objective.label: Carry the court's ferry subsidy note to Ferrymaster Coll at the Gulf Crossing

s_caer_6.desc: Paymaster Vail needs the court's ferry subsidy note carried to Ferrymaster Coll at the Gulf Crossing, at the Ferry Landing on the west side of the Caerdun Fields. The payment is due today, and the ferryman does not come to the vault.
offer: Vail. Paymaster. The court subsidises the gulf ferry, so that Moonmere's scholars can cross the Western Gulf and be superior at us in person instead of by letter. The subsidy is paid on the day it falls due, and it falls due today.
The ferryman does not come to the vault. Vails do not go to the ferry. You will go between us.

Take this note to Ferrymaster Coll at the Gulf Crossing: out through the Landward Gate, across the Caerdun Fields to the Ferry Landing on the west side, down by the water. Hand it to him and watch him count it twice. Everyone counts twice in front of a paymaster's paper; I find it flattering.
progress: The court's ferry note goes to Ferrymaster Coll at the Gulf Crossing: the Ferry Landing, on the west side of the Caerdun Fields, down by the gulf. Hand it to him yourself.
complete: Ferrymaster Coll: The court's note. Let me count it. Let me count it again. The court's coin, on the day, to the copper. Nine generations of Vails have kept that vault and not one of them has been a day late.
Ferrymaster Coll: The gulf does what it likes, but Caerdun pays what it owes. Tell the paymaster the ferry runs. Here, a potion for the walk back; the Fields are always longer going home.

s_caer_7.name: Salve Thickener

objective.label: Bring Chandler Mott 4 slime gel from the meadow slimes

s_caer_7.desc: Chandler Mott's salves are thickened with slime gel. Bring him four slime gel from the meadow slimes south of the watch farms in the Caerdun Fields.
offer: Mott again. Every salve on that shelf is thickened with gel, and the gel comes from slimes, and the slimes are out in the Caerdun Fields being clear and faintly warm at people.
Meadow slimes. They gather south of the watch farms, out past the Landward Gate, in the low grass where the ground stays damp. Burst one and the gel is what is left of it.
Bring me four slime gel and the shelf is stocked for the season. You will get a share of what they thicken: two potions and an antidote, which is the point of the whole business.
progress: Four slime gel. The meadow slimes keep to the damp ground south of the watch farms, in the Caerdun Fields. Burst them and take what is left.
complete: Warm to the touch, every one. That is a season of salves, and the wall's cousins can stop writing to me about their knees.
Take some of the finished article: two potions and an antidote. The wall's cousins will manage without.

s_caer_8.name: Jackdaws on the Knoll

objective.label: Drive 5 beacon jackdaws off Beacon Knoll in the Caerdun Fields

s_caer_8.desc: Marshal Grett wants five beacon jackdaws driven off Beacon Knoll, north-east of Milestone Zero in the Caerdun Fields, where they nest in the old beacon post and steal the garrison's muster paper.
offer: JACKDAWS! On my beacon knoll! They nest in the old beacon post out in the Fields and they carry off anything with a seal on it: the muster sheets from my gate, the coach passengers' charter papers, the lot!
Beacon Knoll is north-east of Milestone Zero, on the way to the North Road. The birds are big and they come at you in a flock, child; think of it as a line to hold.

Drive five of them off my knoll and I will believe you have held a line. Do not bring me the paper; Watchman Dorran at the Landward Gate collects paper. Bring me the count. There are hi-potions in it; the wall drinks them by the cask.
progress: Five beacon jackdaws, off Beacon Knoll. The knoll is north-east of Milestone Zero in the Caerdun Fields, toward the North Road. I want the count, child, not the paper.
complete: Five. Wall-form third, that was: you took them one at a time and kept your feet under you. You would have made a sergeant in a slower century.
Hi-potions. The wall drinks them by the cask, so nobody will miss two. Come back when you have a few more years on you; I have longer lines for you to hold.

s_caer_9.name: Winter Lining

objective.label: Bring Armourer Brann 5 wolf pelts for the winter kit

s_caer_9.desc: Armourer Brann lines the garrison's North Road winter kit in wolf. Bring him five wolf pelts from the winter wolves on the North Road beyond the pass, or the grey wolves in the Caerdun Fields.
offer: The garrison's North Road kit is lined in wolf, because the North Road is lined in wolves. Every hood that goes up to the pass this winter wants a pelt in it, and I am five short.

Winter wolves run the North Road beyond the pass, in the snow; grey wolves run the Caerdun Fields, if you would rather stay warm while you hunt. Either pelt will do, though the winter wolf's is the thicker.
Five wolf pelts, and a Greywall helm off my rack for a head that is going up that road anyway. Greywall is the garrison's own pattern, the grey of the sea ramparts.
progress: Five wolf pelts. Winter wolves on the North Road beyond the pass, grey wolves in the Caerdun Fields. Either kind will line a hood.
complete: Winter coats, every one of them, thick enough to turn the wind on the pass. That is the garrison's hoods lined for the season.
Yours is the helm: Greywall, the garrison's pattern. You have earned the lining; the helm is so you keep the head it goes on.

s_caer_10.name: Composure

objective.label: Walk the Old Milestones to the Border Cairn on the North Road without turning back

s_caer_10.desc: Duelist-Master Sabel wants the player to learn composure the way a second does: walk the North Road from the Old Milestones to the Border Cairn, past the wolves and the Frozen Tarn, without running and without turning back.
offer: Sabel, duelist-master. Composure is half of duelling and all of being a second: the one who stands at a duelist's side with no stake in the quarrel and keeps the peace if it breaks. Nobody learns composure on a parade square. It gets learned where things want you to hurry.

So: the North Road, north-east out of the Caerdun Fields through the pass. Start at the Old Milestones, where Caerdun's ground ends, and walk the road to the Border Cairn, where Heartwood's begins. Wolves on the ridge above you. Snare lines strung across the road past the Frozen Tarn. The tarn itself, breathing at you.
Do not run. Do not hurry. Reach both stones, then come back and tell me you looked at all of it. Two ethers for the walk, which you will want by the end of it.
progress: Walk the North Road from the Old Milestones to the Border Cairn. Walk it; do not run it, and do not turn back. Look at everything that wants you to hurry.
complete: You walked it, and you came back the same shape you left in. Good. One day you will stand as a second in that ring and the whole yard will be watching you not flinch.
The road is where that gets learned; the yard only tests it. Here are your ethers. Rest the legs.

s_caer_11.name: Snares on the Pass

objective.label: Clear 5 snare spiders from the North Road pass

s_caer_11.desc: Gate-Sergeant Ottey wants five snare spiders cleared from the North Road pass, up past the Frozen Tarn, where they string webs across the road and take the coaches' mules.
offer: The North Road coach came in this morning one mule short and with a wheel full of web. Spiders. On the pass. On my road.

Snare spiders, up past the Frozen Tarn on the North Road, where the road narrows into the pass. They string the whole width of it and wait for whatever walks in. A mule is slow and cannot see a web in falling snow; neither can a coachman at night.
Clear five of them off the pass and the coaches keep their mules. There is a sword in it for you, iron: the wall's sword. The wall has spares.
progress: Five snare spiders on the North Road, up past the Frozen Tarn where the road narrows into the pass.
complete: Five snares fewer on my road, and the coachman owes you a mule's worth of thanks he will never pay.
Take the sword. Iron; keep it oiled. Steel does not know it has never been drawn in anger, and now this one has.

s_caer_12.name: The Kennel's Numbers

objective.label: Bring the Lord Marshal 3 hound collars from the King's Hounds in the Hunting Wood

s_caer_12.desc: The Lord Marshal wants three brass hound collars from the King's Hounds that run the rides of the Hunting Wood, beyond the Border Gate, so the kennel numbers can be written in Caerdun's wage book beside the garrison's dead.
offer: I am the Lord Marshal; Caerdun is mine to rule, and I keep to the parade square. I have a thing I want written down, and I want you to fetch it.

Through the Border Gate, in the Hunting Wood, the king's hounds still run the rides: three straight cuts through the forest, laid so the king could see a stag from the lodge door. Each hound wears a brass collar stamped with a kennel number, and the numbers are in the thousands. The empire kept breeding hounds for a king's sport for three hundred years, and in all that time did not once send a relief to the garrison it left outside.

Bring me three collars from the King's Hounds on the rides. Paymaster Vail will enter the numbers in the wage book beside the names of our dead. When the empire's accounting comes, I want it to be an accounting: what they spent on dogs on one page, what they owed us on the other.
progress: Three hound collars, from the King's Hounds on the rides of the Hunting Wood, through the Border Gate in the Caerdun Fields. Read the number stamped on each one.
complete: Four thousand and upward. Three centuries of hounds, each one numbered and fed. Vail will write it down tonight; the book has a page for it.
Take this from the garrison's rack: a Greywall hauberk. You are on the book now too, you understand. Every night you spend inside that border is a night of watch, and Caerdun writes those down.

s_caer_13.name: Signed by the Regent

objective.label: Bring Paymaster Vail 3 sentinel work orders bearing the Regent's signature

s_caer_13.desc: Paymaster Vail wants three sentinel work orders bearing the Regent's signature, taken from the ride wardens of the Hunting Wood, the felling sentinels of the Timber Estates or the garden sentinels of the Summer Lakes, so the garrison's invoice has a debtor's name.
offer: Vail, paymaster; this is Caerdun's wage vault, where every night the garrison has stood watch since the Sealing is written down and owed. The sentinels on the doorsteps, the empire's servants left behind to keep the interior and still at their work, carry standing orders. The orders are signed by someone called the Regent. I know nothing else about that name, and I do not need to. An invoice wants a name on the other side, and after three hundred years I have one.

The ride wardens in the Hunting Wood, the felling sentinels in the Timber Estates, the garden sentinels at the Summer Lakes: every one of them carries a work order on its person. Put one down and take the paper.
Three orders, with the signature legible. I will do the rest with a pen. Sabatons from the vault's own stores when it is done.
progress: Three work orders with the Regent's signature legible. Ride wardens in the Hunting Wood, felling sentinels in the Timber Estates, garden sentinels at the Summer Lakes: all of them carry one.
complete: 'By order of the Regent.' Three orders, three provinces, and the same hand on every one, though the paper of one is three hundred years older than the paper of the next. Whoever signs these has been signing them since the Sealing.
There is our debtor. I am writing the name into the book now, on the page facing the first night owed. Sabatons from the vault's stores; the vault noticed you, and approves.

s_caer_14.name: Hold the Crypt

objective.label: Hold the Mausoleum against 4 tomb wardens

s_caer_14.desc: Caerdun's scouts ran from the Mausoleum in the Hunting Wood. Marshal Grett wants four tomb wardens defeated in its Lantern Gallery and Long Vigil, to prove a line can be held under that roof.
offer: Marshal Grett; I command these drill yards and hold the garrison's oath. The Mausoleum. In the Hunting Wood, north-west under the ridge; the Mausoleum Door is the way in. It is the tomb of the empire's emperors, and its lamps never went out. Our scouts went in and came out at a run, and I do not train people to run.

Tomb wardens in the crypts: the tomb's own guard, armoured, and they do not ask you to leave the way the sentinels outside do. The scouts met them in the Lantern Gallery and the Long Vigil, the two long halls past the Crossing Hall.
Go in and put four of them down. Then you will have held a line under a roof that wants you dead, which is the only kind worth holding. Hi-potions from the yard's stores for it; you will use them.
progress: Four tomb wardens, in the Mausoleum in the Hunting Wood. The Mausoleum Door is north-west under the ridge; the wardens stand in the Lantern Gallery and the Long Vigil.
complete: Four. Held until relieved, and you relieved yourself, which is irregular, and I will allow it.

The scouts say the Warden of the Mausoleum is still down there at the back, in the Emperors' Vault, keeping its visitors' list, and the list has our names on it now. Someone should close it. Come to me when you are ready for that, child, and bring friends.

s_caer_15.name: The Visitors' List

objective.label: Fell the Warden of the Mausoleum and close the visitors' list

s_caer_15.desc: The Warden of the Mausoleum keeps a visitors' list three hundred years long, and Caerdun's names are the last on it. Marshal Grett wants the Warden felled in the Emperors' Vault at the back of the Mausoleum in the Hunting Wood, and the list closed.
offer: Three hundred years of names in the Warden's hand, and the last of them are ours: every Caerdun explorer who has walked into that tomb since the gates opened. I do not like being on a list I did not sign.

The Warden of the Mausoleum stands in the Emperors' Vault, the great domed room at the very back, past the Long Vigil. It is the tomb's officer of the watch, and it has been at its post since the Sealing.
Take a party. The oath says hold; it does not say hold alone. Fell the Warden and close the list. The garrison's best cuirass, and a title, for the one who does it.
progress: The Warden of the Mausoleum, in the Emperors' Vault at the back of the Mausoleum in the Hunting Wood. Take a party; the oath says hold, not hold alone.
complete: The list is closed. Three hundred years of visitors, and the last entry on it is a Caerdun explorer, written in full.
The garrison's best cuirass, Wardenbark, and the word every soldier of this city has wanted to hear for three centuries: relieved. You relieved that post. Wear the title; it is yours.

s_caer_16.name: Imperial Casing

objective.label: Bring Armourer Brann 3 sentinel plates for the guild to study

s_caer_16.desc: Armourer Brann wants three sentinel plates, shed by the ride wardens of the Hunting Wood, the felling sentinels of the Timber Estates or the tally sentinels of the Overseer's Lodge when they fall, so the guild can learn how the empire made armour that turns a blade better than anything on his rack.
offer: Brann, armourer to the garrison. Sentinel plate. Stamped with a work order, chased with nothing, plain as a shovel, and it turns a blade better than anything on my rack. I have spent my life making armour and I do not know how it is done.

The sentinels on the doorsteps shed plates when they go down: the ride wardens in the Hunting Wood, the felling sentinels in the Timber Estates, the tally sentinels in the Overseer's Lodge, through the Overseer's Door east among the Estates' ranks. Pick the plates up.
Bring me three and the guild will learn what the empire knew about iron. The cuirass I make from learning it is yours, the first of its pattern.
progress: Three sentinel plates. Ride wardens in the Hunting Wood, felling sentinels in the Timber Estates, tally sentinels in the Overseer's Lodge: each sheds plate when it falls.
complete: Look at the grain. Folded, not cast: layered steel, hammered over on itself until the whole plate is edge. Three centuries ahead of us, and now three plates behind.
Here: a Dam-Warden cuirass, the first of the new pattern, made the way these taught me. Wear it where the sentinels can see it.

s_caer_17.name: Ruled to the Millimetre

objective.label: Bring Guildmaster Torv 3 blocks of the Border Wall's masonry

s_caer_17.desc: Guildmaster Torv wants three blocks of the Border Wall's masonry, carried by the wall sentinels on the Rampart Road or sold by Wall-Runner Ketch on the wall's outer face, so the guild can learn how the empire cut stone to the millimetre.
offer: Torv, of the Smiths' Guild. The Border Wall. A hundred miles of it, closing the gaps the mountains left round the interior, and every block of it ruled to the millimetre. It is the same grey stone as our sea ramparts, and nobody who built our ramparts ever cut to a millimetre.

The wall sentinels on the Rampart Road carry blocks of it; they shed them when they fall. Wall-Runner Ketch, the freebooter who climbs the outer face, sells the same stone if you would rather pay than fight.
Three blocks. The guild wants to know how they cut it, and I want to know before the empire comes back asking why we cannot. There is a lockplate coif on the bench for you.
progress: Three wall stone from the Border Wall: from the wall sentinels on the Rampart Road, or bought from Wall-Runner Ketch on the wall's outer face.
complete: Sawn. Not chiselled, sawn, clean through granite, with something we do not have and I cannot picture. Well. That is a thing to know, even if knowing it stings.
The lockplate coif on the bench is finished; wear it while I think. The guild has three hundred years to catch up on, and the courts say there is not long to do it in.

s_caer_18.name: The Other Wall

objective.label: Clear 5 rampart sentinels from the Border Wall's road

s_caer_18.desc: Gate-Sergeant Ottey wants five rampart sentinels cleared from the Rampart Road of the Border Wall, so the courts' embassy camped on the wall can walk its own rampart.
offer: Ottey, gate-sergeant; I keep the muster for this city's wall. There is a wall up there, the Border Wall, that has been walked every night for three hundred years by things that do not have knees. Rampart sentinels. I have walked ours every night on knees that complain, and I take it personally.

The courts have an embassy camped on the Border Wall now, the Embassy's Camp, and the rampart sentinels patrol the Rampart Road straight through it as if nobody were there. Our people cannot walk their own stretch of wall.

Clear five rampart sentinels off the Rampart Road. Then the embassy walks its own rampart, and then you and I will talk about who is up top in the Great Watchtower. X-potions for it; the wall sent a cask.
progress: Five rampart sentinels on the Rampart Road of the Border Wall, the stretch by the Embassy's Camp. Clear them so the embassy can walk its own rampart.
complete: Five. The wall reported your climb, I am told; the sentinels log every soul that goes up. Let it report this too.
Take the x-potions. When you have your breath, come back: the thing that seals those reports sits at the top of the Great Watchtower, and I want a word with it. Through you.

s_caer_19.name: Relieved at the Wall

objective.label: Fell the Wall-Warden in the Great Watchtower

s_caer_19.desc: The Wall-Warden, the Great Watchtower's officer of the watch, has been on duty for three hundred years and seals every dispatch the Border Wall sends. Gate-Sergeant Ottey wants it felled at the top of the Great Watchtower, and the word 'relieved' said to it.
offer: The Wall-Warden. It is the Great Watchtower's officer of the watch, on duty three hundred years without a relief, and every dispatch the wall sends out goes under its seal. It is the nearest thing that wall has to a sergeant.

The Great Watchtower stands on the Border Wall, up the Rampart Road from the Embassy's Camp, and the Warden keeps the top of it. Take a party up it. The Warden does not fight alone, and neither should you.

Relieve it. Fell it, I mean, but say the word to it first: relieved. Our oath is hold until relieved, and nobody ever relieved us. I want to know if it knows the word. The wall's own coif for whoever does it, and an x-potion.
progress: The Wall-Warden, at the top of the Great Watchtower, up the Rampart Road on the Border Wall. Take a party up the stair. Say the word to it before it falls: relieved.
complete: Relieved. Did it hear the word? You cannot be sure. Well. It does not matter: it has been said, on that wall, by one of ours, and that is three hundred years late and not too late.
The wall's coif, off the wall's own rack: a rampart coif, and the potion. Go and stand somewhere warm. You have earned a fire.

s_caer_20.name: What Stood Before

objective.label: Fell 4 ash giants in the Burned Land

s_caer_20.desc: Ash giants are taking the pickets from the courts' camp before the Capital's gates in the Burned Land. The Lord Marshal wants four of them felled on the ash roads, and wants to know what they were before the fire.
offer: The Lord Marshal, ruler of Caerdun. The Burned Land, the ring of ash round the capital. The courts have a camp there now, before the Capital's gates, and the ash giants that walk the ash roads are taking its pickets at night. Nobody knows what the giants were before the fire, and I have a garrison's worth of guesses.
Fell four of them on the ash roads and the camp stops losing pickets. That is the order.
Then do one thing more: bring me a tooth. I want to know whether they were ever people, and if they were, whether they were ours. Cinderguard sabatons from the courts' war-chest for the work.
progress: Four ash giants, on the ash roads of the Burned Land near the courts' camp before the gates. Keep a tooth from one of them for me.
complete: Four. And the tooth is human. So they were people once, whoever they were. I will not say more than that until I know more than that.

Sabatons from the courts' war-chest, Cinderguard: walk on the ash in them. And know that Caerdun has written your four down. The garrison held on the empire's own order, and an order is billable; so is every night you have stood in that land.

s_caer_21.name: The Regent's Reply

objective.label: Read the Regent's Reply, posted at the Embassy's camp on the Border Wall

s_caer_21.desc: The courts' embassy on the Border Wall received a reply from the Regent, now posted at the Embassy's Camp. Paymaster Vail wants it read in full, word for word, and the exact wording brought back to the Wage Vaults.
offer: Vail, Caerdun's paymaster. The embassy on the Border Wall, the three courts' letters to whoever commands inside, received a reply. A reply. Three hundred years of invoices from this vault and not one word back, and the courts write one letter and are answered the same hour.
It is posted at the Embassy's Camp on the Border Wall, on the camp's post, for any explorer to read. Go up and read it. All of it: the address, the body, the signature.
Then come back and tell me the exact wording. Not the gist. Vails do not work from summaries, and I will know if you have given me one.
progress: The Regent's Reply, on the post at the Embassy's Camp on the Border Wall. Read it all, address to signature, and bring me the exact words.
complete: 'To the caretaker governments of the free cities.' Caretaker. Nine generations of my family kept this room, every night of watch valued and owed, and they call us caretakers.
Well. Caretakers keep the receipts. It wants an accounting of our stewardship; it will have one, and it will be itemised. Ethers for the climb. Go and rest; I have a great deal to write.

s_heart_1.name: Fetch My Tea

objective.label: Ask Innkeeper Tamsin at the Elder's Rest to prepare Mother Alder's tea

s_heart_1.desc: Mother Alder, the oldest chanter on the Song-Steps, wants her tea and nobody will fetch it. Ask Innkeeper Tamsin at the Elder's Rest, the inn on the west side of Heartwood, to put the kettle on.
offer: You. Yes, you, the new one. I am Mother Alder, the oldest chanter in this city; I have buried two Speakers, and my tea is at the Elder's Rest while I am on the Song-Steps, and not one of these children will fetch it because they are 'rehearsing'.

The Elder's Rest is the inn on the west side of the city, under the elder's boughs. Go down off the steps, west through the Grove Ring and past the crossroads, and you'll find it. Innkeeper Tamsin keeps it.

Tell her Mother Alder wants the usual leaf, piping hot, and that she knows what the usual leaf is. She can send the cup up with the next tray to the Song-Steps; you need only get her to put the kettle on. There's a potion in it for you, and my good opinion, which is worth more and harder to come by.
progress: Ask Innkeeper Tamsin, at the Elder's Rest on the west side of the city, to put the kettle on for Mother Alder: the usual leaf, piping hot, sent up with the next tray to the Song-Steps.
complete: Mother Alder's tea? Again? And she's sent the newest face in the city for it, which means she likes you, so don't waste it. The kettle's on now; I'll send her cup up with the next tray to the Song-Steps, the usual leaf, as hot as she can stand it.
You've done your part. Sit a minute if you like; the stew here has a verse of its own, and you'll be back for it.

s_heart_2.name: Frog Legs by the Verse

objective.label: Bring Grocer Nell 4 frog legs from the brook in the Heartwood Fields

s_heart_2.desc: Grocer Nell at Heartwood's crossroads wants four frog legs from the brook frogs in the mill brook in the Heartwood Fields. She will fry two for the explorer and sell the rest at the board price.
offer: Grocer Nell, the crossroads. Potions, remedies, travelling clothes, and frog legs when I can get them. Heartwood eats frog legs; Caerdun pretends not to and buys them by the barrel through a cousin, and I know the cousin.

I'm short of legs. The brook frogs are in the mill brook in the Heartwood Fields: out through the West Gate, and down to the water below the Mill on the Brook, north-east of the Fields' crossroads. Fat ones this time of year, and they'll come at you, so you needn't feel bad about it.

Bring me four legs. I'll fry two for you, with the song that goes with frying, and the other two go on the board at the board price, like everyone else's. Nobody haggles with Nell; the song for haggling has nine verses and I know all nine.
progress: Four frog legs for Grocer Nell. The brook frogs are in the mill brook in the Heartwood Fields, below the Mill on the Brook, north-east of the Fields' crossroads. They'll come to you.
complete: Fat ones. Good. The song for frying has three verses: one for the fat, one for the heat, and the third is just 'don't touch the pan', over and over, because somebody always does. Here, two plates of legs, hot. Eat them before you go anywhere; the rest go on the board.

s_heart_3.name: Reed for the Loom

objective.label: Bring Woodwright Hollis 3 mere reed for the guild's loom

s_heart_3.desc: Woodwright Hollis at the Woodwrights' Guild wants three mere reed for the guild's loom, cut from the reed beds at the north and south edges of the Heartwood Fields.
offer: Hollis, woodwright. The guild teaches leatherwork, weaving and the shaping of what the wood gives, and weaving starts with reed, and reed starts with wet feet.

There are reed beds in the Heartwood Fields: one at the north edge, where the brook runs out above the mill, and one down at the south edge of the Fields. Cut me three mere reed, the hollow kind that whistles when the wind gets in it; you'll hear a bed before you see it.
Bring them here and the guild will show you the loom. The hood that comes off it is yours, and I'll have something harder for you after, once your hands have learned something.
progress: Three mere reed, hollow and whistling, from the reed beds in the Heartwood Fields: the one at the north edge above the mill, or the one at the south edge. Bring them to Hollis at the Woodwrights' Guild.
complete: Good reed. It whistles in a north wind, which the loom doesn't mind and the weavers do. Your hood, off the loom you've just fed. Now, when you've the weight for it, come back; there's a ring the guild has made since before the empire left, and I want your hands to learn it.

s_heart_4.name: Thorn and Tusk

objective.label: Bring Woodwright Hollis a Thorn Band; the guild's pattern is in your crafting book

s_heart_4.desc: Woodwright Hollis wants a Thorn Band, the ring the Woodwrights' Guild has made since before the empire left: thorn resin set round two boar tusks. Make one from the guild's pattern in the crafting book (three thorn resin, two boar tusks) or find a sound one, and bring it to the guild.
offer: The harder thing. There's a ring the guild has made since before the empire left: thorn resin, warmed and set round two boar tusks until it grips them. We call it the Thorn Band. Press K and you'll find our pattern in your crafting book; it's a smith's working, and you can do it anywhere you have the materials and a fire.

It takes three thorn resin and two boar tusks. The young thornfangs about the orchards in the Fields carry the resin, and the bramble boars by the Border Gate carry the tusks; or you'll find both at the auction house, if your knife is slow.

Make one, or find a sound example from another crafter, and bring it here. A good ring can teach a pair of hands as much as a lesson can; I want yours to have held one. There's a vest off the guild's rack for you when it's done.
progress: One Thorn Band for Hollis at the Woodwrights' Guild. The pattern is in your crafting book under smithing: three thorn resin, two boar tusks. Make it yourself, or buy one sound from another crafter.
complete: Set clean. Look here, at how the resin seats the tusks, how it grips without a pin: that's the lesson, and now your hands know it. The band stays with the guild; the knowing stays with you. The vest is from the guild's rack; wear it into the woods that made it.

s_heart_5.name: A Verse for the Stew

objective.label: Bring Innkeeper Tamsin 2 windfall tarts

s_heart_5.desc: Innkeeper Tamsin at the Elder's Rest has forgotten the middle of the windfall tart's song. Bring her two windfall tarts, baked from three windfall apples each by the cooking pattern or bought from Auntie Wren at the Halfway Inn, and she will remember the verse.
offer: The stew has a verse. The tart has a whole song, and I've forgotten the middle of it, and an innkeeper who can't sing her own tarts is a disgrace to the elder she sleeps under.

I need the tart in my hands to find it; the words are in the smell. Windfall tart: three windfall apples to a tart if you follow the cooking pattern in your crafting book, and the apples are lying under the trees at the Wild Orchards in the Fields, ground fruit only, never picked. Or, if you'd rather walk than bake, Auntie Wren sells them at the Halfway Inn on the North Road, and don't tell her I said so.
Two tarts, and I'll remember the verse and sing it to you, and there's two flasks of my hot stew for the road besides. It burns warm going down; you'll want that where you're going.
progress: Two windfall tarts for Tamsin at the Elder's Rest. Bake them yourself from three windfall apples each, picked up under the Wild Orchards in the Heartwood Fields, or buy them from Auntie Wren at the Halfway Inn on the North Road.
complete: There it is. There it is! 'Three to the tin and the fourth to the cook.' I knew the middle was about stealing; every good kitchen verse is. Thank you, love.
Two flasks of hot stew, lidded, as promised. A warm kitchen's no use to a traveller who's three days from the door.

s_heart_6.name: Where the Verses Live

objective.label: Stand at the Mill, the Charcoal Camps and the Ridge Path in the Heartwood Fields

s_heart_6.desc: Chanter Ives at the Song-Steps says every verse of Heartwood's counting-song belongs to a place. Stand and listen at the Mill on the Brook, the Charcoal Camps and the Ridge Path in the Heartwood Fields, then sing them back on the Song-Steps.
offer: Stop slouching; you'll dent the note before you've sung it. Now listen. Every verse in the counting-song, the old song this city keeps one verse to a family, belongs to a place. The words came out of a place, and a voice that's never stood there sings them wrong, every time, and I can hear it.

Three places, all in the Heartwood Fields, out through the West Gate. The Mill on the Brook, north-east of the Fields' crossroads, where the wheel turns for nobody; the Charcoal Camps in the south, where the clamps smoke; and the Ridge Path, up on the high ground in the far west, south of the Border Gate.

Stand at each one and listen. Don't talk, don't hum: listen. The wheel, the fire, the wind on the ridge. Then come back to the Song-Steps and sing the three verses back to me. There's ether for you after; singing is thirsty work, and so is walking.
progress: Stand and listen at the Mill on the Brook, the Charcoal Camps and the Ridge Path, all in the Heartwood Fields, then come back to Chanter Ives on the Song-Steps and sing the verses back.
complete: Better. Much better; the camps verse has smoke in it now, and the ridge verse has wind. The mill verse still wobbles on the turn of the wheel; go back one day and sit with Old Tammon by the brook, he's sat there longer than the wheel has. The rest you've got.
Ether, two. Drink one now; I can hear your throat from here.

s_heart_7.name: Fox for the Collars

objective.label: Bring Tanner Wick 4 fox pelts for the chanters' collars

s_heart_7.desc: Tanner Wick at Heartwood's crossroads wants four fox pelts from the red foxes around the Wild Orchards in the Heartwood Fields, to make collars for four chanters.
offer: Wick, tanner, the crossroads. Everything on this rack was a boar or a tree first; Heartwood wastes nothing. Every chanter's collar is fox: rust-red, sheds water, and a fox has usually stolen something, so it's a moral lesson as well as a collar.

I've four chanters waiting on collars and no fox. The red foxes run about the Wild Orchards in the Heartwood Fields, north of the Fields' crossroads, after Petta's windfall and whatever else they can carry. Four pelts; the trade calls them marsh-fox pelts whatever fox they came off, and don't ask me why.
Bring them here and there's a wayfarer's cap for you off the bench, and the chanters' thanks, which they'll sing at you whether you want it or not.
progress: Four fox pelts for Tanner Wick at Heartwood's crossroads. The red foxes are about the Wild Orchards in the Heartwood Fields, north of the Fields' crossroads. The trade calls the pelt marsh-fox.
complete: Good and red, all four, and not a tooth-mark on them. Four collars, four chanters, and four fewer foxes in Petta's orchards, so she owes me a pie and doesn't know it yet. The chanters will be on the Song-Steps in these by the week's end; look for the red at the neck and you'll know whose hands cut it.
The cap's yours, off the bench. It was a boar first.

s_heart_8.name: Grave-Robbers

objective.label: Drive 5 barrow diggers from the displaced families' graves in the Fields

s_heart_8.desc: Barrow diggers are digging up the graves of the families the empire moved off their land, in the Heartwood Fields between the Wild Orchards and the Border Gate. Grudge-Keeper Morrow wants five of them killed, for the digging itself.
offer: Wipe your feet; the floor is grudges. I'm Morrow, grudge-keeper. This hall's floor records everything the empire took from Heartwood: every grove felled, every family moved at pike-point so the empire could lay out its King's Gardens inside the border. People call us bitter. We prefer accurate.

Here is today's entry. Something is digging up the graves of those families, the ones who were moved, and died out here, and were buried in the Fields. Barrow diggers: badger-sized, spade-clawed, and they drag the grave-goods down into their setts. They dig in the west of the Heartwood Fields, between the Wild Orchards and the Border Gate, in the open ground under the ridge.

Kill five of them. Not for the goods; the hall has hands to dig those back. For the digging. A grave is a record, and I am adding whatever disturbs one to the floor. Two hi-potions when it's done, and a place on the floor for the deed.
progress: Five barrow diggers, in the west of the Heartwood Fields, between the Wild Orchards and the Border Gate, in the open ground under the ridge. Morrow wants them dead for the digging itself.
complete: Five. Then the graves lie quiet tonight, and the families who visit the hall on Thursday will find them whole. The hall records a grudge, and it records when it's answered; this one's answered, and the floor has your name against it.
Two hi-potions. Wipe your feet on the way out as well; you've earned the right to the floor, and the floor is still grudges.

s_heart_9.name: Antler for the Ring

objective.label: Bring the Speaker of the Ring 3 elder antlers

s_heart_9.desc: The Speaker of the Ring wants three elder antlers for the Grove Ring, which keeps everything the wood gives. The old stags in the south of the Heartwood Fields shed them, as do the striders on the Moonmere Shores and the ridge stags of the North Road.
offer: Sit under the ring with me, child; it's rude to talk about the trees where they can't hear. These four elders are the Grove Ring, and the families who sit beneath them are the ring too, and I am only the one who speaks for it.

The old stags shed their antlers under the elders every spring, and the ring keeps them at the elders' feet, as the ring keeps everything the wood gives. This year the store is three short, because the woodwrights borrowed them, and the ring does not like a short store. I want three elder antlers to make it whole.

The old stags graze in the south of the Heartwood Fields, down toward the Shore Road, and they'll fight you for their crowns. If you've crossed the water, the mire striders on the Moonmere Shores carry antler too, and so do the ridge stags of the North Road. A hunt of your own, or another hunter's; the ring doesn't mind.
Bring the three here and sit with me under the trees while I set them down, where they can hear you. There's a band in it for you, one the ring has been keeping.
progress: Three elder antlers for the Speaker at the Grove Ring. The old stags graze in the south of the Heartwood Fields toward the Shore Road; the mire striders of the Moonmere Shores and the ridge stags of the North Road carry antler too.
complete: Three. The ring thanks you, child; I'm only the one who talks. They'll go at the foot of the north elder, with the ones the stags gave, and the store is whole again.

This band was cut from a thorn that grew up through a shed antler and set round it, years ago, until nobody could say which was holding which. It knows the difference between a guard and a wall. Wear it where that matters.

s_heart_10.name: Two Inns

objective.label: Carry Tamsin's recipe letter to Auntie Wren at the Halfway Inn

s_heart_10.desc: Innkeeper Tamsin wants her sealed recipe letter carried by hand to Auntie Wren at the Halfway Inn on the North Road, because she is sure the coach reads them. Wren will feed the bearer.
offer: Auntie Wren, who keeps the Halfway Inn on the North Road, and I have been swapping recipes by coach for twenty years, and the coach reads them. I know it does. Her broth has my thyme in it, and it did not have my thyme in it before I wrote the thyme down and put it on the coach.

So this one goes by hand, sealed, and the seal comes back to me unbroken or I'll know. Take it west through the Heartwood Fields and out the north-west corner onto the North Road, then follow the road west to the inn; it sits halfway to Caerdun, on neither city's ground. Give it to Wren and nobody else.

She'll feed you; she feeds everybody, it's compulsive. That's the whole of our disagreement, if you want the truth: two women who can't let anyone leave hungry, arguing about whose thyme it is. She'll send you off with broth for the road. Taste it, and come and tell me one day if that's my thyme.
progress: Carry Tamsin's sealed letter to Auntie Wren at the Halfway Inn: west through the Heartwood Fields, out the north-west corner onto the North Road, then west along the road to the inn.
complete: From Tamsin? Sealed, is it? She still thinks the coach reads them. Love, the coach can't read; Coachman Pell can barely read the milestones. Sit. Eat. Nobody carries a letter this far on an empty stomach, not in my house.

Take two bowls of broth back to her with my compliments, and tell her from me that the thyme was mine first, and I've the recipe to prove it, in my own hand, from before she was keeping an inn. Go on. Stamp your boots on the way out.

s_heart_11.name: Winter Wolf Leather

objective.label: Bring Tanner Wick 4 wolf pelts for a waywatcher's jerkin

s_heart_11.desc: Tanner Wick wants four wolf pelts from the winter wolves of the North Road to make a waywatcher's jerkin, the kit Heartwood's road-watchers wear.
offer: The waywatchers, the ones who walk the roads out of Heartwood and come back with the news, wear winter wolf: thick, grey, and it's already been up the North Road, so it knows the way. That's the joke the waywatchers make. I don't make it; I make the jerkins.

I'm short of pelts. The winter wolves run the North Road, in the snow country beyond the Heartwood Fields' north-west corner; you'll find packs along the road on either side of the Halfway Inn, up on the Wold and down by the cliff coast. Four pelts, whole.
Bring them here and the jerkin is yours; that's the trade, that's always been the trade. Four pelts for the jerkin, since my grandfather's day.
progress: Four wolf pelts for Tanner Wick at Heartwood's crossroads. Winter wolves run the North Road on either side of the Halfway Inn: the Wold, the Rime Cut, the cliff coast. Whole pelts.
complete: Winter coats, thick as they come, and the grey's right the whole way through. Everything on this rack was a boar or a tree first, and now a wolf; Heartwood wastes nothing, including the North Road. The jerkin's yours, off the bench; your pelts go into the next one. It's been to the pass before you; let it show you the way, and keep the snow off while it does.

s_heart_12.name: The Song the Cold Keeps

objective.label: Lay 6 rime sprites to rest at the Frozen Tarn on the North Road

s_heart_12.desc: Mother Alder says the rime sprites at the Frozen Tarn on the North Road sing the last line of a banned verse wrong. Lay six of them to rest and she will teach the line the way it goes.
offer: There is a verse about the frozen tarn on the North Road. The empire banned it, with the rest of our war-songs, and my grandmother kept it anyway, in her chest, the way this city keeps everything. I have it from her. Nobody else living has it.

And the rime sprites at the tarn, the little cold things that gather on the ice, are still singing the last line of it. Wrong. They have been singing it wrong for three hundred years, in the one place in the world the verse belongs to, and it sets my teeth every time the wind comes from the north.

Go up the North Road to the Frozen Tarn; it lies off the road not far from the Halfway Inn. Lay six of the rime sprites to rest, and come back to me on the Song-Steps and I'll teach you the line the way it goes. Fetch my tea first. No. Go. Tea after. There's a hood for you when it's done, a good one.
progress: Six rime sprites, at the Frozen Tarn on the North Road, off the road near the Halfway Inn. Lay them to rest and come back to Mother Alder on the Song-Steps for the line.
complete: Six. Then the tarn's quiet, and the only voice left on that ice is the right one, which is mine. Now, come close: the line goes down where they took it up. Down, the whole last word, like something set on the ground and not dropped. Again. Again. And you don't slouch while you sing it.
The hood was my son's. He walked the North Road in it for years, and he'd want it walked in, not kept in a chest with the verses. Go on. And somebody fetch my tea.

s_heart_13.name: Stop the Felling

objective.label: Stop 5 felling sentinels in the Timber Estates

s_heart_13.desc: Beyond the Border Gate the empire's felling sentinels are still cutting the Timber Estates, three hundred years on, where Heartwood's groves once stood. The Speaker of the Ring wants five of them stopped so the ring can hear the saws fall silent.
offer: Sit, child. The Border Gate is open to you now, with the courts' letters, and you've seen what's behind it: the Timber Estates, every grove the empire felled out of Heartwood, planted back in rows straight as a rule.

The sentinels in the Estates are still felling. The empire's caretakers, the metal ones; the felling sentinels, with the saws. Three hundred years, and the saws have not stopped once. Every tree they cut is imperial stock planted where a Heartwood grove stood, and they cut it on orders three hundred years old that nobody has ever told them to stop. On a still night the ring can hear them from here. The trees can hear them.

Stop five of the felling sentinels. They work the Felled Block, by the Haul Road in the Estates' west, and up on the scarp at the Old Wood, where the last of the old trees still stand and the saws are closest to them. Five, and the saws go quiet long enough for the ring to hear it. Then come back and sit, and tell the elders. There are boots for you from the Thornhide set; there's thorn in every step of them.
progress: Five felling sentinels, in the Timber Estates beyond the Border Gate: at the Felled Block by the Haul Road, and up on the scarp at the Old Wood where the last old trees stand. Then return to the Speaker at the Grove Ring.
complete: The saws stopped. We heard it here, under the elders, at dusk: a quiet that hadn't been in the air for three hundred years. For an hour, child, only an hour, before the rest of them took up the work again. But they stopped, and the ring heard it, and the trees heard it, and that is in the ring's memory now, where nothing is lost.
Boots, for the Felled Block; Thornhide, Heartwood's own. There's thorn in every step of them, and so there should be.

s_heart_14.name: What the Roots Kept

objective.label: Bring Woodwright Hollis 3 root amber from the Estates and the Wood

s_heart_14.desc: Woodwright Hollis wants three root amber, sap turned to stone round something still moving, from the root creepers of the Timber Estates or the elder stags of the Hunting Wood, so the Woodwrights' Guild can learn to set it.
offer: Root amber. Sap turned to stone round something that still moves; hold a piece to the light and you'll see it turn. The Timber Estates are full of it, because the Estates are full of things the wood didn't finish with before the empire cut it down and planted over it.

The guild has never set it, and I want it to. Three pieces. The root creepers carry it in the Estates, about the Felled Block and the Log Flume in the west; the elder stags of the Hunting Wood, beyond Caerdun's Border Gate, have it grown into their antlers, down by the Hart's Pool; and the bramble boars by the Border Gate here in the Fields root it up now and again.
Three, and the guild learns to set it, with me making the mistakes first. The trews I make while I'm learning are yours: thornhide, and they'll be the better for the amber at the knee.
progress: Three root amber for Hollis at the Woodwrights' Guild. Root creepers in the Timber Estates about the Felled Block and the Log Flume; elder stags in the Hunting Wood by the Hart's Pool; bramble boars by the Fields' Border Gate.
complete: Look at that. Something's moving in every one; turn it and it turns back. The guild's never set a stone that argues with the setting before, and now it has, three times, and I've the burns to show for it.

Your trews. Thornhide, with the amber set at the knee; they'll stop arguing there, and so will whatever hits them. Wear them into the Estates and let the rows see what Heartwood does with what they left in the ground.

s_heart_15.name: The Rota

objective.label: Silence 4 shift clerks in the Overseer's Lodge

s_heart_15.desc: In the Overseer's Lodge, the empire's office in the Timber Estates, shift clerks are still marking the felling rota against Heartwood's groves after three hundred years. Grudge-Keeper Morrow wants four of them silenced so the hall's readers can recover their orders.
offer: The Overseer's Lodge, in the Timber Estates, is the office the empire ran the Estates from, and it keeps a rota. Every grove they felled has a shift written against it, who cut it and on which day, and the clerks are still marking the shifts. Metal clerks, sentinels, bent over the rota three hundred years after the last foreman walked out of the door. I've read the copies. I'd like the originals.

Go in by the Overseer's Door, in the north-east of the Estates. The clerks work the Clerks' Hall just inside, the Rota Hall beyond it, and the room they call Centuries of Ledgers, deeper in. Silence four of them, and the rota hall is quiet enough for the hall's readers to go in behind you and recover the clerks' orders.

Then report to me. The hall's floor has room for what they wrote down; the hall's floor always has room. Two hi-potions for the lodge, and one of the orders stays with you when the readers are done, so you know what we're reading.
progress: Four shift clerks, in the Overseer's Lodge in the Timber Estates, in by the Overseer's Door: the Clerks' Hall, the Rota Hall and Centuries of Ledgers. Then report to Morrow at the Grudge Hall.
complete: Four. The rota's short four hands, and the readers are in. Here's your copy of what the clerks were holding: a sentinel's standing order, the same words on every page for three hundred years. 'Keep the rides. Keep well.' The rides are the lanes cut between the rows. They were told to look after the place, and they did, and nobody told them whose place it had been first.

And one more thing the readers found. Under the lodge, in a side chamber, something is growing. Not imperial stock; ours. Heartwood stock, grown in their rows, under the roof that counted our groves. Someone should go and ask it what it remembers. Come back to me when you've a party at your back, and I'll tell you what it is.

s_heart_16.name: The Rootbound Warden

objective.label: Fell the Rootbound Warden beneath the Overseer's Lodge

s_heart_16.desc: Beneath the Overseer's Lodge grows the Rootbound Warden, a thing grown from Heartwood stock in imperial rows under the roof that counted Heartwood's groves. Grudge-Keeper Morrow wants it felled, with a party, and its heartwood returned to the ground.
offer: The readers have named it. The Rootbound Warden: grown from Heartwood stock, from the groves they felled, planted in imperial rows under the lodge that counted our groves, and left to stand guard over the counting. It is the grudge, standing up.

It's in the side chamber of the Overseer's Lodge, off the Rota Hall toward the Hound Court, past where you silenced the clerks. Take a party; the trees will forgive you for not going alone, they have never once gone anywhere alone. Fell it, and report to me. Let its heartwood go back into the ground that made it, not the floor of their lodge.
The hall's own jerkin is yours after, Thornhide, and a name the ring will use for you. I don't do this often. Note that I'm doing it.
progress: The Rootbound Warden, in the side chamber of the Overseer's Lodge in the Timber Estates, off the Rota Hall toward the Hound Court. Take a party. Fell it and report to Morrow at the Grudge Hall.
complete: Then its watch is ended, and the lodge has nothing of ours left standing in it. Every grove they felled was going to be a tree like that one, and they made it a warden instead, and set it to guard the rota that counted its own felling. The floor takes the record of your deed, in full, the way it takes everything.

The jerkin is the hall's; Thornhide, Heartwood's own pattern. Wear it to the appointments. And the ring will call you Keeper of the Grove from today, which is a thing the ring has not called anyone since the Felling, the year the empire cut our groves. Wipe your feet.

s_heart_17.name: Drakescale

objective.label: Bring Tanner Wick 4 drake scales for a sounder's cap

s_heart_17.desc: Tanner Wick wants four drake scales for a sounder's cap, the kit of the explorers who sound the Reservoir's drowned valley. The loch drakes of the Summer Lakes and the bed drakes of the Reservoir carry them.
offer: Drake scale over wolf. That's the sounders' kit for the Reservoir, where the courts have their joint camp now; the sounders are the ones who wade the drowned village testing the ground with a pole, and everything there is wet and half of it bites, so they want scale.

Four drake scales. The loch drakes at the Summer Lakes, Moonmere's doorstep, carry them; they haul out on the Boathouse Crescent and by the Walled Orchard. So do the bed drakes at the Reservoir itself, in the shallows under the Orchard Terraces. And if you're passing the Moonmere Shores, the mireback drakelings by the North Gate carry scale too.
Bring the four here, unchipped, and the first cap off the bench is yours. Heartwood wastes nothing, and that includes a drake.
progress: Four drake scales for Tanner Wick, unchipped. Loch drakes at the Summer Lakes, on the Boathouse Crescent and by the Walled Orchard; bed drakes at the Reservoir, in the shallows under the Orchard Terraces.
complete: Four scales, no chips. That's four caps, and yours is the first: drake over wolf over boar, and all of it was something else before it was yours. Heartwood wastes nothing, including you. Mind that in the valley; the sounders who come back are the ones who tested the ground first.

s_heart_18.name: A Flower in the Dark

objective.label: Bring Chanter Ives 3 pale petals from the King's Gardens

s_heart_18.desc: A verse of the counting-song tells of a flower that blooms without light, unseen for three hundred years. Chanter Ives wants three pale petals from the King's Gardens, where the pale blooms grow on the northern terraces and the pale stags and garden panthers carry their petals, to prove the verse true.
offer: There's a verse in the counting-song about a flower that blooms without light, in the dark, where no sun gets. Nobody in Heartwood has seen one in three hundred years, and there are chanters who'll tell you it's a pretty line and nothing more. I have never believed that about any line in that song.

Petta says they're in the King's Gardens, the empire's pleasure grounds beyond the Timber Estates, out along the Gardens Road, laid out on the land our families were moved off. The pale blooms themselves grow on the terraces in the north of the Gardens, above the Great Stair and up by the Cleared Row, where Heartwood's houses stood; they move, Petta says, and they don't care to be picked. The pale stags that graze in the east of the Gardens carry the petals caught in their coats, and the garden panthers that hunt there carry them too. Take them from whichever you meet.

Bring me three pale petals. Three, and I'll know if the verse is true or just pretty, and I'll know what to teach the children when they ask. There's a cap for you from the Gardens road, and don't slouch on the way there; the Gardens have staff.
progress: Three pale petals for Chanter Ives on the Song-Steps. The pale blooms on the northern terraces of the King's Gardens drop them, above the Great Stair and by the Cleared Row; the pale stags in the east and the garden panthers carry them too.
complete: It's true. Look at it: it's giving off its own light, in my hand, on the Song-Steps, in the middle of the day. Blooms in the dark. The verse was never pretty, it was a description; somebody stood in the Gardens three hundred years ago and wrote down what they saw, and gave it to us to carry.
Every verse in that song is a receipt. Every one. The cap is from the Gardens road; wear it there, and when you see the blooms again, sing them the verse. They've waited long enough to hear it.

s_heart_19.name: The Count

objective.label: Stop 5 count sentinels in the Great Granary

s_heart_19.desc: In the Great Granary on the Granary Plains, count sentinels tally forty towers of grain filling for a city that is not there. The Speaker of the Ring wants five of them stopped, to see what happens when the count is wrong for the first time in three hundred years.
offer: Sit, child. You've been to the Granary Plains; the courts talk of nothing else. Forty towers, filled and filling, for a city that isn't there, and inside the Great Granary the count sentinels tally every sack that goes in. They have never once been wrong, and they have never once asked why.
The ring wants to know what happens when the count is wrong. Not out of spite; out of need. Everything the empire built in there runs on being right, and we have never seen it be anything else.

Go into the Great Granary, the halls under the towers, and stop five of the count sentinels. They work the Count Floor, at the heart of the place, and the passage before the Granary-Master's Office beyond it. Five, and for the first time in three hundred years the number in that granary will not match the grain. Then come back under the elders and tell me what the place did.
progress: Five count sentinels in the Great Granary on the Granary Plains: the Count Floor at its heart, and the passage before the Granary-Master's Office. Then return to the Speaker at the Grove Ring.
complete: The count is wrong, and nothing happened. The towers didn't open. The harvesters didn't stop. Nothing came to put it right. Which is the answer, isn't it, child: the count was never for them to check. It was for someone else to read, later. The Granary-Master will be along to correct it in its own time; it keeps the ledger the count feeds.
Someone should be there first. Rest, and come back to me; I'll tell you what the ring wants of the master.

s_heart_20.name: Enough to Feed Their City

objective.label: Fell the Granary-Master in its office in the Great Granary

s_heart_20.desc: The Granary-Master keeps the Great Granary's provisioning ledger: forty towers of wheat for the empire's homecoming, grown on land that was Heartwood's. The Speaker of the Ring wants it felled, with a party, so the hall's readers can bring the ledger home.
offer: The Granary-Master keeps the provisioning ledger: forty towers of wheat, so much a day for so many mouths, from the morning they come home. Enough to feed their city. And the land it grows on, child, was ours. Heartwood's groves, felled in the Felling, the year the empire cut them, and the ground ploughed and sown with their wheat.

It sits in its office at the back of the Great Granary, past the Count Floor where you stopped the counters, at the far end of the place. Take a party; it has kept that office three hundred years, and it will not give the ledger up to one pair of hands.

Fell the master and report to me. Our readers will go in behind you and recover the ledger from the cleared office, and the ring will hear every acre of it read aloud beneath the elders, grove by grove. That is what the ring is for.
progress: The Granary-Master, in its office at the back of the Great Granary on the Granary Plains, past the Count Floor. Take a party. Fell it and report to the Speaker at the Grove Ring.
complete: The office is clear, and our readers are in it now. They've sent the first pages ahead. It is what we knew it was: Heartwood's groves, listed by name, felled, cleared, planted with wheat, for them, for the day they come home. Every acre will be read beneath the elders, and the trees will hear what grew where they should have.

Take the jerkin; it's bargeman's leather, and the barges carried our timber down the flume to their yards. Let it carry something back. Sit a while first, child. The reading will take days, and the ring would like you under the trees for the start of it.

s_heart_21.name: Wolves of the Fire Line

objective.label: Cull 5 cinder wolves on the Burned Land's fire line

s_heart_21.desc: Cinder wolves hunt the courts' pickets inside the Burned Land's fire line and den on the land round Emmer's Farm. Grudge-Keeper Morrow wants five culled, so the last camp sleeps and the man who waited there gets his quiet.
offer: The Burned Land is the ash round the capital, out to the fire line, where the burn stopped, and there are wolves in it that eat the ash and come out warm in any weather. Cinder wolves. They hunt the courts' pickets at night, and the courts lose a man a week to them, and nobody has had the time to deal with it because everyone is looking at the walls.

Inside the fire line there's a farmhouse. A man called Emmer lived in it; he missed the Night, he was outside the gate when the empire left, and he stayed on that ash sixty-one years, knocking at the walls and keeping his orchard. He's buried in front of his own door. The cinder wolves den on his land.

I want them off it. Cull five, inside the fire line, about Emmer's Farm, in the south-east of the Burned Land, east of the Old Road Cut. Five, and the last camp sleeps a night, and so does he. The grudge hall has a long floor, but Emmer's not on it; he waited at that door for all of us without knowing it, and we owe him that much. A cap for the ash when it's done.
progress: Five cinder wolves, inside the fire line of the Burned Land, about Emmer's Farm, in the south-east of the Burned Land, east of the Old Road Cut. Then report to Morrow at the Grudge Hall.
complete: Five. Emmer's farm is quiet, and the pickets slept. The hall will put that on the floor as a debt paid, which we don't do often; the floor is mostly debts owed. His name goes in beside it, the one name on that floor that isn't a grudge, and I find I don't mind the irregularity.
A cap, for the ash; it'll keep the cinders out of your eyes on the road to the gates. Wipe your feet.

s_heart_22.name: The Chorus at the Beacon

objective.label: Silence 3 cinder choristers in the Beacon Fort

s_heart_22.desc: The Beacon Fort on the Burned Land's melt ridge has a choir: cinder choristers that burned singing and have sung on for three hundred years. Chanter Ives wants three of them silenced, and the song they were singing brought back to the Song-Steps.
offer: The Beacon Fort, on the melt ridge in the Burned Land, has a choir. Three hundred years of one song, sung by things that burned singing it and didn't stop. The courts' scouts came back with the tune in their heads and couldn't say what it was, because none of them can hold a note, and it's been three nights and I can't sleep for wanting to know which song.

So I want it from someone who can hold a note, and you've stood on these steps long enough to be able to. Go to the fort, up the Beacon Stair, and find the cinder choristers in the Wardens' Cells off the stair. Three of them.

Listen first. Listen to what they're singing before you silence them; get the whole line in your chest, and then silence all three. Then come back to the Song-Steps and sing it to me. Don't dent it on the way home. There are boots for you, for the ash, and ether; it'll be a long song.
