progress: Three cinder choristers in the Beacon Fort, in the Wardens' Cells off the Beacon Stair. Listen to the song before you silence them, then sing it to Chanter Ives on the Song-Steps.
complete: Sing it. Again. Oh. Oh, that's the beacon hymn. Ours, Heartwood's. The chanters have kept half of it in their chests these three hundred years, and the fort has been singing the other half. They took it from us and taught it to the fort, and the fort kept singing it after they'd gone, in the fire they left burning.

A song lives in too many chests to steal, I've always said that. I never thought to add: even theirs. Boots, for the ash, and the ether. Sit down before you fall down; you held that note the whole way home and I heard every step of it.

s_moon_1.name: Something for the Damp

objective.label: Call at the Harbour and the Observatory for Sundries-Keeper Ada

s_moon_1.desc: Sundries-Keeper Ada's deliveries are late: her ink is waiting at the Harbour and the Provost's permit stamps at the Observatory. Call at both so the porters send the goods on, and learn the island of Moonmere from the bottom to the top.
offer: Sundries-Keeper Ada, the Causeway Road, Moonmere. Ink, ether, potions, and something for the damp; everything on this island is something for the damp, including the deliveries, which are late. You are new, which means you have legs and no idea where anything is. I can fix the second.

Two deliveries are sitting where they were landed. My ink is down at the Harbour, at the bottom of the island, where the boats put in below the causeway. The Provost's permit stamps, which her office buys from me and I have never asked why, are up at the Observatory, the tower at the very top.

Go to the Harbour and show your face to the porters there, then climb to the Observatory and do the same. Tell them Ada sent you; they will send the boy after you with the goods, which is how deliveries work here. Nobody carries anything the first time they are asked.
By the time you are back you will know the island, which is mostly stairs and a causeway, and I will give you two potions for the climb.
progress: The Harbour first, down at the bottom of Moonmere below the causeway; then the Observatory, the tower at the top. Show your face at both and say Ada sent you.
complete: Ink and stamps, both on their way; the boy came through ten minutes after you and complained the whole time. There: you have been to the bottom of Moonmere and to the top. Everything else is in between and wet. Two potions. You will want them; the damp gets into everything.

s_moon_2.name: Sunroot

objective.label: Bring Alchemist Imre 3 sunroot from the Moonmere Shores

s_moon_2.desc: Alchemist Imre wants three sunroot, the pale tuber every potion is brewed from. It grows in the wet herb beds on the Moonmere Shores, by the Reed Flats; gather three and bring them to the Alchemists' Guild.
offer: Alchemist Imre, of the Alchemists' Guild, and of the cooking the academy insists is a different discipline. If you are going to walk the shores for other people, you may as well learn to walk them for yourself. Start with sunroot.

Sunroot is a pale tuber that holds a day of light; dig it up and it is faintly warm in the hand. It is the base of every potion on that shelf behind me. It grows on the Moonmere Shores, across the causeway, in the wet: look for the herb beds by the Reed Flats and dig where the leaves are yellow.

Gather three sunroot and bring them to me. I will show you how the guild bottles a day of sunlight into a potion, and the first two bottles from your roots are yours. After that you can brew your own: bring the guild its makings and press K to see what you can make.
progress: I still need three sunroot. Gather them from the herb beds on the Moonmere Shores, across the causeway by the Reed Flats; the leaves are yellow and the root is pale.
complete: Pale and full; you dug them whole, which most students do not. That is three days of light, bottled: two potions for you, one for the bench. Come back to me here at the Alchemists' Guild when you can stand the smell of the next lesson, and I will tell you what sprite dust is for.

s_moon_3.name: Dust That Thinks Better of It

objective.label: Bring Alchemist Imre 4 sprite dust from the wisps on the shores

s_moon_3.desc: Alchemist Imre's next lesson is ether: two pinches of sprite dust make one. Bring Imre four sprite dust from the mist sprites and bog wisps on the Moonmere Shores, and keep it dry.
offer: Good, you came back. The next lesson is ether, which is what a mage drinks when the spell is bigger than the mage. Ether is made from sprite dust: it glitters faintly when you shake it, and then thinks better of it and goes dull. Two pinches make an ether. The academy calls that chemistry; I call it persuasion.

The dust comes off the mist sprites and the bog wisps on the Moonmere Shores: the small lights you see drifting over the flats and the reed beds at dusk. Put one out and, as often as not, it leaves a pinch of dust where it was. Collect it before the wet gets to it.

Bring me four sprite dust, dry. I mean that; everything on this island wants to be wet, and wet dust is mud with ambitions. Four pinches is two ethers, and both of them are yours, along with the recipe.
progress: I still need four sprite dust, dry. Mist sprites and bog wisps drop it; they drift over the flats and the reed beds of the Moonmere Shores at dusk. Keep it out of the water.
complete: Dry. Good; you listened. Two ethers, made from your dust, and the recipe is on the bench now: bring the guild sprite dust whenever you have it and press K to brew your own. That is the whole of the alchemist's trade, by the way: things that want to be one thing, persuaded to be another.

s_moon_4.name: A Room Over the Water

objective.label: Carry Innkeeper Rue's oil chit to Lamp-Keeper Orla at the Point

s_moon_4.desc: Innkeeper Rue's guests watch the Point's lamp from their windows, and Lamp-Keeper Orla lets it gutter when the academy is late with her oil. Carry Rue's chit for a month of oil to Orla at the Point, on the west arm of the Moonmere Shores.
offer: Innkeeper Rue; the Shelf Inn, a room over the water and the sound of the causeway all night. From every window in this house you can see exactly one thing after dark: the lamp on the Point, out on the shore's west arm. My guests sit up and watch it. It is the whole of the view.

Lamp-Keeper Orla keeps that lamp. Her family kept it before the academy took it over, and the academy is supposed to send her oil, and the academy is late with the oil as often as not, and when it is late Orla lets the lamp gutter to make the point. Then my guests ask me why the view has gone out.

Take her this chit. It is good at Ada's, on the Causeway Road, for a month of lamp oil, and it is paid by me, not the academy; tell her that. Orla is at the Point: cross the causeway to the Moonmere Shores and follow the shore west along its arm to the lamp.
Walk the causeway; scholars ride the crystal and miss the whole of it. There is a potion in it for you, and a lit window for my guests.
progress: Rue's oil chit is for Lamp-Keeper Orla at the Point. Cross the causeway to the Moonmere Shores and follow the shore west, out along the west arm, to the lamp.
complete: From Rue? A month of oil, paid by the innkeeper. The academy took my family's lamp and the innkeeper pays to keep it lit; that is Moonmere for you, in one chit. Tell her the lamp will be lit tonight and every night; it always was, whatever I let her think from her windows. And thank you for walking it out here.

s_moon_5.name: Shell for the Ferrules

objective.label: Bring Outfitter Quill 3 fen shells for the staves' ferrules

s_moon_5.desc: Outfitter Quill shoes the feet of the academy's staves in shell, and needs three fen shells from the reed crabs in the reed harvest's beds on the Moonmere Shores.
offer: Outfitter Quill, the Causeway Road. Staves, cudgels, and robes cut for people who read while they walk. Every stave I sell has its foot shod in a ferrule of shell, because a bare wooden foot wears through on the causeway's stone in a single term, and a scholar with a short stave leans.

The right shell is fen shell, and the reed crabs on the Moonmere Shores carry it: the big flat plate on their backs. They are in the reed beds by the harvest, across the causeway; wade into the beds and they will find you before you find them.

Bring me three fen shells and I cut three ferrules. For your trouble there is a robe off the fieldhand rack, cut for walking and reading at once. The academy's colours are optional; the academy's prices, for once, are not being charged.
progress: I still need three fen shells for the ferrules. Reed crabs carry them: in the reed beds by the harvest on the Moonmere Shores, across the causeway.
complete: Tough as boiled leather, all three. That is three ferrules, and three scholars who will arrive at the Observatory the same height they left the harbour. The robe is yours; wear it with the academy's colours or without, I fold either. The ferrules go on this afternoon, and the first stave out of the door goes to a first-year who has been leaning since spring.

s_moon_6.name: Foxes at the College Gate

objective.label: Drive 5 marsh foxes from the mending college's drying racks

s_moon_6.desc: Warden Liss of the Mending College dries its bandages on racks on the Moonmere Shores, and the marsh foxes steal them for bedding. Drive off five marsh foxes about the reed harvest so the racks stay full.
offer: Warden Liss. I keep the Mending College, the academy's college of healing, and its infirmary. The college dries its bandages on the shore racks across the causeway, because linen dries in sea wind and never in this building, and the marsh foxes take the linen for bedding. I have patients wrapped in reed.

Marsh foxes, about the reed harvest on the Moonmere Shores. Five of them driven off or killed, I do not mind which, and the racks stay full long enough to dry a batch. Keep one pelt for yourself; it sheds fen-water, which is more than my bandages do.
The college pays in what it has. Potions from our own shelf: the ones the academy does not know we buy.
progress: Five marsh foxes, about the reed harvest on the Moonmere Shores, across the causeway. They den near the drying racks; follow the trail of stolen linen.
complete: Five. The racks are full again, the ward has linen instead of reed, and one patient has stopped itching. Potions from the college's own shelf, the ones the academy does not know we buy, and the pelt I promised. That is how the college says thank you.

s_moon_7.name: A Shore Is a Clock

objective.label: Stand at the Reed Flats, the Shore Wood and the North Gate on the Moonmere Shores

s_moon_7.desc: Provost Selk sets you a student's exercise: stand at the Reed Flats, the Shore Wood and the North Gate on the Moonmere Shores, and notice what has changed there in three hundred years. Then tell her the time.
offer: Provost Selk. I am head of the academy and of Moonmere's court, and I keep the Observatory. I hear excellent things about you, which always worries me; excellence is so rarely convenient. I have an exercise I set my students, and you may as well have it.

I tell them a shore is a clock if you read it slowly enough: it tells the time by what changes on it, and the academy has surveyed this one for three hundred years, so we know exactly what it ought to look like. The students would rather read a book. So would I. That is not the assignment.

Cross the causeway to the Moonmere Shores and stand at three places: the Reed Flats, west of the road; the Shore Wood, east across the road from them; and the North Gate, the Border Gate at the road's end, where Watch-Sergeant Haldis stands. At each, look at what has changed since the empire left. The answer is nothing, almost everywhere, which is the point.
Then come back up to the Observatory and tell me the time. There are two ethers in it, and my attention, which is worth more and costs more.
progress: Stand at the Reed Flats, the Shore Wood and the North Gate on the Moonmere Shores, and look for what has changed there in three hundred years. Then tell the Provost the time.
complete: The time is this: the North Gate has unlocked itself. One morning this spring its locks let go on their own; the court's watch pushed the leaves to and holds them shut, but for three hundred years that gate did not need holding. Everything else on that shore stands exactly where the academy's surveys have always had it. That is what has changed, and you read it. I hear excellent things, and now I have seen one. Take the ethers.

s_moon_8.name: Fire for the Mist

objective.label: Burn 5 mist sprites off the Moonmere Shores

s_moon_8.desc: Master Corvo of the Burned Shelf, the academy's college of fire, wants five mist sprites burned off the Moonmere Shores past the reed harvest, where they drift in off the water at dusk.
offer: Master Corvo, of the Burned Shelf. My college takes its name from a fire: the week after the empire vanished the academy burned its own astronomy section, indoors, and now teaches fire magic in the room where it happened. The Provost calls that economy. I call it a confession with seating. You will hear me say so again.

The mist sprites on the Moonmere Shores are what a college looks like from outside when it is not being careful: a glow, a drift, no sense of direction, and they startle the reed-cutters' children. They come in off the water past the reed harvest at dusk.

Burn five of them off the shore for me. Fire, preferably; it is what we are for, and it is the one thing mist cannot argue with. There is a willow staff in it for you, which, given what we burned and what we teach, is a confession with a handle.
progress: Five mist sprites, on the Moonmere Shores past the reed harvest; they drift in off the water at dusk. Burn them if you can.
complete: Five. Ruin is legible if you went to school long enough, and you are at school now, whether you enrolled or not. The staff: willow. It burns well, which I will pretend I did not say, and which you will remember when it matters. The sprites will be back by spring; so, I expect, will you.

s_moon_9.name: Scale for the Bindings

objective.label: Bring Archivist Junn 3 drake scales for the returns desk's bindings

s_moon_9.desc: Archivist Junn's oldest ledgers are bound in drake scale, and the Returns Desk has three to rebind. Bring Junn three drake scales from the fen hatchlings and mireback drakelings on the Moonmere Shores.
offer: Oh good, hands. Archivist Junn, the Returns Desk; I take back what the academy lends out, and I am drowning in it. Three of my oldest ledgers came back this month with their boards hanging off, and I cannot shelve a book that is trying to leave.

The old bindings are drake scale. They last three centuries, which is the one thing in this building that does; the ledgers I mean were bound three hundred years ago this year and are only now letting go. I will not rebind them in anything less.

Drake scale comes off the fen hatchlings and the mireback drakelings on the Moonmere Shores, across the causeway: the hatchlings bask on the eastern flats, and the drakelings keep further north, toward the North Gate. Bring me three scales and the desk rebinds three ledgers for another three hundred years. You get a hood, because you will be back here with more returns, and the stairs are wet.
progress: I still need three drake scales. Fen hatchlings carry them on the eastern flats of the Moonmere Shores, and mireback drakelings further north, toward the North Gate.
complete: Three scales, three ledgers, three hundred years each; I like a sum that comes out. They will be rebound by the week's end and back on the shelf, trying to leave nowhere. The hood is yours. Show nobody, especially not the Provost; she will want it catalogued, and then it is hers and you are the borrower.

s_moon_10.name: Light That Will Not Fill

objective.label: Bring Alchemist Imre 2 wisp essence from the marsh lights

s_moon_10.desc: Alchemist Imre has finally made a lantern that holds wisp essence, the light that pours like water. Bring Imre two wisp essence from the marsh lights that walk the Moonmere Shores after dark, and the lantern is yours.
offer: You have come far enough for the thing the guild does not teach. Wisp essence: light that pours like water and will not fill anything. Tip it into a cup and the cup stays empty and glows. Alchemists have been trying to bottle it since the academy was a shed on a rock, and we have mostly failed.

It comes from the marsh lights on the Moonmere Shores, the ones that walk: not the drifting sprites you have met, but the taller lights that keep pace with you along the road and the flats at night. Put one out and, now and then, the essence pools where it stood. Scoop it quickly.

Bring me two wisp essence and I will show you what we have managed at last: a lantern that holds it. It is yours. It is a ring, technically, worn on the hand, and it is called the Causeway Lantern. Don't tell the academy; they would want to catalogue the one thing we got right.
progress: I still need two wisp essence. The marsh lights carry it: the tall walking lights that pace you along the road and the flats of the Moonmere Shores after dark.
complete: Two. Poured, and it holds; look at that, three hundred years of failed bottles and it sits in a ring. The Causeway Lantern. Every scholar walks the causeway once and rides the crystal ever after; wear this, walk it once more at night, and you will see the water properly.

s_moon_11.name: Gull Feather Quilting

objective.label: Bring Outfitter Quill 5 feathers from the shore gulls for the argent quilting

s_moon_11.desc: Outfitter Quill quilts the academy's argent robes with gull down. Bring Quill five feathers from the shore gulls at the Coach Halt on the Shore Road, and take a pair of shoes from the argent rack.
offer: The argent robes, the silver-grey ones the senior scholars wear, are quilted in gull. Warm, dry, light, and it is the only part of a gull anyone has ever wanted. I have a term's worth of robes to quilt and no down.

The shore gulls are on the Shore Road, the warm road east toward Heartwood: they mob the Coach Halt, where the coach stops, because Stall-Keeper Ren feeds them, meaning to or not. Bring me five of their feathers; only the breast feathers are any use, so not every gull will give you one. The stores book them as hen feathers, do not ask me why; a gull's are what I want.
When you are back there is a pair of shoes for you from the argent rack. The road is warmer every mile you walk it and your feet will still be wet; that is this coast.
progress: I still need five feathers from the shore gulls. They are on the Shore Road, mobbing the Coach Halt where the coach stops. Not every gull gives a feather worth quilting.
complete: Five. Quilting for a term, and the senior scholars will never know whose hands plucked it, which is how they prefer everything. Argent shoes, as promised: the academy's prices are not optional, but this pair is on me. They dry overnight on the sill. Nothing else on this island does.

s_moon_12.name: Drakes on the Strand

objective.label: Clear 5 strand drakes from the Shore Road's palm strand

s_moon_12.desc: Every student who walks the Shore Road to Moonmere arrives at Warden Liss's infirmary with drake-bite. Clear five strand drakes from the Palm Strand, past the Coach Halt on the Shore Road, before the next term walks in.
offer: Every student who walks the Shore Road to this island arrives at my infirmary with drake-bite. Every one. I have treated the same bite on the same calf so many times I could set the stitches blind. I have started to think the drakes are on the academy's payroll, to make the first lesson humility.

Strand drakes. They lie on the Palm Strand, the beach past the Coach Halt on the Shore Road, where the palms come down to the sand, and they take anyone who walks the tideline instead of the road. Students always walk the tideline.
Clear five of them off the strand and the next term arrives whole. The college pays in what it has: hi-potions, and a remedy for whatever the road does to you on the way.
progress: Five strand drakes, on the Palm Strand of the Shore Road, past the Coach Halt where the palms meet the sand. They lie on the tideline.
complete: Five. The next term will arrive bored instead of bitten, and complain about the walk, and I will enjoy that more than I should. Hi-potions, and a remedy for whatever the road did to you on the way; I can see the salt on your boots from here, and I know what lives in it.

s_moon_13.name: The Lilies Burn Badly

objective.label: Burn 5 lily slimes off the Lily Meres at the Summer Lakes

s_moon_13.desc: Student Pell is counting lilies on the Lily Meres at the Summer Lakes, through the North Gate, and the lily slimes have begun counting him. Master Corvo wants five of them burned so his student keeps all his fingers.
offer: Now that the North Gate stands open, the academy has sent students through it, because of course it has. Student Pell is at the Summer Lakes, the empire's old villa lakes just beyond the gate, counting lilies on the Lily Meres for the Provost: when they open, how many, which morning. Useful, I am told.

The lily slimes are counting Pell. They sit under the pads and come up when something leans over the water, and a student counting lilies leans over the water all day. He has lost a glove and nearly a hand. I want my student back with all of his fingers.

Go through the North Gate to the Summer Lakes and burn five lily slimes off the Lily Meres. They burn badly; the water is in them, and fire has to argue with it. Learn something from that about what fire can and cannot do. The rod is yours for the learning.
progress: Five lily slimes, on the Lily Meres at the Summer Lakes, through the North Gate from the Moonmere Shores. They rise when you lean over the water. Fire works, slowly.
complete: Five, and Pell has ten fingers; I made him hold them up, and I counted. The Moonmere rod. It knows what to do with wet things, which is more than the academy does, and now so do you. Pell sends his thanks, and a lily count I did not ask for.

s_moon_14.name: Filled In to the Last

objective.label: Bring Provost Selk 3 dance cards from the Sunken Ballroom

s_moon_14.desc: Provost Selk wants three dance cards from the guests of the Sunken Ballroom under the Summer Lakes, the ball the empire's household was dancing on the night it left. She wants the names on them, and what the last dance was.
offer: The ballroom under the west mere at the Summer Lakes, the Sunken Ballroom, kept dance cards: a small card for each guest, with the evening's dances listed and a partner's name written against each. Every card was filled in to the last dance, and the last night was the night the empire left.

I have told you an archive is for deciding when a thing is safe to know. That ballroom decided for itself: it wrote the whole evening down in advance and then left in the middle of it. I would like to read what it wrote.

The guests are still on the floor, after a fashion: what is left of household people, the empire's own, who did not go with the household when it went, and they still hold their cards. Go down the Ballroom Stair on the west mere's shore, and bring me three dance cards from the ballroom guests. Take company; they do not give the cards up kindly.
I want the names on them, and I want to know what the last dance was. Sandals from the merewoven rack for your trouble; the floor down there is wet, and you will be back on it.
progress: Three dance cards, from the ballroom guests in the Sunken Ballroom: down the Ballroom Stair on the west mere's shore at the Summer Lakes. Bring them to the Provost at the Observatory.
complete: Three cards, three hands, the same ink. The last dance was a waltz, and the names against it are all household names: the empire's own people, each written in by their own hand, in advance. After the waltz, on every card, the same line: final dance, reserved, upon our Return. They knew the hour was coming, and they did not stop the music for it. They danced through it. Take the sandals. You will be back down there.

s_moon_15.name: The Stewards

objective.label: Lay 4 house stewards to rest in the Sunken Ballroom

s_moon_15.desc: The house stewards of the Sunken Ballroom under the Summer Lakes are still serving a supper nobody ate three hundred years ago. Archivist Junn wants four of them laid to rest, so the evening can finally be closed.
offer: The Sunken Ballroom, under the west mere at the Summer Lakes: the scouts' reports are on my desk, and the house stewards are still serving. Trays up, napkins over the arm, three hundred years of a supper nobody ate, carried round a floor nobody is dancing on. I catalogued the menu from the reports. I am not proud of it.

They are not alive, and they are not dead by anyone's rolls; they are what is left of the household's servants who did not go with the household when it went, and they are still at their posts. Nobody has told them the evening is over, because nobody could.

Lay four house stewards to rest for me. Down the Ballroom Stair on the west mere's shore, in the salons and on the floor; they come at anyone who is not holding a card. When the trays are down, someone has to tell the Master of Ceremonies at the door that the evening is over, and that should be someone with a party behind them. That is the next errand, and I will give it to you when you are back.
progress: Four house stewards, laid to rest in the Sunken Ballroom: down the Ballroom Stair on the west mere's shore at the Summer Lakes, in the salons and on the floor.
complete: Four. The trays are down, and the floor is quieter than it has been in three centuries. The Master of Ceremonies is still at the door, announcing guests who left three hundred years ago, to a room with nobody in it. Row nine hundred, annex, for all of it; that is where I file what belongs somewhere and has nowhere to go. Come back to me here at the Returns Desk when you have a party behind you; the Master is next.

s_moon_16.name: The Last Waltz

objective.label: End the ball: fell the Master of Ceremonies in the Sunken Ballroom

s_moon_16.desc: The Master of Ceremonies still stands at the Sunken Ballroom's door announcing a guest who is not coming. Archivist Junn asks you to take a party down and fell it, so the ball under the Summer Lakes can be filed as closed.
offer: The Master of Ceremonies. It stands at the ballroom door and has been announcing the same guest since the night the lamps went out, in the same voice, with the same pause for applause. The guest is not coming. It has not been told, and it would not listen.

It is the last thing holding that evening open. Take a party down the Ballroom Stair on the west mere's shore at the Summer Lakes, through the salons to the ballroom floor, and fell it; a ball is not a thing you end alone, and the Master will not go quietly for one person.

When it is down, stand on the floor a moment and listen to the music box on the bandstand; tell me what it plays when there is nobody left to announce. Then I can file the evening as closed, three hundred years late, and I would very much like to. There is a robe in it, the college's merewoven, and the court will give you a title for closing the ball.
progress: The Master of Ceremonies, on the floor of the Sunken Ballroom at the Summer Lakes: down the Ballroom Stair on the west mere's shore, through the salons to the floor. Take a party.
complete: One bar of a waltz, repeating. Still. Well: the floor is empty, the door is unannounced, and the ball is over. Closed. Filed. Three hundred years of an evening, and it is in the annex now, where things go that happened and are finished. The robe is the college's; the ballroom, I suppose, is yours. Closer of the Ball; the court likes a title that says what you did.

s_moon_17.name: Concentrated

objective.label: Bring Sundries-Keeper Ada 3 mere tears

s_moon_17.desc: Sundries-Keeper Ada wants three mere tears, the cold heavy beads the mere wraiths at the Summer Lakes and the rain wisps at the Reservoir shed, to make something for the damp that finally works.
offer: You remember something for the damp: the stuff I sell by the pot that keeps the wet out of boots and books for about a week. I want to make one that works for a winter, and for that I need the damp itself, concentrated.

The mere wraiths at the Summer Lakes and the rain wisps at the Reservoir each shed a bead when they go: a mere tear, we call it. Cold, clear, and heavier than water has any right to be; a bead of the old Mere, people say: our inner harbour, the water that keeps everything. Nobody knows why it is heavy. I do not need to know. I need three.

Bring me three mere tears in a closed hand; they roll, and they find the lowest point in any room. The Lakes are through the North Gate from the Shores; the Reservoir is the drowned valley the courts have their joint camp on, further in. Either will do. When I have made the stuff, you get the hood off the valley rack for the trouble.
progress: I still need three mere tears. Mere wraiths at the Summer Lakes and rain wisps at the Reservoir shed them. Carry them in a closed hand; they roll.
complete: Heavier than water, all three, and colder than the hand that carried them. That is a winter of something for the damp, the kind that works, and the first pot is yours when it has set. The hood: it is valleyweave, woven in the drowned valley, and it has been wetter than you will ever be.

s_moon_18.name: Nobody Asks What For

objective.label: Bring Alchemist Imre 3 leech glands from the Canal Works

s_moon_18.desc: Alchemist Imre needs three leech glands for the guild's antidotes. Fen leeches carry them, in the still water of the Canal Works, the drowned canal country past the Summer Lakes.
offer: Leech gland. The alchemists want it and nobody asks what for, because the answer is ugly. I will tell you anyway: antidotes. Every remedy on the cure ladder, from a bee sting to a drake's bite, stands on a fen leech, because what a leech puts in to keep your blood running is the one thing that undoes what a venom puts in to stop it.

The fen leeches are in the Canal Works, the empire's drowned canal country past the Summer Lakes, where the sentinels are dredging the locks. The leeches live in the still water between the sunken barges and come to anything warm. Three glands, taken whole; not every leech has one worth taking.

Bring them and the guild's remedies are yours to make. Sandals for the fen, glasswoven: the fen hates glass and glass does not care, so your feet stay dry where nothing else does. And a remedy, since you will be standing in leech water to earn it.
progress: I still need three leech glands. Fen leeches carry them, in the still water of the Canal Works between the sunken barges, past the Summer Lakes. Take them whole.
complete: Three, whole; you did not squeeze them, which is the whole trick. Antidote for a term, and the recipe is on the bench; press K when you want more. Take the remedy for whatever the fen left in you, and the sandals for the walk back. Nobody asked what for, and now you know.

s_moon_19.name: Stoke Nothing

objective.label: Put down 5 furnace stokers in the Furnace Hall

s_moon_19.desc: Under the Glassworks' furnaces, the Furnace Hall's stokers have fed the fires for three hundred years and burned in the feeding. Master Corvo wants five of them put down: the fire is his college's to teach, not theirs to keep.
offer: The Glassworks, the empire's glass desert, has a hall under its furnaces: the Furnace Hall. Its stokers have stoked for three hundred years without an order to stop, and they burned in the stoking; what walks that row now is what fire leaves of a servant who would not leave the fire. My college's founder would have called that devotion. I call it a lesson.

Put down five furnace stokers for me. Go down into the Furnace Hall by the Kiln Mouth on the Glassworks' Furnace Row; they are on the stoking floor, feeding the fires, and they will turn on anyone who comes between them and the coal. Take company; they are hot.

The fire is mine to teach, not theirs to keep. There is a reedwoven hood in it for you, and a hi-ether. Then somebody should speak to the Abbot down there about arithmetic, and I suspect that will be you too.
progress: Five furnace stokers, on the stoking floor of the Furnace Hall under the Glassworks. They defend the fires; take company.
complete: Five. The row is cooler by five hands, and I felt it from here, or chose to. Something is still down there: the Cinder Abbot, in a side chamber off the hall, computing. I know what happens to colleges that compute something and then set the working to the fire. Come back to me here at the Burned Shelf when you are rested; the Abbot is the next errand.

s_moon_20.name: The Abbot's Arithmetic

objective.label: Fell the Cinder Abbot in the Furnace Hall's side chamber

s_moon_20.desc: In a side chamber of the Furnace Hall under the Glassworks, the Cinder Abbot is still working a sum it set to the fire three hundred years ago. Master Corvo asks you to take a party down and fell it, and bring him its ember.
offer: The Cinder Abbot. Listen to what it is: a college of fire that burned its own arithmetic, in a room it built for the purpose, and has been working the same sum in the ashes ever since. I am describing my college. I am also describing the Abbot. You see why I want it to be me who sends you.

It sits in the side chamber off the Furnace Hall under the Glassworks, past the stoking floor you cleared. Take a party; it has had three hundred years to get the sum right and it defends the working. Fell it.

What a thing like that leaves behind is one ember. Bring that up to me. I will keep it on the burned shelf, in the room where our fire happened, where it can see what it did. The court will call you Reader of the Ember for it, and I have a crown for you: amber, poured from the same furnace.
progress: The Cinder Abbot, in the side chamber off the Furnace Hall under the Glassworks, past the stoking floor. Take a party, and bring Master Corvo its ember.
complete: The ember. It is still computing; I can hear it, a small tick, carrying the one. On the shelf it goes, next to ours: two fires that finished their sums. The crown is amber from the same furnace it burned in. Wear it in the room where the fire happened; nobody else will, and somebody should.

s_moon_21.name: Every Climb, Every Hour

objective.label: Bring Provost Selk 3 pages of the Border Wall's watch ledger

s_moon_21.desc: The Border Wall's sentinels have kept a ledger of every climb for three hundred years, and the academy's own record of the border has a gap. Provost Selk wants three pages of the watch ledger from the rampart and watch sentinels on the Border Wall and in the Great Watchtower, to compare.
offer: The Border Wall keeps a ledger. Every climb onto its ramparts, every hour of every watch, for three hundred years, written by the sentinels who patrol it and never once left blank. The academy keeps a ledger of the border too, from this tower, and ours has a gap: years in it where the academy wrote nothing down at all. Theirs does not. I would like to compare.

The rampart sentinels on the Border Wall and the watch sentinels inside the Great Watchtower carry the pages on them; a sentinel's ledger is part of the sentinel. Bring me three pages of the watch ledger. The stairs up from the Reservoir or from the Glassworks take you onto the wall; the Great Watchtower's door is on the wall-top by the Embassy's Camp.

I will read them here and decide when they are safe to shelve. Deciding when is what this office is for, and for once it is a decision I expect to enjoy. The hood is deepsilk; it was cut for a Provost.
progress: Three pages of the watch ledger, for the Provost. Rampart sentinels carry them on the Border Wall; watch sentinels carry them inside the Great Watchtower, whose door is by the Embassy's Camp.
complete: Every climb, every hour. Three hundred years of the wall's own patrols, and then, this year, the three envoys who sat at Wren's table, Sabel, Junn and Morrow, climbing to the Great Watchtower with the courts' letters, entered by date. So they did reach the wall; the wall says so, and the wall has not missed an hour in three centuries. Filed, beside ours, gap and all. The hood: deepsilk, cut for a Provost, and I have decided when.

s_moon_22.name: Lamps That Should Have Gone Out

objective.label: Put out 4 oil wisps in the Beacon Fort

s_moon_22.desc: The Beacon Fort on the Melt Ridge of the Burned Land is full of oil wisps that have burned since the beacon was lit on the Night, and the courts' wounded come to Warden Liss with burns three centuries old. Put out four of them; she wants the fort dark.
offer: The Beacon Fort, on the Melt Ridge in the Burned Land, is where the empire's beacon was lit on the night it left. The oil that fed the beacon never stopped burning. It walks the fort now as oil wisps: flames with nothing left under them, going from room to room as if there were still lamps to fill. Things that end violently are loud. These are very quiet.

The courts' explorers come back to my infirmary from that fort with burns that are three hundred years old, if you follow me: the fire that made them was lit on the Night and has not gone out since. I can mend the skin. I cannot mend the fact.

Go up to the Beacon Fort and put out four oil wisps. Water does nothing; smother them or beat them down. The burns stop coming when the fort is dark, and I want the fort dark. Sandals from the embersilk rack, which the ash cannot hurt, and an X-potion for the walk.
progress: Four oil wisps, in the Beacon Fort on the Melt Ridge in the Burned Land. Smother them or beat them down; water does nothing.
complete: Four, out. The fort is darker by four lamps that should have gone out three hundred years ago, and the burns will stop coming, or come less. Sandals for the ash, and the potion; the college mends what the road did. That is how I say thank you. It will have to do.

s_moon_23.name: The Works Ledger

objective.label: Read the Works Ledger in the Great Sluice's master chamber

s_moon_23.desc: In the Sluice Master's Chamber of the Great Sluice, on the Canal Works fen, stands the Works Ledger: every lock's repair order, every one dated this season, 'navigable by the Restoration'. Archivist Junn asks you to read it and bring her the season.
offer: The Great Sluice, the pump house on the Canal Works fen, keeps a ledger of repairs. The survey reports from the Canal Works describe it: a great book on a stand in the Sluice Master's Chamber, and in it every lock from the fen to the capital, each with a repair order against it, each dated to one season, each marked 'navigable by the Restoration', which is the sentinels' word for the day the household comes home.

I am not allowed to move it. The sentinels who work the sluice keep it where the empire left it, and they are firm about it. So I cannot carry it up here and read it at my desk, which is how I would like to read everything.

Go down into the Great Sluice, clear your way to the Sluice Master's Chamber, and read the Works Ledger on its stand. All of it, every order and every date. Then come back and tell me the season they were all dated to. The catalogue says the sluice has no ledger. The catalogue lies, and I want to know by how much.
progress: Read the Works Ledger on its stand in the Sluice Master's Chamber of the Great Sluice, on the Canal Works fen. Every order, every date; then bring Junn the season.
complete: The same season as the Regent's orders in the King's Gardens' nursery. The same as the granary's rations, the same as the furnace's panes. Every lock from the fen to the capital, mended on one schedule, for one date. They were all mending for the same morning. Row nine hundred, annex: I have said that about everything I could not place for years. I found the shelf. It is the whole interior, and it is dated.

s_capr_1.name: The Board Is Full

objective.label: Bring Baker Ilsa 2 flour sacks from the Granary Plains

s_capr_1.desc: Baker Ilsa in the returned Capital has a full board and no flour. Bring her two Flour Sacks from the Granary Plains, where the sack ants carry them off and the mill hounds of the Great Granary guard the rest.
offer: Next! Oh. You're not on the board. Well, you are now. I'm Ilsa, this is the bakery, and the board is the chalk list of every house that gets a loaf off my first tray. It's full. It was full last night when I chalked it, and it's full this morning, and this morning every name on it is awake and hungry.

My trouble is flour. The tray that's just come out is the last of what was in the bins last night. The rest is out in the Granary Plains, in the towers, stencilled for this city; and the sack ants on the plains carry the sacks off whole, and the mill hounds in the Great Granary sit on what's left as if it were theirs.

Two sacks. Take them off the sack ants on the Granary Plains, or off the mill hounds in the Great Granary, I don't mind which. Bring them here and you're on the board for good: first tray, every morning, your name in chalk. And three loaves today, warm.
progress: I still need two Flour Sacks. The Sack Ants carry them on the Granary Plains and the Mill Hounds guard them in the Great Granary; either will do. Bring them to the bakery.
complete: Two sacks, and good flour. 'Phase five,' it says on the stencil, 'rations for the city, from the morning they arrive.' Well. It's phase bread now. Three loaves, still warm, and your name's on the board in chalk, first tray, every morning, for as long as there's a board. Next!

s_capr_2.name: Emmer's Chair

objective.label: Read Emmer's letters at his table in the Burned Land

s_capr_2.desc: An old woman of the West Ward in the returned Capital knew Emmer, the farmer who missed the night the household left and waited at the walls for the rest of his life. She cannot bear to read the letters he left on his table at Emmer's Farm in the Burned Land; read them for her and tell her he would have laughed.
offer: Emmer's chair. Somebody bring Emmer's chair in from the ash. You don't know who that is. I'll tell you, since nobody here can bear to. Emmer farmed outside the walls; he was drunk in his orchard the night we left, and he was left behind. He waited on that farm for this morning for the rest of his life, and he missed it by a season. He'd have wanted to be here for this, the daft old hope that he was.

His table is still standing in the farmhouse, inside the fire line in the Burned Land, with his letters on it. Your courts' people say there are three. I can't read them. I knew him. For me it was one evening. Last night he was alive, and this morning he's a grave with flowers on it, and I can't.

Go and read them, all three, oldest first, somebody who never knew him. Then come back to me here in the West Ward and tell me he'd have laughed. He always laughed. I need to hear it from someone who's read what he wrote.
progress: Emmer's three letters are still on the table at Emmer's Farm, inside the fire line of the Burned Land. Read them, oldest first, and come back to the West Ward and tell me whether he'd have laughed.
complete: Year one, year forty, and the last. 'A good joke after everything, and I hope somebody laughs.' He'd have laughed. He always laughed. 'It wasn't your fault either.' That's him. That's Emmer, that is. Thank you. We'll fetch the chair tomorrow, with the proclamations, and it'll sit here in the ward, and anyone who wants to can sit in it. Go on, now.

s_capr_3.name: Something for the Shock

objective.label: Bring Apothecary Wren-of-the-City 4 first ash from the empty city's keepers

s_capr_3.desc: Apothecary Wren-of-the-City in the returned Capital's market needs four pinches of First Ash, ash from the morning of the burn at the centre, for the tincture for shock the whole square is buying. The First Keepers and Household Echoes of the empty city carry it, as do the Pale Drakes of the King's Gardens and the Garden Keepers of the Propagating Cellars.
offer: Tinctures, powders, and something for the shock. I'm Wren, the apothecary; Wren-of-the-City, apparently, since one of your people told me there's another Wren with an inn. Everyone in this square is buying something for the shock this morning, and I don't blame them: for all of us it was one evening, and this morning the world outside the walls is three hundred years older and full of strangers whose names were in our rolls all along.

The tincture for shock wants first ash. Ash from the morning of the burn, from the centre, where the flash began. It's in my book and I've never had any; the burn hadn't happened the last time I stood here. The empty city has it: the first keepers, the palace's own sentinels, and the household echoes still walk its streets with the first ash on them. So do the pale drakes in the King's Gardens, and the garden keepers in the Propagating Cellars under the glasshouse there.
Four pinches of first ash. Bring them and I can dose the whole square. Two of the strong ones for you, mega potions, on the house, because you'll have earned a dose yourself by then.
progress: I still need four pinches of First Ash. The First Keepers and Household Echoes carry it in the empty Capital, the Pale Drakes in the King's Gardens, and the Garden Keepers in the Propagating Cellars.
complete: From the centre. It falls upward, did you see that? Hold a pinch out and it lifts off your palm and goes up. I'll not put that in the tincture book; nobody would believe it. Four doses of the strong tincture, and the square's calmer already. Two mega potions for you. Everyone's strange today. Take yours before you need it.

s_capr_4.name: Chased With the Crown

objective.label: Bring the Household Armourer 3 palace plates from the sentinels of the Keep

s_capr_4.desc: The Household Armourer in the returned Capital's market square wants three Palace Plates from the Palace Sentinels of the empty city and the Keep, to see how the crown-chased plate forged in the armourer's grandfather's time wore through three hundred years of duty. The first helm off the forge this morning is the reward.
offer: Household steel, made on this square. I'm the household armourer; my forge is the one on the square. The palace sentinels, the household's own guard of the Keep, wear plate chased with the crown, and that plate was forged in my father's father's time. I learned my trade on that pattern, and I know how it wears in fifty years of palace duty. Nobody knows how it wears in three hundred.

It has been worn three hundred years now, on duty, without a rest or a smith. I want to see how it wore. Whether the chasing held, whether the joints went, whether my grandfather's rivets kept. No armourer has ever had the chance, and I'd like to be the one.

Three palace plates. The palace sentinels still stand in the empty city and in the Keep; the plates come off them when they fall. Bring them to me and the first helm off my forge this morning is yours: Firstward, the pattern the Keep's first watch wore. Crown coin or free-city coin for anything else; the proclamation says par.
progress: I still need three Palace Plates. The Palace Sentinels carry them in the empty Capital and in the Keep; bring them to my forge on the market square.
complete: Not a scratch on the chasing. Look: three hundred years of duty, and the crown on the breast still bright, and my grandfather's rivets every one still tight. He'd have said nothing and gone red. Here, as promised: the Firstward helm, the first off my forge this morning, forged for a morning that has now arrived. Wear it in the square where they can see it.

s_capr_5.name: The Hounds Have Not Been Told

objective.label: Put down 6 ward hounds in the empty city and the Keep

s_capr_5.desc: A Household Guard at the gates of the returned Capital wants six Ward Hounds put down in the empty city and the Keep. The gates stand open by order of the crown and the household now includes the free cities by proclamation, but the hounds have not been told.
offer: The gates stand open by order of the crown. Residents and... residents. Proceed. I'm a household guard; I keep this gate, and I kept it last night, the night we left, which you tell me was three hundred years ago. The crown's order this morning says the gates stand open to the household, and by proclamation the household now includes you. All of you. I'm still saying it to get used to it.

The ward hounds have not been told. They're the household's dogs, kennelled in the old wards to keep strangers off the household's streets, and they've kept at it the whole time with nobody to feed them or call them off. They don't read proclamations. They bite.

Six of them, put down, in the wards of the empty city and in the Keep. The household's hounds should learn what the household is now, and that's the only way they listen. Boots for you from the gate stores after. Proceed.
progress: Six Ward Hounds still hold the old wards of the empty Capital and the Keep. Put them down; they have not been told the household includes you. Report to me at the gates.
complete: Six hounds. The old wards are quieter now. The hounds have been told, in the only way they listen; the rest will learn it from the quiet. The boots: Lastlight, from the gate's own rack, the pattern this gate wore on the last night. The first pair issued to a... resident. Proceed.

s_capr_6.name: Read Into the Record

objective.label: Bring the Clerk of the Archive 4 archive minutes from the wisps of the empty city

s_capr_6.desc: A Clerk of the Archive in the returned Capital must read three hundred years of the Regent's minutes into the record by tomorrow, and needs four Archive Minutes back from the Archive Wisps that carry the loose pages through the empty city's Archive and the Keep.
offer: Three hundred years of minutes to be read into the record by tomorrow. The Regent kept them: every order it signed, every acre it had tended, every hour of every watch, written up and filed in the archive of the empty city. I am a clerk of the archive, and the First Minister has said 'by tomorrow' in the voice that means it.

The trouble is the loose pages. Three hundred years is a great deal of paper, and the archive wisps, the lights that drift through the empty city's archive and the halls of the Keep, have gathered up the pages that were never bound and carry them about. Every acre. Every hour. I can't read into the record what I haven't got.

Four archive minutes, back from the wisps. You'll find them in the Archive of the empty city and in the Keep. Bring the pages and the record is that much closer to complete. There's a hood for you from the archive's own press after; it's what we give readers.
progress: I still need four Archive Minutes. The Archive Wisps carry the loose pages through the Archive of the empty Capital and the halls of the Keep. Bring them to me at the Archive.
complete: Four. Every acre, every hour, on these four pages, and now read into the record in my own voice; the Regent's hand, our voice, that's how it's to be done. The minister will want the rest by tomorrow, and there is no rest. The hood: Wildweave, from the archive's own press, for someone who reads. Thank you.

s_capr_7.name: The Proclamations

objective.label: Carry the morning's proclamation to the Lord Marshal, the Speaker of the Ring and the Provost

lord_marshal: 'The gates stand open.' Three hundred years of my family on the wall, and that's how they put it: a clerk's phrase. Well. Tell the minister Caerdun's court will come, and that it brings the wage book, every night of watch since the Sealing, valued and owed. Tell her the book is heavy, and that we have carried it this far.
speaker_of_the_ring: Read it again. Under the ring, where the four elders can hear it; nothing is decided in Heartwood that the trees haven't heard. There. The trees heard. Tell the minister Heartwood will come to her accounting, and that Heartwood will count: every grove, every family, every year of the song. We have had the practice.
provost_selk: 'The accounting begins.' An archive is for deciding when a thing is safe to know. They have decided; it is their archive and their when. Tell the minister Moonmere will come, and that Moonmere has been keeping notes since the morning after, and has every page.

s_capr_7.desc: The First Minister of Vanai's first proclamation says the gates stand open, the accounting begins, and the free cities are asked to send their courts. Carry it by hand to the Lord Marshal in Caerdun, the Speaker of the Ring in Heartwood and Provost Selk in Moonmere, read it to each, and come back to the Palace Steps and tell her their faces.
offer: There will be proclamations. This is the first, and I have written it myself: the gates stand open; the accounting begins; and the free cities, Caerdun, Heartwood and Moonmere, are asked to send their courts to the capital to sit at it. Three sentences. They took me most of the night, and we have only had the one night.

It must be carried by hand, not read down from a wall by a herald sentinel; the free cities have had three hundred years of paper from us and not one face. And it must be carried by someone whose face the three courts know. Yours, I am told, is known in all three. That is rarer than you think.

The Lord Marshal of Caerdun, on his parade square. The Speaker of the Ring in Heartwood, under the Grove Ring. Provost Selk in Moonmere, at her observatory. Read the proclamation to each of them, in full, and hear what each says in answer. Then come back to these steps and tell me their faces. I am owed their faces, and they are owed mine. A title for it, Herald of the Morning, and the palace's thanks.
progress: The proclamation still has to be read to the Lord Marshal in Caerdun, the Speaker of the Ring in Heartwood and Provost Selk in Moonmere. Read it to each, then come back to the Palace Steps.
complete: Three faces. Yes. Long faces, all three, and proud ones. Morrow told me this morning that theirs would be exactly as long as ours, and she was right. Caerdun brings its book, Heartwood its count, Moonmere its notes. Tomorrow the accounting, and it will be the longest in the empire's history, and I find I am glad of it. Today: thank you. Herald of the Morning. It is the first title the returned have given, and it is yours.

s_capr_8.name: Relieved

objective.label: Fell the Unlit King in the Keep's last chamber

s_capr_8.desc: The Regent, off duty since the crown said the word to it, has found one post in the Keep the word never reached: the Unlit King, in the King's Chamber behind the throne. Take a party, fell it, and say the word to it.
offer: Do not mind me. I am off duty; the crown said the word to me on the steps this morning. Relieved. I had never heard it. Afterwards I went to every post in the Keep to see whether the word had reached them all; it was the only use I could think of for myself. There is one it has not reached.

I kept the city. Under the city, behind the throne I stood before for three hundred years, something else kept the dark: the Unlit King. A king's shape in the King's Chamber, in a dark no lamp was ever lit against, that night or since. I did not know until this morning. I should have. I signed every order in this city and never looked behind my own post.

Take a party; I am given to understand one does not go alone, and I have never gone anywhere. The King's Chamber in the Keep, behind the throne in the Great Hall. Fell it, and when it falls, say the word to it. Relieved. It is the only word I have, and it is the right one. A crown for you after; everything here is borrowed now.
progress: The Unlit King still keeps the dark in the King's Chamber of the Keep, behind the throne in the Great Hall. Take a party, fell it, and say the word to it: relieved. Then come back to me.
complete: Relieved. You said it, and it heard; I felt it go from here. The last light of the old king is out, the one dark that outlasted every lamp in this city, and now the morning is the only light there is. Here: the Borrower's Crown. I stood before a borrowed throne, and now you wear a borrowed crown, and everything in this city is borrowed as of an hour ago. Wear it. You were the first I hoped would pass the last door, and you did.

s_capr_9.name: The Lamps That Night

objective.label: Lay 4 silence haunts to rest in the Keep

s_capr_9.desc: A Chaplain of the returned Capital lit every lamp on the night the household left, and cannot pray in the Keep's chapel for the hush that came after. Lay four Silence Haunts to rest in the Chapel of the Keep.
offer: We lit every lamp that night. I remember lighting them, every one in the chapel of the Keep, and I remember the song we sang, and then I remember this morning. I do not remember the three hundred years, and I am told I should be grateful. I am the chaplain here. I would like to be grateful; I find I cannot pray.

The silence haunts are why. They are in the Chapel of the Keep: the hush that came after the lamps, after the song, whatever quiet fell on this city when we went out of it, left behind and still standing in the pews. When I go in to pray, the song goes out of my head and the hush is all there is.

Lay four of them to rest, in the Chapel of the Keep. Take people with you; the Keep is not kind. Then the chapel will be quiet in the right way, and I think I will have the song back. There are sandals for you from the vestry, a small thing, for a large one.
progress: Four Silence Haunts still stand in the Chapel of the Keep. Lay them to rest so the chapel is quiet in the right way, then come back to me at the chapel in the city.
complete: Four. I went in after you. The chapel is quiet in the right way now, the quiet a room has before a song and not the one after, and I had the song back before I reached the rail. Sandals from the vestry, Wildweave; walk softly in them. Everyone is strange today, and I am grateful. There. I said it, and it was true.

s_capx_1.name: The Census Hall

objective.label: Read the census rolls in the empty city's Census Hall

s_capx_1.desc: Duelist-Master Sabel has found the Census Hall in the empty Capital. The census rolls on its desks are the free cities' own: every family of Caerdun, Heartwood and Moonmere, kept current for three hundred years. Read them; she wants someone else to have seen it.
offer: Found the census hall. You should come see the census hall. I mean that: I need you to walk in there and look, so that I'm not the only one who has.

The rolls are open on the desks, and they're current. Not theirs. Ours. Caerdun, Heartwood, Moonmere: every family in the free cities, births, deaths and marriages, three hundred years of them, updated in that same calm hand that wrote 'Seal it behind us', by a city that never once wrote to us.

Read them. Find the page with your own city on it and copy it, so there's a copy of it somewhere outside this hall. I want someone else to have seen it, in case I walk out of here and decide I imagined it. The rolls are through there, on the desks. I'll wait here.
progress: The Census Rolls are still open on their desks in the Census Hall of the empty Capital. Read them, copy the page with your own city on it, and come back to me.
complete: You saw. Then it's real. My grandmother's name is in there, with the year she died, in their hand, written the week it happened. Three hundred years of us, every birthday, every burial outside their locked door, and they wrote every one down. They knew. Every year, they knew. Well. There's nothing in here to draw on. Drinks after.

s_capx_2.name: Kept Well

objective.label: Put 3 first keepers to rest on the Great Stair

s_capx_2.desc: Morrow wants three First Keepers put to rest on the Great Stair of the empty Capital: the household's first watch, still standing guard three hundred years past any relief, which is what kept the free cities out and kept them well.
offer: Kept out and kept well, all along. That's what the census says, and that's what the first keepers on this stair are: the household's first watch, the ones set at the top of the Great Stair the night everyone left, still watching, three hundred years past any relief. They're what kept the door, and the door was never locked. It was only ever watched.

I have spent my whole life sharpening a grudge for a locked door, and I've just learned they were recording my birthdays behind it. I said I'd burn something or weep, and I haven't managed either yet. In the meantime I would like to sharpen the grudge on something that will hold still for it.

Three first keepers, put to rest, on the Great Stair. They stand on the flights between the square and the Keep. Then the stair is ours to climb. Sabatons from a keeper's rack after; Firstward, the pattern they wore. Wear them up it.
progress: Three First Keepers still stand on the flights of the Great Stair in the empty Capital, between the square and the Keep. Put them to rest and come back to me on the stair.
complete: Three. The stair's ours to climb, and the first watch is relieved, which is more than anyone ever did for them. I'm angrier than I was, and more exactly; it helps to know what I'm angry at. Sabatons from a keeper's rack, Firstward pattern. Wear them up the stair. We're going to the top of it.

s_capx_3.name: Every Door in the City

objective.label: Bring Junn 3 household keys from the guards of the empty city

s_capx_3.desc: Junn wants three Household Keys from the Household Guards and Ward Hounds of the empty Capital and the Keep. Every door in the city is locked, every guard carries a ring of keys, and behind one of those doors is three hundred years of the Regent's minutes.
offer: The gates opened for us. No fanfare, no herald; the Regent just unbarred them, the way you let the inspectors in when the audit can't be avoided. And then every door inside is locked. The archive, the census annex, the halls off the square: every one. I am an archivist, and I have walked across an empire to reach these doors, and I want in.

The household guards carry the keys. Every guard that still walks the city has a ring at its belt, and every door in the capital opens to one key or another on those rings. The ward hounds have carried off a few; they carry anything a guard drops. Three keys, and I can open the doors I know about and start on the ones I don't.

Household guards and ward hounds, in the empty city and in the Keep. Three household keys. Bring them to me and I'll start with the archive, because behind one of these doors is three hundred years of minutes in the Regent's hand, and I have spent my whole life reading copies. I would like, once, to read the original. Slops for you after, from the archive.
progress: I still need three Household Keys. The Household Guards carry them on their belts in the empty Capital and the Keep, and the Ward Hounds carry what the guards drop. Bring them to me in the city.
complete: Three. The first opens the archive door; the second, the census annex, the room behind the rolls; and the third opens a door I haven't found yet, which is my favourite kind. Slops from the archive's own press, Wildweave, the archive clerks' pattern; the press will be the first thing I find inside. Now, doors.

s_cf_5.name: Distances From Zero

objective.label: Stand at the North Road Pass, the Ferry Landing and the Border Gate

s_cf_5.desc: Coachman Pell at Milestone Zero wants a newcomer to learn the Caerdun Fields by standing at its three far points: the North Road Pass to the north-east, the Ferry Landing to the west and the Border Gate to the south-east.
offer: Pell. I drive the North Road coach, and this stone I am leaning on is Milestone Zero. Every road in the empire was measured from here. Zero. If you want to know the Caerdun Fields, learn its three distances the way a coachman does: by walking them.

The North Road Pass lies north-east of here, where the road climbs out of the Fields into the snow. The Ferry Landing is west, down by the gulf, where Coll's ferry crosses to Moonmere's shore. The Border Gate is south-east, the locked door into the interior.
Stand at each of the three. Then you will know how far anything in the Fields is from anything else, which is the only thing a coachman knows and the most useful. Potions for the road.
progress: Stand at the North Road Pass, north-east of Milestone Zero; the Ferry Landing, west, by the gulf; and the Border Gate, south-east. All three are in the Caerdun Fields.
complete: Three distances walked. Now you are measured from zero too, like every road on the continent.
Potions for the road, as promised. The coach does not stop for anyone, and you will be walking most places for a while yet.

s_cf_6.name: Pitch for the Hull

objective.label: Bring Ferrymaster Coll 3 slime gel to pitch the ferry's seams

s_cf_6.desc: Ferrymaster Coll's ferry is leaking at the seams. Bring him three slime gel from the meadow slimes south of the watch farms in the Caerdun Fields; warmed, it seals a plank better than pitch.
offer: Coll. I run the gulf ferry from this landing to Moonmere's shore. The gulf does what it likes, and this week what it likes is coming in through my seams.

Slime gel, warmed over a fire, holds a plank better than pitch does, and it is cheaper, since the slimes make it for nothing. Meadow slimes, south of the watch farms, in the low grass. Burst them and take the gel.

Three gel and the crossing stays dry, which the Moonmere scholars will complain about anyway; they complain about a dry crossing the way other people complain about a wet one. Potions for your trouble.
progress: Three slime gel. The meadow slimes are south of the watch farms in the Caerdun Fields, in the low grass. Bring the gel to Coll at the Ferry Landing.
complete: Still warm. Into the seams it goes tonight, and the ferry sails dry tomorrow.

The scholars will have to find something else to write about on the way over. Potions, as promised. If you ever want Moonmere, talk to me while the boat is in at the landing; ten gold takes you across.

s_cf_7.name: Fur From Beyond the Gate

objective.label: Bring Gate-Warden Hesk 3 feral pelts from the wold pups

s_cf_7.desc: Gate-Warden Hesk at the Border Gate wants three feral pelts from the wold pups that came through the gate the morning it unlocked itself, now loose in the pine breaks of the Caerdun Fields, to send to the court as proof of what lies beyond.
offer: Hesk. Gate-warden. My family has watched this door, the Border Gate, for three hundred years, parent to child, and in all that time nothing came through it. Then one morning this spring the gate unlocked itself. Nobody turned a key. The court had us push the leaves shut again, and shut they stay until the court says otherwise.

But in the hour it stood open, things came through. Pups: wolf pups of a breed nobody on this side has ever seen, with fur like nothing on this side of the gate: a colour no animal here grows, whatever light you hold it to. They have made themselves at home in the pine breaks.
Bring me three feral pelts from the wold pups in the pine breaks. I will send them to the court with a note that says 'this is what is beyond'. There are boots in it for you; the breaks are wet.
progress: Three feral pelts from the wold pups. They have settled in the pine breaks of the Caerdun Fields. Bring the pelts to Hesk at the Border Gate.
complete: Look at the colour of it. Nothing on this side grows that. Three hundred years of nothing, and now this, from the far side of my own door.

These go to the court today with a note: 'this is what is beyond.' Let them make of it what they will. The boots are yours: watchfarm boots. My family has watched this door in worse weather than the breaks can give you.

s_hf_5.name: Frogs in the Brook

objective.label: Clear 5 brook frogs from the mill brook

s_hf_5.desc: Brook frogs have filled the mill brook in the Heartwood Fields and sing over the sound of the wheel. Old Tammon wants five cleared out so the mill's verse can be heard again.
offer: Tammon. I sit by this brook most days, beside the mill. The wheel turns whether anybody grinds or not; I come down to make sure it's still true. It is.

But the frogs have filled the brook this spring, right under the wheel, and they are singing over it, loud, and not one of them knows the verse. There's a verse of the counting-song, our old song, that goes with the sound of this wheel, and nobody sings it right who hasn't sat here and heard the wheel plain.

Clear five of the brook frogs out of the water below the mill, here, where the brook runs under the wheel. Then come and sit with me and listen. That's the whole of it. Two potions for your trouble, and the verse, if you've the ear.
progress: Five brook frogs, in the mill brook below the Mill on the Brook in the Heartwood Fields. Then sit with Old Tammon and listen to the wheel.
complete: Hear that? The wheel. Turning, and nothing over it. That's the verse, right there in the sound; the words only sit on top of it. You've sat here now and heard it plain, and you'll sing it right for the rest of your life. Two potions. Sit a while longer if you like; the wheel doesn't mind.

s_hf_6.name: Amber for the Apple Knife

objective.label: Bring Elder Hazel 3 thorn resin to set her apple knife's handle

s_hf_6.desc: Elder Hazel's grandmother's apple knife has a cracked handle, and the verse she folded into coring an apple lives in the grip. Bring Hazel three thorn resin from the young thornfangs around the Wild Orchards to set it.
offer: My grandmother's apple knife. She folded a verse, a kitchen verse of our family's, into the way she cored an apple, and taught it to me with the knife in my hand, and the verse is in the way you hold it; so the handle matters, and the handle's cracked.

Thorn resin will set it. The young thornfangs about the orchards carry it, the little thorny wolves that run the rows below Petta's trees and along the brook; three lumps of resin, warmed in the hand, and the handle's whole again.

Bring them to me here at my gate and I'll set it while you watch, and then I'll show you the coring, and the verse with it. Sit. There are shoes for you, fieldhand's; you'll be walking these orchards for years, if you've any sense.
progress: Three thorn resin for Elder Hazel at her orchard gate. The young thornfangs carry it, about the Wild Orchards and along the brook in the Heartwood Fields.
complete: Set. Feel that, in the grip: the verse is back in the handle, where she put it. Now watch my hands. Round, and under, and the core comes out in one, and the words go with it; that's how she taught me, and now it's how I've taught you.
The shoes. You'll be walking the orchards for years, if you've any sense, and I think you have.

s_hf_7.name: Boars at the Border

objective.label: Cull 4 bramble boars at the Border Gate

s_hf_7.desc: The Border Gate at the west end of the Heartwood Fields unlocked itself one morning this spring, and the bramble boars have taken the ground before it for their own. Gate-Warden Ilse wants four culled so the gate is a gate again.
offer: Ilse, gate-warden. Beyond this gate is the Timber Estates: every grove the empire felled out of Heartwood, planted back in rows. Three hundred years this gate stood locked, and one morning this spring it unlocked itself; nobody pushed it. The court had us put the leaves to and hold them, and we hold them, until the court says otherwise.

And the bramble boars think it opened for them. They've come down off the ridge and rooted up the whole approach, and they stand about the gate like it's a sty. Three hundred years shut, and the first thing that wants through is pigs.

Cull four of them, here, on the ground before the gate. Then it's a gate again. A hi-potion for you, and a tusk off one of them for your trouble; and when the court lets you through, go and look at what the empire did on the other side. In rows.
progress: Four bramble boars on the ground before the Border Gate, at the west end of the Heartwood Fields. Then report to Gate-Warden Ilse at the gate.
complete: Four. The gate's a gate again, not a sty, and I can see the road to it. Here, the potion, and a tusk; the woodwrights set them in rings, if you want to know what a tusk is for in this city.
When the court sends word that the leaves can open, go through and look at the rows. Everyone should, once. Then come back and tell me if you still think a tree is just a tree.

s_ms_5.name: The Far Shore

objective.label: Stand on the Ferry Piers and in the Shore Wood, where the far shore went quiet

s_ms_5.desc: Mereth's grandmother was rowing the last crossing on the night the far shore went quiet. Stand on the Ferry Piers where she told the story, then in the Shore Wood where you can see across the water, and listen for the difference between hushed and finished.
offer: Mereth; my grandfather kept the ferry here, and his mother before him. My grandmother was on the water the night the far shore went quiet: rowing home on the last crossing, with the empire's shore across the gulf making its evening sounds, dogs and a smith and a mother shouting her children in to supper. Then, between one pull of the oars and the next, nothing.

She told it the same way every time, and the family has told it her way ever since. Not hushed, she said; finished. Hushed is a held breath. Finished is a door. She said the difference is the whole story, if you are listening. She told it from the piers, where she landed, and then she would walk us up into the shore wood, where you can see the whole gulf and the far shore across it.

Do what she did. Stand on the Ferry Piers first. Then go up into the Shore Wood, north-east of the piers across the road, and look across the water at where the far shore is. See if you can hear it. Two potions, for walking it.
progress: Stand on the Ferry Piers, then go up into the Shore Wood, north-east of the piers across the road, and look across the water to the far shore. Then come back to Mereth at the piers.
complete: You looked. Everyone looks the same after; it is in the shoulders. It is quiet over there still, and it is not the hushed kind. She would have liked you. She liked people who listened to the whole of it and did not fill the end in for her. The potions, as I said.

s_ms_6.name: Lights That Are Not the Lamp

objective.label: Put out 4 bog wisps that draw boats off the Point

s_ms_6.desc: Lamp-Keeper Orla's lamp on the Point tells boats where the rock is, and the bog wisps on the flats below tell them otherwise. Put out four bog wisps so the Point's lamp is the only light on the Moonmere Shores tonight.
offer: Lamp-Keeper Orla. The Point's lamp was my family's before the academy took it over, and we kept it anyway; it says one thing to every boat on the water, 'here is the rock', and it has said it every night for three hundred years, including the one that mattered.

The bog wisps on the flats below the Point have taken to saying 'here is a better rock'. They are pale lights that drift low over the mud at the water's edge, and a boatman out past dusk sees two lights and believes the nearer one. Last week a reed-boat went onto the mud under them and the cutter walked home wet.

Put out four bog wisps for me. They are on the flats directly below the Point, between the lamp and the water. Then the only light on this shore is mine, which is how my family kept it before the academy and how we keep it now. There are two ethers from the lamp store in it; the academy pays for them, and I decide who gets them.
progress: Four bog wisps, on the flats directly below the Point, between the lamp and the water, on the Moonmere Shores. They drift low over the mud at dusk.
complete: Four. One light on the shore tonight, and it is the right one. Ether from the lamp store, as I promised: the academy pays for it, and I decide who gets it, and tonight that is you. If you are ever out on the water after dark, steer for mine.

s_ms_7.name: Off the North Road

objective.label: Drive 4 marsh lights off the north road below the border gate

s_ms_7.desc: Marsh lights have come onto the north road of the Moonmere Shores below the North Gate, and the watch's supplies and relief go up that road. Proctor Anselm wants four of them driven off so the road is the academy's again.
offer: Proctor Anselm, Causeway Proctor; I keep order at the causeway head, explorers to the left of the causeway, fares to the right, and I keep the roads the academy owns on this shore. The academy keeps the road; it does not keep the water. That has always been the arrangement, and the water has always kept its side of it.

The marsh lights have stopped keeping to the water. They are on the north road now, up by the North Gate, where the road ends at the Border Gate the court's watch holds shut. The carters I send up with the watch's supplies, and the relief I send up to stand Watch-Sergeant Haldis's shifts, come back saying something walked beside them the whole way with a light and no lantern.

Drive four marsh lights off the north road below the gate. They are the tall lights that pace you; they go out if you hit them hard enough. Explorers to the left, fares to the right, and nothing glowing between here and the gate. There are woldcloth slops in it from the proctors' stores.
progress: Four marsh lights, on the north road of the Moonmere Shores below the North Gate, the Border Gate at the road's end. They are the tall lights that pace you after dark.
complete: Four. The road is the academy's again, from the causeway head to the gate, and the carters can stop looking over their shoulders on the way up to Haldis. Slops from the proctors' stores, as I said: you carry a court's charter, you may as well look as if you do.

s_nr_5.name: The Cliff Coast

objective.label: Walk the Cliff Coast to the Western Shelter

s_nr_5.desc: Duelist-Master Sabel of Caerdun, waiting at the Halfway Inn, asks you to walk from the Cliff Coast north of the inn west to the Western Shelter at the road's Caerdun end and tell her what you thought about on the way; she calls it composure.
offer: Sabel. Duelist-Master of Caerdun; I keep the duelling ground in the drill yards and teach the code there. I came up the North Road because Caerdun's wage book, the record of every night our garrison has stood watch since the empire left, ends in a settlement in full, with a date on it, and I wanted to sit at a table with two people who would tell me their cities had found the same thing.
They have. So now I wait, and I think, and the Cliff Coast is where I think.
A duelist learns one thing before the sword: to stand somewhere frightening and keep her mind her own. The cliff is good for that. Wind, wolves, and a long drop into the sea beside you the whole way.

Walk it for me. From the inn go north to the Cliff Coast, then follow the cliff west and come down to the Western Shelter, by the road at the far western end, near the way down to the Caerdun Fields. Then come back and tell me what you thought about. I am not asking for the view. I have a Hi-Potion for you, which is what one gives a student.
progress: North from the inn to the Cliff Coast, then west along the cliff and down to the Western Shelter, by the road near the way to the Caerdun Fields. Keep your mind your own. Then tell me what you thought about.
