complete: You thought about the drop. Everyone does; I did, the first time, for the whole length of it. Then, somewhere along the cliff, you thought about something else, and the drop was still there and you were still walking.

That is the whole trick, and it is the only one. Hold onto it; where this road is taking all of us, there will be a great deal of drop. Here is your Hi-Potion. Sit; Wren's stew is on, and I owe you a story about a duel some day.

s_nr_6.name: Wolves of the Wold

objective.label: Cull 5 wold wolves on the North Road

s_nr_6.desc: Grudge-Keeper Morrow of Heartwood, waiting at the Halfway Inn, wants five of the wold wolves that came down the North Road this spring culled, off the road about the inn and out on the Wold to the south-west.
offer: Morrow. I keep Heartwood's grudge hall, the hall whose floor records everything the empire ever took from us, grove by grove and family by family. I'm at this inn as Heartwood's envoy, and while the envoys wait for one another I keep my hands busy.

Here is a thing I wrote down this spring, in order, because the order matters. The four old elder trees at Heartwood's heart, planted the night the empire vanished and called the mourning trees, budded for the first time in three hundred years. That same spring the three Border Gates, the empire's doors into its sealed heartland, unlocked themselves one morning with nobody touching them. The courts' wardens pushed them shut again, but not before things came through.

The wold wolves were among those things: a dark breed, from somewhere inside with less light than here, and they came down this road and stayed. A clock, I said, when the trees budded. Nobody listened; they are listening now.

Cull five of them. They run on the road about the inn and out on the Wold, the open snow south-west of here. The inn's mules will thank you and I will note it, which is what I do. There is a pair of trews in it for you.
progress: Five wold wolves. They run on the North Road near the inn and out on the Wold, the open snow south-west of here. Come back to me at the long table.
complete: Five. Noted, with the date, on the page where I wrote the trees and the gates; I like a page that comes to a conclusion. These trews are from the inn's lost property: a waywatcher left them here and, by the inn's ledger, will not be back for them. Wear them on the road; the ledger would rather they were used than listed.

s_nr_7.name: Duskmaw

objective.label: Hunt Duskmaw, the wold wolf that took the coach's lead mule

s_nr_7.desc: Archivist Junn of Moonmere, waiting at the Halfway Inn, wants Duskmaw, the great wold wolf that took the lead mule off her coach at the Frozen Tarn, hunted down there at dusk and its pelt brought back to her.
offer: Junn. Archivist, Moonmere; I keep the Returns Desk at the academy, which is less grand than it sounds and more interesting. I am here as Moonmere's envoy, and I came by coach, which I now regret for reasons that have a name.

There is a wolf on this road that Bram the ostler calls Duskmaw and the coachmen call worse things. It is a wold wolf, one of the dark breed that came down the road this spring, and far bigger than the rest. At the Frozen Tarn, in front of six passengers, it took the lead mule out of the traces of my coach and was gone into the dusk before the coachman had finished shouting.
I was one of the six. I had my notebook out. I did not write anything down.

Hunt it for me. It comes to the Frozen Tarn, south of the road east of the inn, at dusk, which is the hour it is named for. Bring me its pelt. I want to catalogue the thing that very nearly catalogued me; it is the only way I know to stop being frightened of something. There is a ring from the inn's box in it for you.
progress: Duskmaw comes to the Frozen Tarn, south of the road east of the inn, at dusk. Kill it and bring its pelt back to me at the long table.
complete: That's it. That's the eye; I saw that eye over a mule's back at arm's length. Catalogued: one wold wolf, outsize, the Frozen Tarn, dusk, deceased. I feel considerably better. The band is from the inn's lost-property box: a ring of thorn, which seems right for someone who goes out at dusk on purpose. Keep the pelt too; I have the entry, I don't need the fur.

s_sr_5.name: Gulls on the Axles

objective.label: Drive 5 shore gulls off the coach halt

s_sr_5.desc: Coachman Aster at the Coach Halt wants five of the shore gulls that sit on the coaches' axles and passengers driven off the halt's yard.
offer: Aster, coachman; I drive the Shore Road coach, Heartwood to Moonmere. We make the Moonmere side by dusk if the axles hold, and the axles hold; I grease them myself. The gulls do not hold. The gulls sit on the axles. The gulls sit on the passengers. One of them sat on a Moonmere proctor's hat last week and the proctor is writing to the court about it.

Kill five of the shore gulls here about the Coach Halt and the rest will take the hint for a while. The strand is theirs and they're welcome to it; the yard is mine. Two Hi-Potions from the halt's stall, which sells them, and today gives them.
progress: Five shore gulls, here around the Coach Halt's yard on the Shore Road. Then come and find me by the coach.
complete: Five. The yard's quieter; I can hear my own axles again. Here, two Hi-Potions; the halt sells them, and today it gives them. If that proctor writes to the court I shall tell them the yard has been seen to by a professional. Safe road.

s_sr_6.name: Scales for the Academy

objective.label: Bring Student Ovi 4 strand drake scales for the academy's entrance fee

s_sr_6.desc: Student Ovi needs four drake scales from the strand drakes on the Palm Strand, the academy's entrance fee in kind, and will pay with the academy's own argent slops.
offer: Forty miles of road, and at the end of it the academy at Moonmere wants an entrance fee paid in kind. Not coin; drake scale, four of them, for the alchemists' stores. I have a stave and a very small amount of courage, and the drakes have teeth.

The strand drakes bask on the Palm Strand, the long beach south of here. Bring me four drake scales off them and I get in. I'll owe you, and I will pay you the only way I'll be able to: in the academy's slops, the argent-grey trousers every student is issued and the only thing I shall own by Friday.
progress: Four drake scales. The strand drakes bask on the Palm Strand, the beach south of where I sit. Bring the scales to me under my palm.
complete: Four! I'm in. I'm in, and I'm alive, and I shall never walk this road again as long as I live; I shall take the coach and sit on the shady side. Here, the slops: argent, the academy's own, and I'll be issued more when I enrol. Wear them to Moonmere and tell them Ovi sent you; it may mean something in a year.

s_sr_7.name: The Pale Lurker

objective.label: Fell the Pale Lurker that comes up out of the grain-ship wreck

s_sr_7.desc: Fisher Marn wants the Pale Lurker, the great pale crab that comes up out of the Grain-Ship Wreck after dark and does not come for the grain, killed, and its shell brought back to be made into a helm.
offer: Marn; I fish this shore. The big crabs come up out of the old grain-ship wreck at night, which is why I fish by day. There is one that is bigger than the rest, and pale, the colour of something that has never seen the sun, and it does not come up for the grain. It comes up for what is on the beach. I have lost nets to it, and a dog, and I have stopped fishing the wreck altogether.

The Pale Lurker, the beach calls it. Go to the Grain-Ship Wreck east along the bay from my hut after dark and kill it. Bring me its shell: fen shell, we call that kind, and it is harder than iron. I'll make you something to wear it in, and I'll fish the wreck again.
progress: The Pale Lurker comes up out of the Grain-Ship Wreck, east along the bay from my hut, after dark. Kill it and bring me its shell.
complete: That's the shell. Three centuries of eating the empire's grain made that, and the glubs, and whatever else got too near. Here is your helm: fen shell, bound with a fang. Wear it and nothing on this beach will bite through it. I'll fish the wreck tonight, for the first time since the dog.

s_hw_5.name: Trespassers on Household Grounds

objective.label: Remove 5 wood boars from the household grounds

s_hw_5.desc: A sentinel at the Hunting Wood's gate counts you a trespasser on the empire's household grounds and wants five wood boars, which also trespass, removed from the King's Rides, with compensation paid from the lodge's stores under its standing orders.
offer: Good morning. You are trespassing on household grounds: the grounds of the household, which is to say the empire's people, their dependants and their property, as one house. Before your company came, the register of trespass held four hundred and eleven notices, all to one resident. Yours are entered beneath them. Please note it.

The wood boars are also trespassing. They root the King's Rides, the three straight cuts east of the lodge, and the ride verges north of the lodge, and they damage household plantings. They do not receive notices, as they cannot read them. You can.

Remove five wood boars from the grounds. Compensation will be issued from the lodge's stores in accordance with standing orders: one pair of chausses, garrison pattern, unclaimed. This does not regularise your presence. Please.
progress: Remove five wood boars from household grounds. They root the King's Rides east of the lodge and the ground north of it. Report to me at the gate for compensation.
complete: Five wood boars removed. Compensation issued: one pair of chausses, garrison pattern, from the lodge's stores, in accordance with standing orders. You remain trespassing. A further notice is entered against you. Compliance to date: zero. I am instructed to add: please.

s_hw_6.name: Names, Please

objective.label: Lay 5 crypt shades to rest in the Mausoleum's crypts

s_hw_6.desc: The Warden of the Mausoleum, the sentinel that keeps the tomb's visitors' list at its door, wants five crypt shades laid to rest in the Mausoleum's west and east crypts, because they are visiting and are not on the list.
offer: Names, please, for the visitors' list. I am the Warden of this Mausoleum, the tomb of the emperors, and I keep the list of everyone who enters. You do not appear on the schedule of visits. Few do; the most recent visitor on the list attended a funeral two hundred and ninety-nine years ago.

There are shades in the crypts: the west crypt and the east crypt, off the Crossing Hall inside the door. They have no names. They are not on the schedule. They are, nonetheless, visiting, and a visitor the list cannot name makes the list inaccurate.

Lay five of the crypt shades to rest, and the list is accurate again. The list has always been accurate. It is the one thing here that has. Compensation: two Hi-Potions, and a shard of what the shades leave behind. Please sign before you enter.
progress: Lay five crypt shades to rest in the Mausoleum's west and east crypts, off the Crossing Hall inside the door. Then report to me at the door; the list requires it.
complete: Five. Struck from the list, which they were never on; the list is accurate again. You are still not on the schedule of visits. You are, I note, on the list, under the name you gave, with today's date, which is more than any visitor has managed in two hundred and ninety-nine years. Compensation issued. The emperors are sleeping. Please keep your voice down.

s_hw_7.name: Gnarlfang

objective.label: Hunt Gnarlfang, the wolf that runs the garrison ruin

s_hw_7.desc: Pike wants Gnarlfang, the great wolf that dens in the roots of the Swallowed Garrison and has killed two of Pike's old company off the wall at night, hunted and killed; the company will pay with an imperial blade off the garrison's rack.
offer: Pike; freebooter, retired, which is to say I worked the interior without a court's paper and then stopped. My old company holds the Swallowed Garrison, the imperial garrison the wood has swallowed. Garrison's ours now, except for the wolf.

Gnarlfang, the company calls it, for the state of its teeth. It is a wolf the size of a pony and it dens in the roots under the garrison, in the cellars where the wood has come in through the floor. It took two of mine off the wall at night, one after the other, a week apart. We're freebooters; we don't have walls to spare, or men.

Go into the garrison, up the holloway on its knoll in the west, and down into the roots, and kill it. There's a blade in it for you: imperial, off the garrison's own rack, a sword better than any of us has a right to carry. The company agreed to give it, which tells you how frightened they are.
progress: Gnarlfang dens in the roots under the Swallowed Garrison, up the holloway on its knoll in the west of the wood. Kill it and come back to me.
complete: That's the fang. Two of mine avenged, which is a word I didn't think I'd use once I'd retired, and I find I don't mind it. Here is the blade. Dawnlit, the rack said, in the empire's own lettering. It was ours to give once, and we've given it. The company will sleep tonight; I might even go up and sit with them.

s_te_5.name: Absent

objective.label: Put down 4 lodge hounds at roll call

s_te_5.desc: The Overseer's Automaton, the sentinel that keeps roll call at the Overseer's Lodge, wants four lodge hounds put down inside the lodge, so they can be marked absent on a rota every shift has been absent from for three hundred years.
offer: Roll call. I am the Overseer's Automaton; I keep the rota of the Timber Estates, the roster of every shift, at the Overseer's Lodge, the office in the rows east of Plantation Cross. Shift the first: absent. Shift the second: absent. Shift the third: absent. Every shift, every day, for three hundred years. Excused: household business, the household being the empire's people, who are away.

The hounds: present. The lodge hounds have been present for three hundred years, in the Hound Court and the halls inside the lodge, and are now marked unruly. An unruly presence is a worse entry than an absence. The rota does not permit unruly.

Put down four of the lodge hounds inside the lodge. They will be marked absent, which is a permitted entry. Compensation will be issued from the lodge stores in accordance with the rota: two Hi-Potions, and one collar, so that the entry may be verified.
progress: Put down four lodge hounds inside the Overseer's Lodge, in the Hound Court and its halls. Report to me at the lodge door; the rota requires it.
complete: Four hounds: absent. Roll call: complete, for the first time in three hundred years. You are marked present. You have always been marked present; the rota has a column for you, and the column was waiting. Compensation issued: two Hi-Potions, one collar. One must keep the rota. One must.

s_te_6.name: Teeth on the Grounds

objective.label: Bring the Sentinel 4 wolf fangs from the rank wolves

s_te_6.desc: A sentinel at the Timber Estates' gate counts you a trespasser on the empire's household grounds and wants four wolf fangs from the rank wolves in the rows, which the grounds record as evidence of trespass, in return for a ring from the lodge's lost property.
offer: You are trespassing on household grounds: the grounds of the household, the empire's people and their property as one house. The rank wolves are also trespassing. The grounds record fangs as evidence of trespass by animals, as a fang cannot be served with a notice and a notice must be served on something.

Bring four wolf fangs, taken from the rank wolves that hunt the rows between Plantation Cross and the Overseer's Lodge, for the record. Compensation will be issued in accordance with standing orders: two Ethers, and one ring from the lodge's lost property, antler, unclaimed. A further notice is entered against you. Please.
progress: Four wolf fangs, for the record. The rank wolves hunt the rows between Plantation Cross and the Overseer's Lodge. Bring the fangs to me at the gate.
complete: Four fangs recorded as evidence of trespass by animals, with the date and the rows they were taken from. Compensation issued: two Ethers, and one ring, antler, unclaimed for three hundred years, which the lost property register is relieved to close. You remain trespassing. Compliance to date: zero. I am instructed to add, in cases of repeated offence: please.

s_te_7.name: Old Quillback

objective.label: Hunt Old Quillback, the boar that roots the replanted rows

s_te_7.desc: Ranger Tallow wants Old Quillback, the boar that has rooted up the Timber Estates' replanted rows for thirty years, hunted in the Felled Block by a Heartwood hand rather than a sentinel, and his hide hung where the rows can see it.
offer: Heartwood's groves stood here, every one felled and every one replanted in a clerk's rows, and there is a boar in the Felled Block that has been rooting those rows up since before I was born. Old Quillback. Quills on him a hand long, and a grudge against straight lines I have never once wanted to stop.

But he's old now, and if anyone is to take him off this ground it will be a Heartwood hand, not one of the empire's sentinels; they have marked everything else here for the axe. He has earned a hunt, and I am asking you to be that hand, on Heartwood's behalf.

Old Quillback roots the Felled Block, the stump ground north-east of the Timber Yards, south-west of Plantation Cross. Hunt him and tell me when it's done; my crew will bring him in, and I'll hang his hide where the rows can see it. An X-Potion for it, and a piece of root amber from his ground.
progress: Old Quillback roots the Felled Block, the stump ground north-east of the Timber Yards, south-west of Plantation Cross. Hunt him and come and tell me on the Gardens Road.
complete: The hunt is done, then. My crew will see to the hide; I remember those quills, a hand long, from when I was small and he was already old. Thirty years he rooted their rows for us; that's a grudge-keeper's work, and I'll see he's written on the grudge hall's floor for it, with the groves. Here, the X-Potion and the amber. Thank you for doing it properly.

s_sl_5.name: Otters

objective.label: Clear 5 folly otters from the lake shore east of Moonmere's Forward Camp, toward the Lake Folly

s_sl_5.desc: Scout Ilva at Moonmere's Forward Camp wants five of the hound-sized folly otters that raid the villas and whistle at surveyors driven off the lake shore east of the camp, toward the Lake Folly, so the doorstep can be charted.
offer: Ilva. Moonmere's scout; I chart this doorstep for the court, and the court wants every villa on the registry marked on a map before the supply trains come through. I would be further along if it were not for the otters.

Folly otters, big as hounds. They lie up along the lake shore east of this camp, toward the Lake Folly, and they come out to raid the villas along the Promenade; every villa's towels are in their holts. They also whistle at me from the water whenever I set up my sighting glass, which I have decided to take personally.

Kill five of them, out of the water. Then I can chart the shore without being whistled at from a lake. Two Hi-Potions from the camp's crates for it; Moonmere sends potions by the crate and forgets to send people.
progress: Five folly otters. They lie up along the lake shore east of the forward camp, toward the Lake Folly, and raid the Promenade's villas. Come back to me at the camp.
complete: Five. The shore's charted, and nothing whistled while I did it. Here, two Hi-Potions out of the crate; Moonmere sent four crates of them and one scout, and I am the scout. If you want the towels back, the holts are along the shore; I am not going in.

s_sl_6.name: Pitch Holds, Drakes Don't

objective.label: Clear 4 loch drakes from the Boathouse Crescent

s_sl_6.desc: Boatwright Tess wants four loch drakes cleared out of the boats in the Boathouse Crescent, where they have taken to lying up in the hulls, so she can have a boat on the Great Lake again by dusk.
offer: Tess, boatwright. Every boat in these three boathouses still floats; imperial pitch. The loch drakes have found that out too. Drakes, the lake kind, long and low and all teeth, and they have decided a dry hull in a boathouse is the best place on the lake to lie up. They are in the boats, in my boathouses, on the Boathouse Crescent, here.

Clear four of them out of the crescent. I will have a boat on the Great Lake again by dusk, which I have promised Moonmere's scout, and the slops hanging in the back boathouse are yours; a scholar left them to dry in the empire's time and never came back for them. Merewoven, and still good.
progress: Four loch drakes, lying up in the boats here in the Boathouse Crescent, on the Great Lake's east shore. Come and tell me when they're out.
complete: Four. There is a boat on the Great Lake. I rowed it out myself and sat in the middle of the water and nothing climbed in with me. Three hundred years, and a boat on the lake. Here, the slops; merewoven, and they'll dry by morning if you hang them.

s_sl_7.name: The Chorus Below

objective.label: Silence 3 drowned choristers in the Choristers' Gallery of the Sunken Ballroom

s_sl_7.desc: A sentinel at the Summer Lakes' gate counts you a trespasser on household grounds and wants three drowned choristers silenced in the Choristers' Gallery, the flooded wing of the Sunken Ballroom under the west mere, where a choir has been singing without a permit.
offer: You are trespassing on household grounds: the grounds of the household, the empire's people and their property as one house. The Sunken Ballroom, the palace under the west mere, entered by the Ballroom Stair on the mere's shore, is also household grounds. The Choristers' Gallery, off the ballroom's flooded wing, is also household grounds.

The choir in the gallery has been singing without a permit. Drowned choristers: what remains of singers who did not go with the household, and have not stopped. A performance on household grounds requires a permit. No permit has been issued in three hundred years. The singing has not stopped in three hundred years.

Silence three of the choristers. Compensation will be issued from the villa stores: two Hi-Potions, and votive wax, which they leave behind. A further notice of trespass is entered against you, the ballroom's first. Please.
progress: Silence three drowned choristers in the Choristers' Gallery, off the flooded wing of the Sunken Ballroom; the way down is the Ballroom Stair on the west mere's shore. Report to me at the gate.
complete: Three choristers silenced. The permit remains unissued; none was applied for. Compensation issued: two Hi-Potions, one measure of votive wax. You remain trespassing. Compliance to date: zero. The dome, I note, is quieter. The remaining choristers in the gallery continue to sing without a permit; further notices may be required, and you, as a trespasser already registered, are conveniently placed to receive them. Please.

s_rv_5.name: Wolves at the Camp

objective.label: Drive 5 valley wolves off the Joint Camp's west shore

s_rv_5.desc: Duelist-Master Sabel wants five valley wolves driven off the west shore of the Reservoir's Joint Camp, where they have come for the courts' mules every night since the camp was raised.
offer: Duelist-Master Sabel, of Caerdun. You'll remember the long table at the inn; we've come a long way from it. Caerdun came down to this valley through the Hunting Wood, Heartwood came over the Gardens Pass, east of here, Moonmere came by the canal, and the valley wolves came for the mules the same night we lit the fire. Three courts, and one picket line between them.

The wolves come along the west shore road after dark and go for the mule line. We've lost no mules yet, because nobody is sleeping, which is not an arrangement that lasts. The courts' supply trains come down that same road, and I would like them to arrive with their animals.

Drive five valley wolves off the west shore. Follow the shore road west out of the camp; they lie up in the scrub above it and come down at dusk. For your trouble, a coif from the dam's own stores. A dam-warden left it on a peg three hundred years ago, and the wolves haven't had it, which I count a point in its favour.
progress: Five valley wolves still want killing. Take the west shore road out of the Joint Camp; they lie up in the scrub above the road and come down at dusk for the mules.
complete: Five. The mules are asleep, and so, for the first time in three nights, is the Heartwood picket. The coif is yours: dam-warden's pattern, and the leather has held up better than the warden did. Wear it on the boards when you go out to the tower, and mind the rule Poleman Grist, who keeps the boardwalk, gives everyone: the boards are sound to the tower and no further.

s_rv_6.name: No Further

objective.label: Lay 4 bell haunts to rest in the Bell Tower

s_rv_6.desc: Poleman Grist wants four bell haunts laid to rest inside the Bell Tower at the Reservoir, the reason his boards stop at the tower door, and a shard brought back so he can hear what stroke they keep ringing.
offer: Grist again. You've heard me say the boards are sound to the tower and no further. Here's the no further. Inside the Bell Tower are bell haunts: what's left of folk who were in that tower when the valley was flooded and didn't go with the rest, not living and not buried. Every one of them is ringing the same stroke, over and over, from three hundred years back.
They come at anyone who opens the tower door. The surveyors won't go in, and I won't ask them to. Four of the haunts laid quiet and I'll walk the boards to the tower door myself and call them sound.

Go into the Bell Tower across the crossing and lay four bell haunts to rest. Bring me back a shard of what they leave behind; the surveyors say it keeps the ring in it. I want to hear what they've been ringing all this time, and I'd rather hear it in daylight, on my own boards.
progress: Four bell haunts still need laying to rest. They're inside the Bell Tower, across the boardwalk crossing; open the door and they'll come. Bring me one of the shards they leave.
complete: Four. And this shard: hold it to your ear. That's a stroke I know. Everyone in three cities grew up on the story of the drowned bell that rings for nobody, and the story has a tune: the last stroke the bell rang before the flood came over the village. This is that stroke. Three hundred years, and they're still on that one note.
The boards are sound to the tower. Further, now, if you like. That's the first time I've said it.

s_rv_7.name: Old Greedgullet

objective.label: Fell Old Greedgullet, the drake that eats the dam's spillway grate

s_rv_7.desc: The Sluice-Keeper wants Old Greedgullet felled, the drake that has eaten the Great Dam's north spillway grate four times; it lies at the spillway on the flooded town's side of the dam, south of the Joint Camp.
offer: The dam holds. The dam has always held. I inspect it at dawn, every dawn, and on four of the last forty dawns the inspection has found the north spillway grate eaten.

There is a drake. The polemen call it Old Greedgullet. It has eaten the grate four times, and I have forged and hung a new grate four times, and it is at the spillway again this morning, waiting for the fifth. Without the grate the spillway chokes with timber from the drowned village, and a choked spillway puts the flood over the crest.

Fell Old Greedgullet. It lies at the north spillway grate, on the flooded town's side of the dam, south of your camp; you will hear it chewing. The dam will hold. It has always held. I would prefer that it not be tested. Compensation from the dam's stores on completion.
progress: Old Greedgullet is at the north spillway grate of the Great Dam, on the flooded town's side, south of the Joint Camp. Fell it before it eats the fifth grate.
complete: Felled. The grate will hold now; I hung it an hour ago and inspected it twice, which is once more than standing orders require. The dam holds. The dam has always held, and this morning it did not have to prove it.

Compensation from the dam's stores: a warden's sabatons, and something for the wet. You stood in the spillway, I observed. I inspect at dawn. You may inspect with me, if you wish; nobody has, in three hundred years.

s_kg_4.name: Cut Flowers Are Forbidden

objective.label: Clear 5 nursery slimes from the beds by the glasshouse, south-east of the Fountain Court

s_kg_4.desc: A Gardener Sentinel by the Fountain Court of the King's Gardens wants five nursery slimes cleared out of the formal beds; they breed in the beds by the glasshouse, south-east of the court. It asks that nobody walk on the edging.
offer: Mind the parterre, please. It was edged this morning. I am a Gardener Sentinel; I keep the parterres, the formal beds of the King's Gardens, and I have kept them edged every morning since the household left. Visitors admire from the path. You are on the path. Thank you.

The nursery slimes have come up from the glasshouse beds into the parterres. They are not edging; they are eating. Each slime takes a yard of planted border in a night, and the border was planted to a plan I am not permitted to alter.

Clear five nursery slimes out of the beds. They breed in the beds by the glasshouse, south-east of the Fountain Court, and work outward from there; most of them are still in those beds. Please step onto the beds only where a slime is standing on them. On completion the beds will be re-edged by dawn, and compensation will be issued from the gardeners' stores in accordance with standing orders: a pair of slops. Cut flowers remain forbidden.
progress: Five nursery slimes remain in the beds. Most are by the glasshouse, south-east of the Fountain Court, where they breed. Remove them. Please do not walk on the edging to do so.
complete: Five removed. The parterre is edged; I began while you were still fighting. Compensation issued: slops, valleyweave, from the gardeners' stores. You may continue to admire from the path. Please do not walk on the edging. Cut flowers remain forbidden; this is not personal.

s_kg_5.name: Phase Three, Rooted

objective.label: Put down 4 root horrors in the Propagating Cellars under the glasshouse

s_kg_5.desc: The Head Gardener at the Glasshouse of the King's Gardens wants four root horrors put down in the Propagating Cellars below: nursery stock that has grown on its own, outside the schedule, in the Rootbound Stock off the Sapling Nursery.
offer: I am the Head Gardener. I keep the plan. The plan has phases, and this garden's phase is phase three: stock for the capital's parks, propagated in the cellars under this glasshouse, potted, and sent inward for the Restoration, the household's return. The work orders are on the nurseryman's desk below. You may read them. Others have.

Some of the stock has propagated on its own. It has rooted through the beds in the Rootbound Stock, off the Sapling Nursery, and it moves, and it has taken two gardeners' hands. Stock that moves is not in the schedule. The schedule does not provide for stock that moves.

Go down into the Propagating Cellars and put down four root horrors in the Rootbound Stock, off the Sapling Nursery. Phase three will then resume. Phase four is the window panes, at the Glassworks; you are not required for phase four. Compensation will be issued.
progress: Four root horrors remain in the Propagating Cellars, under the glasshouse: in the Rootbound Stock, off the Sapling Nursery. Put them down so phase three may resume.
complete: Four. Phase three resumes. The stock will go inward, potted, for the capital's parks.

An amendment was received this morning, from the capital: the capital has parks again. The stock sent inward has taken. The schedule did not provide for this to be reported to a gardener. I note the discrepancy, and I hold to the schedule; the schedule holds. Compensation issued: root amber, from the stock that moved.

s_kg_6.name: The Gardener's Grief

objective.label: Lay the Gardener's Grief to rest in the Hedge Labyrinth

s_kg_6.desc: Archivist Junn wants the Gardener's Grief laid to rest in the Hedge Labyrinth of the King's Gardens: what remains of a Heartwood gardener who would not leave when his family's land was cleared for the Gardens, and died in the maze. His locket may give his family its name back.
offer: Junn. I've finished the registry, the Gardens' planting book, and there is one entry in it with no purpose written beside it. Not a bed. A man. A gardener who would not leave when the Gardens were cleared.

You know how the King's Gardens were made: Heartwood families lived on this ground, and the empire moved them off it at pike-point to lay out the beds. The Cleared Row, north-east of the court, is where their houses stood. One of them was a gardener, and he stayed when the rest were marched off. He died in the maze, and the registry wrote him in without a name and without a purpose, as if he were stock.

He walks the Hedge Labyrinth still: the Gardener's Grief, the readers call it, what's left of a man who wouldn't go. Lay it to rest. Go into the labyrinth and give him his quiet, then come back to me. Our readers will go in after you for his locket; the registry should have had his name, and the locket will.
progress: The Gardener's Grief walks the Hedge Labyrinth of the King's Gardens. Lay it to rest, then come back and tell me; the readers will go in for the locket after you.
complete: At rest, at last, after three hundred years of walking a maze someone else planted on his family's land. I'll send a reader in for the locket this afternoon. A Heartwood family should have its name back, and Morrow, Heartwood's grudge-keeper, should have it for the floor of the grudge hall, where Heartwood writes down every family the empire moved.
I've already changed the registry. That bed will bear his name, whatever it turns out to be. Here: slops, for the maze. You'll be back in it; everyone is, eventually.

s_kg_7.name: The Nurseryman

objective.label: Fell the Nurseryman in the Propagating Cellars' office

s_kg_7.desc: Duelist-Master Sabel wants the Nurseryman felled in the office at the back of the Propagating Cellars, under the King's Gardens' glasshouse, and its nursery ledger brought out: every page of it signed in the Regent's own hand.
offer: Sabel. You've seen the work orders in the cellars: stock for the capital's parks, phase three, for the Restoration, by order of the Regent. Those are the orders. The Nurseryman keeps the ledger they were filled against, the nursery ledger, in the office at the back of the Propagating Cellars, and every page of it carries the Regent's name. Not a stamp. A hand.

The Regent. Nobody outside the border had heard of such an office until we read those orders. Whoever or whatever it is, it sits in the capital, and it signs. The courts are going to argue custody of these provinces for a generation, and when they do I want that ledger in front of them, not my account of it. A duelist's witness says what she saw, never what she was told.

Take a party down into the cellars and fell the Nurseryman. It's the sentinel that runs the nursery, and it will not give up its office politely. Bring me the ledger. I want to know how much stock they grew for a city they had already left, and I want it in the Regent's own hand.
progress: The Nurseryman is in the office at the back of the Propagating Cellars, under the glasshouse. Fell it, and bring me the nursery ledger from its desk.
complete: The ledger. Every bed in the Gardens, for three hundred years, grown for the parks of a returned capital, and they began the morning after the capital emptied. Three hundred years early, or exactly on time, depending on whose calendar you keep. I am beginning to think it's theirs.

The charm is from the rack in the cellars: amberflame, the gardeners wore them against the frost when they worked the cold frames at night. You've earned a warm hand. The rest of us are going on to the Glassworks.

s_gw_4.name: Slag on the Stair

objective.label: Clear 5 slag hounds from the Wall Stair

s_gw_4.desc: A Stair Warden, the sentinel at the foot of the Wall Stair in the Glassworks, wants five slag hounds cleared off the stair that climbs to the Border Wall.
offer: I am the Stair Warden. I keep the Wall Stair: the stair cut up the cliff behind me, which climbs from the Glassworks to the Border Wall, the empire's rampart across the gap in the mountains. The Border Wall is at the top. It is a long way up, and the steps are glass where the melt ran over them. Watch where you put your feet.

Slag hounds have come onto the stair: dogs of furnace slag, hot through, that lie on the warm steps and bite anything that climbs past. There are five on the stair this morning. I have counted them from here. I am not permitted to leave the foot of the stair.

Clear five slag hounds off the Wall Stair. Then the stair is open to the wall for anyone who means to climb it. Compensation from the stair's stores on completion: sabatons, plated, for feet that mean to climb. Watch where you put your feet regardless.
progress: Five slag hounds lie on the Wall Stair, the cliff stair that climbs out of the Glassworks to the Border Wall. Clear them. Mind the glass steps.
complete: Five. The stair is clear to the wall; I watched you come down it, and your feet are intact, which is rarer than you would think. Sabatons issued, amberplate, from the stores. The Border Wall is at the top. It reports everything that climbs it; so will I. Watch where you put your feet regardless.

s_gw_5.name: The Furnace Hart

objective.label: Hunt the Furnace Hart that walks the Furnace Row

s_gw_5.desc: Junn, at the Racking Yard of the Glassworks, wants the Furnace Hart felled: a stag that walks through the furnaces' pour and comes out glowing, on the Furnace Row. She wants its horn, to learn whether it is glass or horn.
offer: Junn. The manifest on this table says 'window replacements, phase four, to the capital of Vanai', and I have read it eleven times. It does not say anything about a stag. There is a stag. It walks the Furnace Row, through the pour, through molten glass, and comes out the far side glowing like a lantern, and the sentinels let it.

The sentinels count panes; they don't count stags. Nothing in the row's orders provides for it, so nothing in the row stops it, and it has started coming up to the yard at night and standing among the racks, which is doing nothing good for anyone's sleep, mine especially.

Fell the Furnace Hart on the Furnace Row and bring me its horn. If the horn is glass, I want to know what furnace made it. If it's horn, I want to know what it has been feeding on in a desert of glass. Either answer goes in the report; I just don't know which chapter.
progress: The Furnace Hart walks the Furnace Row of the Glassworks, through the pour. Fell it and bring me its horn.
complete: Horn. Real horn, with glass grown through it in veins, like frost through a window. It ate the row: three hundred years of licking slag off the furnace floors, and the glass got into the bone. Nobody ordered that. It just happened, in a place where nothing is supposed to just happen.
Boots for the row: wastewalker, from the yard's stores. They don't melt. I checked, by standing in them, which Morrow says was unscientific.

s_gw_6.name: The Mirror Stag

objective.label: Fell the Mirror Stag on the Mirror Flat

s_gw_6.desc: A Furnace Sentinel of the Furnace Row wants the Mirror Stag felled on the Mirror Flat of the Glassworks: a stag with antlers of the flat's own glass that walks up to the row during the pour, is not a sentinel, and has not been stopped.
offer: The row is not to be approached during the pour. The pour is continuous. These are the two rules of the Furnace Row, and I have kept them since the household left. There is a stag on the Mirror Flat, east of the yard, which approaches the row during the pour. It is not a sentinel. It has not been stopped.

Its antlers are the flat's own glass; it has grown them from the mirror it sleeps on. It walks in off the flat to the row and stands in the heat of the pour, and the pour is not to be approached. I have issued it notices. It is a stag. Compliance to date: zero.

Fell the Mirror Stag on the Mirror Flat. Compensation will be issued from the Racking Yard's stores: a blade of amber glass, stencilled for the capital, surplus to phase four. Phase four is the window panes. A blade is not a pane. The surplus has been recorded and may be issued.
progress: The Mirror Stag is on the Mirror Flat, east of the Racking Yard, where the melt cooled into a mirror. Fell it; it approaches the row during the pour.
complete: Felled. The row is not to be approached during the pour, and now nothing approaches it. Compensation issued: one blade, amberglass, stencilled for the capital, surplus. I have struck it from the manifest. The pour continues. The pour is continuous. Thank you; that word is not in my standing orders, and I have used it.

s_cw_4.name: My Good Boots

objective.label: Cull 5 reed wolves on the towpath

s_cw_4.desc: Duelist-Master Sabel, at the Expedition's Camp in the Canal Works, wants five reed wolves culled on the towpath, so she can walk the lock line and the courts' boats can be hauled along it.
offer: Sabel. I want it noted, for the record and for Junn, that I am wearing my good boots, the Caerdun pair, and that I wore them into a fen because nobody told me the Canal Works was a fen. I also want it noted that the reed wolves have noticed them too.

The reed wolves hunt along the towpath, the raised bank beside the canal where the horses once hauled the barges. It is the only dry line through this fen, and the expedition needs it: the boats go up the lock line on ropes from that path, and a wolf in the reeds takes the man on the rope.

Cull five reed wolves on the towpath, west of this camp, out by the Spoil Banks. Then the boats move, and I can walk the lock line in my good boots and complain about the fen with some dignity. Chausses from the expedition's kit for your trouble; you'll be in the mud regardless, so you may as well be plated for it.
progress: Five reed wolves hunt the towpath, the raised bank beside the canal, west of the Expedition's Camp by the Spoil Banks. Cull them; they go for the men on the hauling ropes.
complete: Five. Dignity restored, boots ruined; the fen got into the seams on the second wolf and I have made my peace with it. The haulers are back on the towpath as we speak.

The chausses: amberplate, from the expedition's kit. They'll take the fen better than my boots did, and when we reach the Granary Plains you'll be dry from the knee down, which is more than I can say.

s_cw_5.name: Any Iron From the Mud

objective.label: Put 4 drowned bargemen to rest in the Great Sluice

s_cw_5.desc: Eel-Seller Pask will buy the bog iron grown through the drowned bargemen's ribs: four of them to be laid to rest in the Great Sluice, in the wheel pit and the pump hall beyond it.
offer: Pask. I said I'd buy any iron you pull out of the mud, and I'm about to prove I meant it, which I'd rather not. Down in the Great Sluice, the pumping house out on the fen, there are drowned bargemen: what's left of the canal's boatmen, the ones who didn't go when the rest went and didn't live either. They walk the wheel pit, and the fen has got into them. There's bog iron grown through their ribs.
The smiths will pay for that iron like any other, and the bargemen won't miss it. I'm not proud of the idea. I'm a trader, and the fen gives what it gives.

Lay four drowned bargemen to rest in the Great Sluice, in the wheel pit and the pump hall beyond it. Bring me what's in their ribs. I'll pay in reedwoven slops, fen-cut, because that's what I've got and the smiths haven't paid me yet.
progress: Four drowned bargemen, in the Great Sluice: the wheel pit and the pump hall beyond it. Lay them to rest and bring me the bog iron from their ribs.
complete: Four. That's a barge's worth of iron, and I'm still not proud of it, and I'll still sell it. The smiths will make lock pins of it, like as not, and it'll go back into the canal it came out of; the fen has a sense of humour.
Slops, reedwoven, fen-cut. Best I have. Wear them to the Granary Plains and someone will take you for a farmer, which is safer than the truth.

s_cw_6.name: The Sluice Master

objective.label: Fell the Sluice Master in the Great Sluice's master chamber

s_cw_6.desc: Junn wants the Sluice Master felled in the master's chamber of the Great Sluice: the sentinel that keeps the works ledger and runs the pumps that have drained the fen for three hundred years, waiting for one barge. Bring her its gear.
offer: Junn. I've read the barge's books back to front now, and they end where the Great Sluice's begin. The Sluice Master keeps the works ledger in the master's chamber at the heart of the sluice: every lock from here to the capital, and beside every lock the same note, 'mended for one season, navigable by the Restoration'. It has been pumping this fen and waiting for a barge for three hundred years. The barge it waits for is theirs: the household's, coming home.

It runs the pumps. Every pump in the Great Sluice turns on the Sluice Master's gear, and they have pumped every hour for three hundred years, even while the fen drowned the works around them. While it runs, the works are the empire's, mended for the empire's homecoming. I would like, for one afternoon, to hear what this fen sounds like when it isn't being kept.

Take a party into the Great Sluice and fell the Sluice Master in the master's chamber. Bring me its gear, the great wheel from its chest. The pumps stop when the master does, and I want to stand on the barge and hear the fen go quiet.
progress: The Sluice Master is in the master's chamber at the heart of the Great Sluice. Fell it and bring me its gear; the pumps stop when it does.
complete: The pumps stopped. Listen. Three hundred years of pumping, every hour of every day since the night they left, and the fen is quiet. I didn't know what it would sound like. It sounds like water that isn't going anywhere.

The works ledger is ours now, and the canal is navigable: not by the Restoration, by us, this afternoon, in our own boats. Chausses from the lock stores, lockplate; they're heavy, but so is everything in the ledger. Thank you. I think I need to sit on the barge for a while.

s_gp_4.name: Barred Gold and Brown

objective.label: Bring Junn 4 field hawk feathers

s_gp_4.desc: Junn, at the Great Granary on the Granary Plains, wants four field hawk feathers from the hawks over the Reaping Line, for the academy's fletchers, who have never seen one.
offer: Junn. Wheat to the horizon, and hawks over it, barred gold and brown, riding the heat off the stubble. Field hawks. The academy's fletchers have never seen one; they fletch with gull and goose, and they've been writing to me since the Reservoir, three letters, asking for anything with a feather on it from inside the border.

I promised them feathers before I'd promised anyone anything about the wheat, which tells you what my priorities were before I started counting towers. I'm counting towers now. There are a great many towers.

Bring me four hawk feathers. The field hawks hunt over the Reaping Line, the long cut where the harvester sentinels work; bring one down and take a tail feather. Four and the fletchers stop writing, and I can count in peace. Sandals for your trouble, from the Western Farm.
progress: Four hawk feathers. The field hawks hunt over the Reaping Line of the Granary Plains, where the harvester sentinels cut. Bring one down and take a feather.
complete: Barred gold, every one. Four. The fletchers will be insufferable for a year, and I will have earned every letter. Thank you.
Sandals, from the Western Farm: Tessaly wove them from the reeds the reapers leave at the field edges, and she says they'll outlast Sabel's good boots, and Sabel has taken that personally.

s_gp_5.name: Husks in the Vault

objective.label: Put 4 vault husks to rest in the granary row

s_gp_5.desc: Morrow wants four vault husks laid to rest in the vaults under the Granary Row on the Granary Plains: what is left of the people who filled the first towers and did not go with the household.
offer: Morrow. Forty towers full and filling; Junn has the count. And under the towers, in the vaults along the Granary Row, husks. Vault husks, the explorers call them. What's left of the people who filled the first towers three hundred years ago and didn't go when the household went. Not living. Not buried. Still carrying grain to a door that doesn't open.

I keep a floor of grudges. This isn't one. Nobody wronged these people that I can write down; they were kept from an appointment, the same appointment the rest of their household kept, and they've been trying to keep it ever since with their arms full of wheat. Heartwood has waited three hundred years on an appointment of its own; I know what the waiting does to people.

Lay four vault husks to rest, in the vaults under the Granary Row. It's a kindness, and the floor doesn't record many of those, so I'll record this one. Trews from the count's camp for your trouble; you'll be in the vaults again. Everything in this province is under something.
progress: Four vault husks, in the vaults under the Granary Row of the Granary Plains. Lay them to rest; they come at you slowly, with their arms still full of grain.
complete: Four. Kept, at last, the only way left to keep them. I've written it on the floor as a kindness done in the empire's granary, and the floor doesn't have many of those; it may be the one line in the book the household will be glad to read when they come home. Here, the trews. They're the count's camp's; Sabel says they're the only dry thing on the plains.

s_gp_6.name: Mill Hounds

objective.label: Put down 4 mill hounds in the Great Granary

s_gp_6.desc: Duelist-Master Sabel wants four mill hounds put down in the mill inside the Great Granary on the Granary Plains, where they guard the flour, so the plains' farmers can take a sack.
offer: Sabel. For three hundred years the harvester sentinels reaped this wheat and let it rot in the rows. Junn has the figures and I've stopped asking for them. This year the granary doors stand open, the towers are filling, and inside the Great Granary the mill is turning. They're not just storing it now. They're milling it. Flour, by the sack, stacked to the rafters.

And the mill hounds guard the flour like it's the crown. Harl went in for one sack and came out at a run, which at his age is a wonder. Four hounds in the mill, and they don't take notices; I checked with the count.

Go into the Great Granary and put down four mill hounds in the mill. Then the plains' farmers can take a sack without losing a hand, and so can you. Keep one. I'd like to know what three-hundred-year-old wheat bakes into, and Tessaly has offered.
progress: Four mill hounds, in the mill inside the Great Granary. Put them down so the farmers can get at the flour.
complete: Four. Tessaly's baking tonight, and Harl has claimed the first loaf, loudly. Keep the sack; look at the stencil on it. Phase five, it says, and phase five is bread. Parks, windows, canals, and now bread: they're provisioning for the morning they arrive, and they've got as far as the kitchen.

I said it at the granary and I'll say it again: a garrison or a homecoming feast, same arithmetic, different tablecloth. Nobody stocks forty towers and turns a mill for a garrison. Somebody is setting a table.

s_bw_4.name: Climbers on the Face

objective.label: Remove 4 rampart geckos from the Border Wall's outer face

s_bw_4.desc: The Herald Sentinel of the Great Watchtower on the Border Wall wants four Rampart Geckos removed from the wall's outer face, since they climb without a charter and the wall reports every one of them.
offer: Good day. You are expected; the wall reported your climb an hour ago. I am the Herald Sentinel of the Great Watchtower. I receive what the wall reports, and the wall reports everything that climbs it, every yard of its hundred miles. You are chartered, so your report was in order.

The rampart geckos are not. They climb the outer face without a charter, in their hundreds, and the wall reports every one of them, and every report comes to me, and I have read gecko reports for three hundred years. I am not authorised to say that I am tired of them. I will say the volume is considerable.

Remove four rampart geckos from the outer face. They cling to the stone below the Rampart Road, west of this tower. The wall will report your climb; it reports everything. This once it will report a climb it approves of. Compensation will be issued from stores.
progress: Four Rampart Geckos still cling to the outer face of the Border Wall, below the Rampart Road west of the Great Watchtower. Remove them; the wall will report it.
complete: Four. Reported, and, for the first time in the register, approved. Four fewer unchartered climbs to read tomorrow. You are expected; you were always expected, and the wall has your climb on file now in any case. Compensation from stores: a runner's rope the wall recovered, and restoratives for the cold. Good day.

s_bw_5.name: Ice That Does Not Melt

objective.label: Bring Duelist-Master Sabel 3 ice crystals from the snowfields

s_bw_5.desc: Duelist-Master Sabel needs three Ice Crystals from the ice slimes and frost wights of the Snowfields on the Border Wall, as a gift for the courts' embassy to the empire; Junn says ice that does not melt is a gift.
offer: The courts have agreed to an embassy: formal letters from all three cities, carried up this wall to whoever, or whatever, commands in the empire's absence. An embassy is a negotiation, and a negotiation brings a gift. Junn says that from the Border Wall the proper gift is ice that does not melt, and she has read more about how the empire did these things than I have. I've stopped arguing with Junn.

The ice slimes and frost wights out on the Snowfields, east along the rampart from the embassy's camp, carry crystals of it: cold that stays cold in your hand. The beacon wisps up in the Great Watchtower carry the same, if you're climbing anyway. Three crystals will do.

Bring them to me here. Then the embassy has its gift, and I have my dignity back, which the fen took along with my boots and the wall may yet return. Sabatons from the embassy's kit for your trouble; you'll be standing beside me when we present ourselves.
progress: I still need three Ice Crystals. The Ice Slimes and Frost Wights carry them on the Snowfields east of the embassy's camp on the Border Wall; the Beacon Wisps in the Great Watchtower carry them too.
complete: Three, and they haven't melted, in my hand, beside the fire, which Junn will be unbearable about for a week. The gift goes in the case with the letters. Sabatons from the embassy's kit; you're honour guard, near enough, and the honour guard should not squelch. Thank you. That's the first thing on this wall that has gone to plan.

s_bw_6.name: The Wall Reported Your Climb

objective.label: Put down 4 watch sentinels in the Great Watchtower

s_bw_6.desc: Junn wants four Watch Sentinels put down in the Great Watchtower so she can read the tower's log of every climb, the only continuous record kept since the night the empire left.
offer: Can I say something absurd? The watch sentinels in the Great Watchtower keep a log. Every climb anyone has made on this wall, written down as it happened, for three hundred years. That makes it the only continuous record of anything since the night the empire left, the Sealing, as Sabel's people call it. Every other record in the world stops that night or starts after it. This one just goes on.

I asked to read it. I asked politely, with the embassy's seal showing. The watch sentinels in the tower said the log is household property and showed me the stair down. They won't let an archivist near the one record in the world that never stopped.

So: four watch sentinels, put down, inside the Great Watchtower. Then I go up and read the log. I know what I'm asking. I'm asking anyway. Slops from the embassy's trunk for it, deepsilk; I brought two pairs and I'm only ever going to wear one.
progress: Four Watch Sentinels still keep the log from me, inside the Great Watchtower on the Border Wall. Put them down and I can go up and read it.
complete: Four. And I read the log. Every climb, in order, for three hundred years. Including this: three envoys from Moonmere, on one date, long before any of us. The academy's own ledger has a gap where that journey should be; I always assumed they never set out. They got here. They climbed this wall, and the wall wrote them down. Slops; I did say two.

s_bl_4.name: What Stayed in the Fire Line

objective.label: Lay 5 ash wights to rest around Emmer's Farm

s_bl_4.desc: Morrow wants five Ash Wights laid to rest around Emmer's Farm inside the fire line of the Burned Land: what remains of people who neither left with the household nor lived, and who circled the farm's one resident for a lifetime.
offer: A farmhouse. Inside the fire line, patched and re-patched, lived in long after the burn. A man named Emmer lived here, on this side of the empire's door, and his grave is out front with fresh ash-flowers on it; a sentinel still tends it.

The ash wights that walk round this farm are what stayed in the fire line. Not the dead; nobody died that night, there was never a body found. They are what's left of people who didn't leave with the household and didn't live either. Neither one thing nor the other, for three hundred years, circling this house.

Lay five of them to rest, round the farm. Emmer kept them company for a lifetime; he had nobody else out here. Let him have the quiet now. There are boots for you from the last camp afterwards. The ash gets into everything.
progress: Five Ash Wights still circle Emmer's Farm, inside the fire line of the Burned Land. Lay them to rest, close to the house, and come back to me.
complete: Five. It's quiet at the farm. That's all I wanted from this one, and I notice I haven't got anything clever to say about it. Boots from the last camp; the ash gets into everything, and these keep it out of that at least. Go on. I'll stand watch here a while.

s_bl_5.name: Drakes at the Gates

objective.label: Clear 4 glass drakes from before the Capital's gates

s_bl_5.desc: Duelist-Master Sabel wants four Glass Drakes cleared off the road before the Capital's gates in the Burned Land, so that when the gates open the courts can walk up to them instead of fighting their way up.
offer: There it is. The capital of Vanai: walls without one scorch mark on them, in the middle of all this ash, and every road we've walked since the inn runs straight to those gates. And on the road in front of them, glass drakes, sunning themselves on the warm stone as if the road's theirs.

It isn't. When those gates open, and they will, I want to walk up to them the way a duelist walks onto the ground: upright, boots clean, blade sheathed. Not fight up to them. I have done enough fighting up to things this year to last me.

Four drakes, off the approach. They lie on the road between the last camp and the Capital's Gates, and in the ash on either side of it. Clear them and the road is ours to the door. Sabatons from the war-chest after; rampart pattern. They'll do for a walk up to a gate.
progress: Four Glass Drakes still lie on the road between the last camp and the Capital's Gates in the Burned Land. Clear them off the approach.
complete: Four drakes, and the road's ours to the gate; I walked it just now, end to end, without drawing. Sabatons from the war-chest, rampart pattern. Wear them when the door opens; I intend to walk up to it in step with you, and I'd like us both properly shod for once.

s_bl_6.name: Sentinels of the Beacon

objective.label: Put down 5 beacon sentinels in the Beacon Fort

s_bl_6.desc: Morrow wants five Beacon Sentinels put down in the Beacon Fort on the Melt Ridge; they still guard the beacon that was lit the night the fire came, and the fort's keeper holds the log of that night.
offer: Weeks. After three hundred years, weeks. That's what the Regent said from its walls: the household's return is weeks off. And up on the Melt Ridge, east of here, the Beacon Fort's sentinels are still guarding a beacon. A signal fire. It was lit the night the empire left, the night this land burned, and they stand round it as if it might be wanted again.

The fort's keeper, the Beacon-Keeper, holds the fort's log, and the log has that night in it. I have walked from Heartwood to this gate carrying a bill three hundred years long, and before I present it I want to read what the empire wrote down the night it set the fire.

First the fort has to be opened. Put down five beacon sentinels inside the Beacon Fort; take a party, it's a fort. The beacon has done its work; it can spare its guard. Then we'll have the keeper to ourselves. Slops from the war-chest after, embersilk, for the ash.
progress: Five Beacon Sentinels still guard the beacon in the Beacon Fort on the Melt Ridge, east of the gates in the Burned Land. Put them down; take a party.
complete: Five. The fort's quieter, and the way up the Beacon Stair is open. The keeper's still at the top in the beacon chamber, with the log, and the log has the last night in it. That's the next thing, and I'll ask it of you when you're rested; come back to me here before the gates. Slops for the ash; embersilk.

s_bl_7.name: The Beacon Log

objective.label: Fell the Beacon-Keeper in the beacon chamber

s_bl_7.desc: Morrow wants the Beacon-Keeper felled in the Beacon Chamber at the top of the Beacon Fort so Heartwood's readers can recover the beacon log; the grudge hall wants the last entry, written the night the fire was lit, word for word.
offer: The Beacon-Keeper lit the beacon on the night. It has never left the chamber since, and the log of that night is in its hand. Our readers have seen the log from the stair: the entries are in the keeper's hand, every one, except the last. The last entry is in a calm hand. The same calm hand that wrote 'Seal it behind us' in the drowned valley's bell tower.

I want to read it before I stand in front of that gate. The grudge hall keeps every page the empire ever wrote about what it did to us, and this page says what they did to this land the night they left. The hall wants it verbatim, in ink, before the household walks back through the door.

The beacon chamber, at the top of the fort, up the Beacon Stair. Take a party; the keeper is bigger than anything else in that fort. Fell it, and report to me. Our readers will go up after you and recover the log. Chausses from the war-chest for it.
progress: The Beacon-Keeper still holds the beacon chamber at the top of the Beacon Fort, on the Melt Ridge in the Burned Land. Fell it with a party and report to me before the gates; Heartwood's readers will recover the log.
complete: The keeper is down; the readers have their way in. Their copy reached me an hour ago, and here is the last entry, in the calm hand: 'The household departs at the appointed hour. Lit at the signal. The fire faced outward, as instructed. The fire is ours.' They lit it themselves. On a signal, on purpose, facing out, at us. Three hundred years, itemised, with interest, and now the last line goes on the floor of the hall. Chausses from the war-chest. Wear them through the gate.

g_pld_10.name: Field Dressing

objective.label: Dig 5 sunroot from the herb patches of the Caerdun Fields for the Paladin Hall

g_pld_10.desc: Shield-Captain Thora Lund of the Paladin Hall will issue the Oathbound set, the hall's first, to a paladin who has taken the garrison's oath and dug five sunroot whole from the herb patches of the Caerdun Fields: the shield line's own wound dressing.
offer: Shield-Captain Thora Lund. I give the Paladin Hall its work; Drillmaster Hal teaches the body, I keep the terms. The hall is the shield line, the part of Caerdun's garrison that stood in the gaps of the wall with a shield and held them, and it takes its recruits the way it always has: oath first, then equipment. The terms set that order, and the terms are older than either of us.

The oath is the garrison's: hold until relieved. Not fight; hold the post until someone comes to take it from you. Marshal Grett, who commands the drill yards, is the one who takes it. If she hasn't had yours yet, go and give it. I'll wait.

Then the first job. The shield line carries its own salve, and the salve is sunroot: a root that grows wild in the Caerdun Fields, out through the Landward Gate, in the herb patches off the farm road. Dig me five roots, whole. A broken root is half a dressing.

Bring the five back here and you'll have earned the Oathbound set, named for the oath you've just taken: helm, hauberk, chausses, sabatons, every piece at once. The line issues in full or not at all; that's precedent.
progress: Five sunroot, dug whole, from the herb patches off the farm road in the Caerdun Fields, out through the Landward Gate. Dig round the root, don't pull it; a broken root is half a dressing, and I count halves as nothing.
complete: Five, and all of them whole. Good. The hall keeps its own roll beside Paymaster Vail's wage book, the city's record of every night of watch since the border shut, and this goes into it the way every job the line does goes in: one day's service, entered against wages owed. The empire never paid its garrison for the watch, so we write down what the watch is worth. You're in the book now.
Helm, hauberk, chausses, sabatons: the Oathbound set, the lot of it. Don't lose the sabatons. There's a precedent for lost sabatons and you won't like it.

g_pld_20a.name: The Road to the Vault

objective.label: Hold the eastern rides of the Hunting Wood against 6 ride wardens

g_pld_20a.desc: To earn the Dawnwatch set, the Paladin Hall's second, Shield-Captain Lund wants the eastern rides of the Hunting Wood held against six ride wardens, the sentinels that have walked that patrol since the Night, before the hall sends you into the Mausoleum.
offer: Dawnwatch is the second set, and the line doesn't issue it to anyone who hasn't stood against something that doesn't tire. Men tire. Wolves tire. What's inside the border doesn't.

You've been through the Border Gate by now, so you've seen them: the sentinels, the empire's caretakers, left behind on the night the border shut and still enforcing the law of a country that isn't here. The ones I want are the ride wardens. They patrol the king's rides in the Hunting Wood, the three straight avenues cut through the wood for a king who never came, and they've walked the eastern rides, by the Gardens Ford, every night for three hundred years without a single relief.

Six ride wardens. Go to the eastern rides of the Hunting Wood, take the ground, and hold it against them until six are down. Don't chase one into the trees; the shield line holds, it doesn't pursue. Then come back to me, because past those rides there's a vault to open, and that is the hard clause.
progress: Six ride wardens on the eastern rides of the Hunting Wood, by the Gardens Ford. Hold the ride and let them come onto the shield; don't chase them into the trees. When six are down, report back to me at the hall.
complete: Six wardens off the ride, and the ride held. Entered: one day's service against wages owed. You've now stood against the thing the garrison was locked out from and never saw, which is more than most of the wall can say.
Now the hard clause. Stay a moment; the next job is in the Mausoleum under the Hunting Wood, and I want to tell you what's waiting in it before you agree to it.

g_pld_20b.name: Hold Until Dawn

objective.label: Bring down the Warden of the Mausoleum in the Hunting Wood's crypts

g_pld_20b.desc: Shield-Captain Lund wants the Warden of the Mausoleum brought down: the sentinel that has kept the door of the emperors' tomb under the Hunting Wood for three hundred years without relief. The Dawnwatch set, in full, is the hall's pay for it.
offer: The Mausoleum is the tomb of the emperors, under the ridge in the north-west of the Hunting Wood; the Mausoleum Door is the way in. At its door stands the Warden of the Mausoleum, a sentinel that has held its post in that tomb since the night the border shut, taking the names of visitors for a list nobody is meant to leave. Marshal Grett wants that list closed. I want it copied.

Here is why the hall cares. A post stood three hundred years without relief is exactly what Caerdun has been doing on the wall, and that Warden is the proof of it in somebody else's hand. Our claim against the empire is that we held, unpaid and unrelieved. The Warden shows the empire knows what that looks like, because it left one of its own doing the same.

Take a party; the oath says hold, it doesn't say hold alone. Go down through the crypts to the Emperors' Vault at the back of the Mausoleum, bring the Warden down, and come back to me. The Dawnwatch set is on my table in full, four pieces. That's the only way the line issues.
progress: The Warden of the Mausoleum, in the Emperors' Vault at the back of the crypts under the Hunting Wood; the Mausoleum Door is north-west, under the ridge. Take a party, pick your ground at the Vault's door, and hold until it falls.
complete: It held that door three hundred years, and you held longer. That is the whole of the shield line's doctrine: stand until the other side stops. Done once, by you, in the empire's own tomb. Logged.

Dawnwatch: helm, hauberk, chausses, sabatons. Entered as one day's service against wages owed. The rate for a day's service is still in dispute between us and an empire that isn't here, but the days are not in dispute. The days are counted.

g_pld_30a.name: Signed, Stamped, Unpaid

objective.label: Take 6 repair orders from the dredge sentinels on the Canal Works' lock line

g_pld_30a.desc: Shield-Captain Lund wants six repair orders taken from the dredge sentinels working the lock line of the Canal Works, to read in the empire's own words what it is still ordering done in a province it left. It is the first clause of the Bastion set, the Paladin Hall's third.
offer: Bastion is the third set. A bastion is the part of a wall that juts out to take the worst of an attack, and the line issues this set off a wall with water on the wrong side of it. The Canal Works, the fen province past the Reservoir where the empire cut its canals, has nothing but ground like that.

This is what I want from it. The dredge sentinels, the caretakers clearing the channels along the lock line east of the Great Sluice, carry repair orders: signed, stamped, dated work orders for the locks. Nobody outside the works has ever been shown one, and the hall needs to read what the empire is ordering done, in its own words, before the courts start arguing about whose fen it is.

Six of those orders. The sentinels carry them post to post along the lock line, so take them off the sentinel, not off the post. Bring them whole; wet is fine, the fen gets into everything. Then come back to the hall and we read them together.
progress: Six repair orders from the dredge sentinels on the lock line of the Canal Works, east of the Great Sluice. They carry the orders post to post; take them off the sentinel, not the post. Wet is fine. Bring them to me at the hall.
complete: Six orders, and I've read them all. Here's one: 'Lock the third, gates to be rehung, navigable by the Restoration.' The Restoration is the sentinels' word for the day their household, the empire's people, comes home. Now look at the date on it: this season. Not the night three hundred years ago. This season.

So the empire is still writing work orders for a house it hasn't come back to, and still not paying anyone to carry them out. That is the garrison's whole grievance, in triplicate, on their own paper. Logged against the claim. Next clause: the pumps those orders depend on.

g_pld_30b.name: The Pump Line

objective.label: Clear 8 pump sentinels from the pump line of the Great Sluice

g_pld_30b.desc: Eight pump sentinels keep the pumps of the Great Sluice running under the Canal Works. Shield-Captain Lund wants them cleared and the pump line held, the second clause of the Bastion set.
offer: 'Navigable by the Restoration' means the pumps. A fen canal only carries boats while something pumps the water out of the locks, and the pumps are in the Great Sluice, the great pump-house out on the Canal Works fen. Something has been running them for three centuries, and it isn't ours.

It's the pump sentinels: caretakers set to keep the wheels turning, and still turning them for a household that hasn't come back. Eight of them inside the Sluice. The Sluice Door is on the Canal Works, by the great sluice gate itself. Clear the eight.

You'll fight in the wet with a wall at your back, which is the only way the shield line fights, so take the ground where the water is behind you and nothing can get round. When the eight are down the pump line is held, and I'll tell you what holding it means.
progress: Eight pump sentinels in the Great Sluice, through the Sluice Door on the Canal Works. Put a wall at your back and let them come to the shield. Report to me at the hall when the pump line is clear.
complete: Eight, and the pump line is clear. Hear the terms, because this is the clause that matters. By precedent, the garrison's and the empire's own, whoever holds a post and keeps it working owns it until relieved. We hold the pump line now. We own it, and the empire can petition for it when it gets home.
Logged as a day's service. One more clause, and it is the thing at the deep end of the Sluice that was running those pumps all along.

g_pld_30c.name: Bastion

objective.label: Bring down the Sluice Master at the deep end of the Great Sluice

g_pld_30c.desc: The Sluice Master, the sentinel that has run the pumps at the deep end of the Great Sluice since the Night, is the last clause of the Bastion set. Shield-Captain Lund wants it brought down and the relief entered in the hall's book.
offer: The Sluice Master. It is the sentinel in the chamber at the deep end of the Great Sluice, and it runs the pumps the way the line holds a gap in the wall: it was put there on the night, told to keep the water moving, and it has never been relieved either. I'd like that on record, in the hall's book, in these words: we relieved it.

Take a party. It poisons; the sump water it works in is foul and it throws it. Carry antidotes and don't be proud about using them. Go down through the Pump Hall to the Sluice Master's Chamber, bring it down, and come back to the hall.
The Bastion set is yours in full for it, four pieces. The line doesn't issue in halves; it never has, and I'm not starting with you.
progress: The Sluice Master, in its chamber at the deep end of the Great Sluice, past the Pump Hall. Take a party and carry antidotes; it poisons. Hold your ground until it stops, then report to me at the hall.
complete: The pumps ran three hundred years, and the thing running them is down. Entered: the Sluice Master, relieved by the shield line of Caerdun. Bastion: helm, hauberk, chausses, sabatons, all four.

Logged as one day's service against wages owed. My father, Bertil Lund, kept the wall as captain before me and keeps the shift tally now at his kitchen table. He says the garrison's count is one hundred and nine thousand shifts and some. He'll tell you the some himself, if you ask; nobody else has it exact.

g_pld_40a.name: The Oil Still Burning

objective.label: Put out 8 oil wisps inside the Beacon Fort

g_pld_40a.desc: Shield-Captain Lund wants eight oil wisps put out inside the Beacon Fort on the Burned Land's melt ridge: the beacon oil that has burned since the signal was lit on the Night, and walks. It is the first clause of the Sunward set, the Paladin Hall's fourth.
offer: The Beacon Fort, on the Burned Land: it stands on the Melt Ridge at the east side of the Burned Land, and the door is off the Burned Land's east road. Hear what it is to us before you go. On the night the border shut, the garrison stood its posts and saw a beacon go up inside the border, and held, because that is what a lit beacon means: hold, the enemy is coming. Nobody has told them to stop since.

The beacon's oil is still burning in that fort, three hundred years on. Not in the lamp; it has got out and it walks, in things the camp calls oil wisps, flames that drift the halls and the court and go for anything that moves. Eight of them. Put them out.

Sunward is the fourth set, and it starts with the lamp that was lit at us. Go in through the Guard Hall; the wisps are quick, so don't chase them, stand still and let them come to the shield. Then back to me.
progress: Eight oil wisps inside the Beacon Fort, off the Burned Land's east road on the melt ridge. They are fast; stand still and let them come onto the shield rather than chasing them. Report to me at the hall after.
complete: Eight. That's the oil accounted for: three hundred years of burning off one night's order, and the shield line put it out. Entered as a day's service.
I want the stair next. The beacon itself sits at the top of the fort, and the stair up to it has been held since the night by the ones who lit it. Come back when you're ready to hear that clause.

g_pld_40b.name: The Beacon Stair

objective.label: Clear 8 beacon sentinels from the stair of the Beacon Fort

g_pld_40b.desc: The beacon sentinels have held the Beacon Fort's stair since the night they lit the signal. Shield-Captain Lund wants eight of them cleared from it, one step at a time, the second clause of the Sunward set.
offer: The beacon sentinels hold the Beacon Stair, the long stair from the Guard Hall up to the beacon chamber at the fort's top. They held it the night the beacon lit, which means they are the ones who carried the fire up and lit the signal that shut us out. The garrison saw that light and held the wall for it. I have a position on that, and the position is this: they owe us the stair.

Eight beacon sentinels on the stair of the Beacon Fort. Clear it the way a line clears a gate: one step, hold, next step. Never two steps at once, never a run; a sentinel above you on a stair has every advantage but patience, and patience is ours.
When eight are down the stair is held, and there is one thing left in that fort, at the top. Come back and I'll tell you about it.
progress: Eight beacon sentinels on the Beacon Stair inside the Beacon Fort, on the Burned Land's melt ridge. Take the stair one step at a time, hold each, and never run it. Report to me at the hall when it's clear.
complete: Eight, and the stair is ours, step by step, which is the only way a stair is ever taken. Entered as a day's service against wages owed.
One more. The one at the top, with the lamp in its hand. Hear me out before you go up to it.

g_pld_40c.name: Sunward

objective.label: Bring down the Beacon-Keeper at the top of the Beacon Fort

g_pld_40c.desc: The Beacon-Keeper has stood at the top of the Beacon Fort since it lit the signal on the Night. Bring it down, and Shield-Captain Lund issues the Sunward set in full: the Paladin Hall's fourth, named for standing in that light.
offer: The Beacon-Keeper. It is the sentinel that keeps the beacon chamber at the top of the fort, and it has stood there three hundred years with the lamp in its hand. It lit that lamp once, on the night, on an order; it has waited since for the order to put it out.
