The set you'll earn is called Sunward, and it is issued for standing in that light, the way the garrison stood in it that night and didn't look away.

Take a party. It blinds: the lamp is in its hand and it turns it on you before it strikes, so bring a healer with patience, because the first minute is fought by ear. Climb the stair you cleared, bring the Keeper down, and come back to the hall.
Bring the beacon log down with you if it's there; a keeper keeps a log. With the Keeper down the beacon is answered for, and the Sunward set is yours in full, four pieces.
progress: The Beacon-Keeper, in the beacon chamber at the top of the Beacon Fort. A party, and watch your eyes: it blinds with the lamp before it strikes. Bring the beacon log down if you find it, and come to me at the hall.
complete: The Keeper is down, and the beacon log you brought back says it in a calm hand, the last entry: 'Lit at the signal. The fire faced outward, as instructed. The fire is ours.' Ours meaning theirs, the empire's. So the signal the garrison held the wall for, the light we took for an enemy coming, was the empire's own, lit to bar its own door behind it.

Understand what that does to the claim. The garrison didn't hold on a misunderstanding. It held on the empire's own order, lit from the empire's own tower, and an order is billable. Noted for the claim, with the log as the exhibit.
Sunward: helm, hauberk, chausses, sabatons. Four pieces, in full. Wear them in that light.

g_pld_50a.name: The Night Before the Gates

objective.label: Hold the camp's light before the Capital's gates against 10 ash beasts

g_pld_50a.desc: The Paladin Hall's last set, Everwatch, begins at the courts' Last Camp before the Capital's gates, where Shield-Captain Lund wants the camp's fire held through the night against ten ash beasts.
offer: Everwatch. The last set, and the line issues it for the one thing the shield line was raised to do: stand before the gates. Not Caerdun's gates; the empire's. The courts have their Last Camp on the Burned Land in sight of the Capital's walls, Duelist-Master Sabel's camp, with every banner in the world marching to join it, and every night the ash beasts come out of the dark at its fires.

Ten ash beasts, in the ash before the Capital's gates. Go to the camp, take the watch, and hold the camp's light: stay between the fire and the dark, and let them come at the shield rather than at the tents behind you. Ten down is the night held.
You've held tombs and sluices and stairs for this hall. This is the door the oath was sworn to, three hundred years ago, by people who never got to stand at it. Stand at it for them.
progress: Ten ash beasts on the Burned Land, in the ash before the Capital's gates at the courts' Last Camp. Stand between the fires and the dark and hold the light until ten are down. Then back to me at the hall.
complete: Ten. The camp held its first full night with a shield in front of it, and the watch there is the shield line's by precedent now, whoever stands it after you. Entered as a day's service against wages owed.

Next is the Glassed Stag. There's one thing on that burned ground that held through the fire itself, and before the last clause I want it off the road to the gates. Speak to me again here at the hall and I'll give you the terms.

g_pld_50b.name: What the Fire Left Standing

objective.label: Bring down the Glassed Stag on the Burned Land

g_pld_50b.desc: The Glassed Stag, caught by the fire that made the Burned Land and still walking its glassed orchard, is in the way of the road to the Capital's gates. Shield-Captain Lund wants it brought down before the Paladin Hall's last clause.
offer: The Glassed Stag. You've seen the fire line: on the night, one flash went out from the Capital, everything inside it burned outward, and the line is the ring where it stopped. The flash caught a stag mid-stride in the orchard west along that line and glassed it where it was, facing away from the city, and it kept walking. Three hundred years later it still walks that orchard, and it goes for the survey teams. My reading, and it is the shield line's reading: the fire went through it and it held. It's the one thing out there that did.
I respect that. I also want it off the road to the gates, because the last clause of this set is on that road and I won't have a paladin of this hall fighting two things at once.

Take a party. It's fast, faster than anything you've held against; pick your ground in the orchard, put the glass trunks at your back, and make it come to you. Bring it down and we're one clause from the end.
progress: The Glassed Stag, in the glassed orchard west along the fire line of the Burned Land. Take a party, pick your ground among the glass trunks, and make it come to you. Report to me at the hall when it's down.
complete: Down. The Stag held through the fire and you held through the Stag; the hall will cite that as precedent for a long time. Entered as a day's service against wages owed.
One clause left, and it's the one my father has been waiting on his whole life, at his kitchen table with the tally. Hear it from me before you go.

g_pld_50c.name: Everwatch

objective.label: Relieve the Gate-Marshal standing before the Capital's gates on the Burned Land

g_pld_50c.desc: The Gate-Marshal has kept the watch before the Capital's gates since the Night, and no one of its own line is left to relieve it. Shield-Captain Lund sends you to relieve it in the shield line's way, for the Everwatch set and a line in the hall's book.
offer: There is a gate-marshal before the Capital's gates: a sentinel in marshal's plate, at the foot of the city's south wall, west of the gates. It stood the gate watch on the night. The household, the empire's people, walked in and barred the doors behind it, and nobody relieved it. It has stood that watch every night since, exactly as long as Caerdun has stood ours.

The Regent, the empire's last servant, who keeps the city with the keys, has let explorers in as an audit of its keeping; you'll know that by now. That doesn't relieve the Gate-Marshal. A marshal takes its relief from its own line, from the next marshal, not from a keeper of keys, and there is nobody left in its line to give it. So it stands.

That is the last clause. Hold until relieved, and relieve the one post in the empire that has stood as long as ours. Take a party to the south wall, offer the Gate-Marshal the relief, and when it answers, bring it down. Then come back to the hall. Everwatch is on the table in full, and so is a line in the book nobody has written in three hundred years.
progress: The Gate-Marshal, at the foot of the Capital's south wall, west of the gates on the Burned Land. It won't draw first; walk up and offer it the relief, and it will answer. A party, and the whole of the doctrine: hold until it falls.
complete: Relieved. Both of you: the Marshal of a watch nobody came to take, and Caerdun of the post it swore to and was shut out of. That's the line nobody has written in three hundred years, and I've written it in the hall's book: the shield line's post before the gates, held by one of ours, three hundred years late and on time.

Everwatch: helm, hauberk, chausses, sabatons. The title, Who Held Until Relieved, is the line's to give and I give it. My father will want the day count from you himself, every shift of it; he's at the kitchen table, and he's kept a chair.

g_pld_34.name: Rampart Drill

objective.label: Clear 8 rampart sentinels from the Rampart Road for the Paladin Hall's courier

g_pld_34.desc: At the embassy's camp on the Border Wall, Duelist-Master Sabel holds a Bastion Waymark helm sent up by the Paladin Hall for the paladin who clears eight rampart sentinels from the Rampart Road.
offer: Paladin. The embassy walks the Rampart Road every night, the road along the top of the Border Wall, and the rampart sentinels, the wall's own patrol, walk it back at us: east of the Great Watchtower toward the East Stair, and up inside the tower by its Signal Room. Neither side has yielded a yard, which is tidy as a duel and useless as a road.

Shield-Captain Lund's hall sent a helm up with the courier, a Bastion Waymark: the hall's Bastion pattern with the little road-sign the hall cuts into kit it sends out of the city, for whichever paladin clears the road. Eight rampart sentinels off the Rampart Road and it's yours.
Honour guard work. Try not to enjoy it; the sentinels will think you're being rude.
progress: Eight rampart sentinels on the Rampart Road of the Border Wall: they walk the wall-top east of the Great Watchtower toward the East Stair, and a few keep the tower itself. The Bastion Waymark helm stays in the embassy's baggage until they're down; come back to me at the camp.
complete: Eight, and the road is walkable for one night at least. Here is the Bastion Waymark helm, by courier from the Paladin Hall, and here is a chit to sign for it. Lund counts everything, down to the helms, and enters them against the empire's account. Sign it, legibly; she reads every chit, and I'd like your name spelt right.

g_pld_37.name: Before the Gates

objective.label: Clear 8 scorch sentinels from the roads before the Capital's gates

g_pld_37.desc: At the courts' Last Camp before the Capital's gates, Duelist-Master Sabel holds a pair of Bastion Waymark sabatons from the Paladin Hall for the paladin who clears eight scorch sentinels from the roads before the gates.
offer: Scorch sentinels walk the roads to the Capital's gates: the caretakers that walked the fire line on the night, and have kept to the burned roads since. They've taken the camp's fires for a signal, and they come down the roads to answer it every evening, which is a nuisance when you're trying to hold a camp in sight of the walls.

Eight of them off the roads before the gates, Paladin, and you can have the sabatons the Paladin Hall sent out with the quartermaster: Bastion Waymark, the hall's pattern with its road-sign cut into it. Lund's idea of a care package. There's a chit.
progress: Eight scorch sentinels on the roads before the Capital's gates, on the Burned Land around the Last Camp. Come back to me at the camp when they're off the road; the sabatons wait in the quartermaster's store.
complete: Eight. The Bastion Waymark sabatons; sign the chit, Lund will want it back by the next courier. She says to tell you the count is one hundred and nine thousand shifts and some: the garrison's unrelieved shifts since the night, which every recruit in Caerdun hears before breakfast. The and-some is her father Bertil's; he keeps it at his kitchen table, and he'll want you to ask him for it.

g_sam_10.name: Reed for the Reedblade

objective.label: Cut 6 mere reed from the reed beds of the Caerdun Fields for the Samurai hall

g_sam_10.desc: Code-Master Eskil Rudd of the Duelling Code, Caerdun's samurai hall, will issue the Reedblade set, the hall's first coat, to a samurai who cuts six lengths of mere reed from the reed beds of the Caerdun Fields and carries them in.
offer: Code-Master Eskil Rudd. This is the Duelling Code, the samurai hall south of the parade square, and I keep the code it's named for: three pages. A duel is a contract with a witness. You may refuse any duel but the second: when someone asks you to stand at their side as their second, you stand. The challenge goes to the chair. Everything else is commentary, and Duelist-Master Sabel keeps the commentary.

The hall's first coat is reed woven over mail. Not a metaphor; the coat is made of it. The reed takes the edge off a cut that the mail would have turned into a bruise, and reed is cheap, which is the point of being new: you will be cut, and the coat should cost less than you do.

There are two reed beds in the Caerdun Fields, out through the Landward Gate, down by the water. Cut me six good lengths of mere reed, the tall reed that grows standing in the shallows. Cut them yourself; the hall does not issue a coat on reed it did not watch you carry in.
progress: Six lengths of mere reed, from the two reed beds down by the water in the Caerdun Fields. Cut, not bought; nobody sells it anyway. Carry them back to me at the Duelling Code.
complete: Six. Dry, straight, and nobody else's. Lotta, my cousin, will weave them over the mail tonight; she grinds the hall's blades and weaves its coats, and she does not hurry either.
The Reedblade set, then: headguard, coat, legguards, boots. Wear it until it splits. It will. When it does, you will have learned where you let things through, which is the whole of the first lesson.

g_sam_20a.name: The Hounds Before Their Master

objective.label: Kill 8 king's hounds on the rides of the Hunting Wood

g_sam_20a.desc: Code-Master Rudd sends you through the Border Gate into the Hunting Wood to put down eight king's hounds on the rides, so that the sentinel that masters them takes notice before you challenge it.
offer: The second work. Now that the Border Gate is open to you, go through it into the Hunting Wood, the empire's hunting ground on Caerdun's doorstep. The king's hounds still run the rides there, the three straight avenues cut through the wood: hounds loosed three hundred years ago and never whistled in, because the one thing that can whistle them in never has.

That one thing is the Master of Hounds, a sentinel, one of the empire's caretakers, built to answer. I mean to put you in front of it, but the code is particular about how. You do not challenge a master through his dogs; that is cowardice. You also do not let the dogs set the terms; that is stupidity. So the dogs come first, on your terms.
Eight king's hounds, on the rides of the Hunting Wood. Put them down. After that the one who holds their leash will have noticed you, which is what we want. Come back and tell me.
progress: Eight king's hounds, on the rides of the Hunting Wood, through Caerdun's Border Gate. Fight each on your own ground; don't be drawn into the trees after them. Come back to the Duelling Code when eight are down.
complete: Eight. The rides will have reported it by now; everything inside that border reports to something. The Master of Hounds knows your name, or whatever a thing like that keeps instead of names, and it will be waiting at the far end of the rides. That is the challenge half-made. The other half is yours to make in person, and I'll tell you how.

g_sam_20b.name: Stillwater

objective.label: Challenge and kill the Master of Hounds at the far end of the Hunting Wood's rides

g_sam_20b.desc: The Master of Hounds, the huntsman sentinel at the far end of the Hunting Wood's rides, answers a challenge. Code-Master Rudd wants you to make it, and not to move first. The Stillwater set is the hall's second.
offer: The Master of Hounds. Of everything in the king's rides it is the one huntsman that answers a challenge, because answering is what it was built for: a king's hunt wanted something to meet a stag's charge and a poacher's steel alike. Know this before you go: it will not wait for your second, and it will not stop at first blood. The code's courtesies don't bind it. Yours still bind you.

Stillwater is the set you'll earn, and it is the hall's word for what Duelist-Master Sabel preaches in the yard: the water does not move until you move it. The thing that moves first shows its line; the thing that waits reads it.
Go to the far end of the rides in the Hunting Wood, stand in front of the Master of Hounds, and do not move first. Let it commit. Then move. Come back standing.
progress: The Master of Hounds, at the far end of the rides in the Hunting Wood. Stand in front of it and don't move first; let it commit, then cut. It won't stop at first blood, so neither should you. Report to me at the Duelling Code.
complete: It's down and you're standing, and nobody has told me about any running, and in this city somebody always tells me. The challenge was made properly and answered properly; that is a duel, and the first one the hall will enter against your name.

The Stillwater set: headguard, coat, legguards, boots. The coat is cut for standing still in; it sits heavy at the shoulders and you'll feel every time you shift your weight without meaning to. That's the point. You'll find that out.

g_sam_30a.name: A Polished Mirror

objective.label: Bring Code-Master Rudd 5 wasp glass from the glass wasps of the Glassworks

g_sam_30a.desc: Code-Master Rudd wants five pieces of wasp glass from the glass wasps of the Glassworks, to polish into the mirror a samurai trains against. It is the first step toward the Windborne set, the hall's third.
offer: The third work begins in the Glassworks: the province between the Timber Estates and the Burned Land, where the empire's furnaces turned a desert to glass, and still run. The glass wasps there, on the slag flats west of the Furnace Row, carry glass inside them, grown in the body the way a bee grows wax. That is a sentence I'd have doubted before the Race, the courts' scramble for the interior, started sending crates of such things home.
I want five pieces of wasp glass. Take them off the wasps; nothing else there yields it. Bring them back to the hall.

Here is why. The hall polishes a mirror out of wasp glass, and the mirror work is the hardest stage of the code's training, because it is a duel against the only opponent who knows exactly what you will do. You cannot surprise yourself. You can only stop flinching.
progress: Five wasp glass, from the glass wasps on the slag flats of the Glassworks, west of the Furnace Row. Bring them to me at the Duelling Code; Lotta will do the polishing.
complete: Five. Good glass, no cracks; they'll polish. Lotta will have the mirror flat and silvered within the week.
You'll see yourself in it before this work is over, and then you'll understand why nobody enjoys this stage, and why nobody who finished it would skip it. Come back for the next step while she works.

g_sam_30b.name: Windborne

objective.label: Kill 8 glasswing drakes over the Glassworks

g_sam_30b.desc: Eight glasswing drakes hunt the air over the Glassworks past the furnace row. Code-Master Rudd wants them cut down, to learn the Windborne set's lesson: cut what you cannot plant your feet against.
offer: Glasswing drakes, over the Glassworks past the furnace row: drakes with wings gone to glass from the furnace heat, and they hunt the hot air rising off the melt. They come off the wind, not the ground, which the code did not anticipate, having been written by people who fought other people, on floors.

Eight of them. You can't root your stance against a thing that strikes from above and is gone, so you'll learn to cut what you can't plant your feet against: read the dive, move as it commits, cut on the way through. That is the Windborne set's whole argument, and it's the set you're working for.
Go past the furnace row to the south flats, east of the Kiln Watch, let them find you on open ground, and bring down eight. Then back to the hall.
progress: Eight glasswing drakes, over the Glassworks past the furnace row, on the south flats east of the Kiln Watch. Stand in the open, let them dive, and cut as they commit; don't chase them into the air with your eyes. Report to me at the Duelling Code.
complete: Eight, off the wind, and you've still got both eyes, which is the usual price of learning that lesson the slow way. Good.
The mirror is polished. Lotta finished it this morning, and you'll stand in front of it in the yard before you leave. One thing left in the Glassworks, and it's the thing the mirror was for.

g_sam_30c.name: The Mirror

objective.label: Challenge and kill the Mirror Stag at the east end of the Glassworks

g_sam_30c.desc: The Mirror Stag at the east end of the Glassworks wears glass over its hide, and shows a duelist their own stroke the moment before they commit. Challenge it and bring it down for the Windborne set, the hall's third.
offer: The Mirror Stag. It stands at the east end of the Glassworks, past the furnaces and beyond the Mirror Flat, below the Wall Stair. The furnace heat has laid glass over its hide, so clear that when you stand before it you see yourself in it: your own guard, your own stroke, the moment before you commit. Most people flinch at that. The stag does not. It has had three hundred years of its own reflection.
This is why you polished a mirror. Everything you did in front of the glass at the hall, you do once more in front of a thing that will kill you if you hesitate.

By the code the challenge is yours to make and yours to withdraw; I remind you of the right so you know you're not using it. Nobody withdraws from this one. Go to the east end of the Glassworks, make the challenge, and bring it down.
progress: The Mirror Stag, at the east end of the Glassworks past the furnaces, beyond the Mirror Flat below the Wall Stair. Make the challenge, watch your own stroke in its hide, and don't flinch. Report to me at the Duelling Code when it's down.
complete: It's down. Did you flinch? Don't tell me. It's down and you're here, and that is the only answer the code accepts.
The Windborne set: headguard, coat, legguards, boots. Lighter than the Stillwater by a third, because you're done standing still; the next work moves. Wear it on the wall. You'll be on the wall.

g_sam_40a.name: The Storm Side

objective.label: Kill the Wall Drake on the storm side of the Border Wall's rampart road

g_sam_40a.desc: Code-Master Rudd names three duels a samurai cannot refuse. The first is the Wall Drake, which holds the storm side of the Rampart Road toward the far end of the Border Wall.
offer: The fourth work. The code lets you refuse any duel but the second, when you stand for someone else. The hall's fourth work is three duels you can't refuse, not because the code forbids it but because the things in question won't take no for an answer, and the first is on the Border Wall, the hundred-mile wall that closed the gaps the mountains left in the border.

The Wall Drake keeps the storm side of the Rampart Road, the weather side of the wall-top, toward its far end, east of the Great Watchtower near the East Stair. It nests in the wall itself and comes up through the parapet. It has held that ground exactly as long as Caerdun has held its wage claim, three hundred years, with less paperwork.

Get up onto the wall, walk the Rampart Road east past the Great Watchtower toward the East Stair on the storm side, and when the drake comes up, take it. The set at the end of this is called Stormguard; you'll see why.
progress: The Wall Drake, on the storm side of the Rampart Road toward the far end of the Border Wall, east of the Great Watchtower near the East Stair. Walk the weather side until it comes up through the parapet. Report to me at the Duelling Code when it's down.
complete: Down. The wall will have reported it before you were off the stair; the embassy says that wall reports everything, down to the weather. Let it report that. The first of three, and the only one of the three that will have fought you honestly. Two more.

g_sam_40b.name: They Do Not Duel

objective.label: Kill 6 ash giants in the Burned Land, on the west road into the last camp

g_sam_40b.desc: Six ash giants walk the west road into the courts' Last Camp on the Burned Land. They answer no challenge, so Code-Master Rudd sends you to cut them down without one: the second duel a samurai cannot refuse.
offer: The second of the three. Ash giants, in the Burned Land, on the west road into the Last Camp, the courts' camp before the Capital's gates. Grey as the ash and taller than the palisade, and they walk that road into the camp's fires every night.

They do not duel. They don't answer a challenge, they don't salute, they don't stop at first blood or at any blood; they come on until they are down or you are. I'm telling you so you don't waste a bow on one. A duelist who bows to a thing that cannot bow back has given it a free stroke.

Six. The code has nothing to say about giants; its three pages were written for people. So this one is between you and your arm, with no contract and no witness, and the hall will accept your word on it.
progress: Six ash giants, in the Burned Land on the west road into the Last Camp before the Capital's gates. No bow, no challenge; cut and keep cutting. Report to me at the Duelling Code when six are down.
complete: Six, and no witnesses, which breaks the first page of the code; a duel is a contract with a witness. The hall will overlook it on this one occasion, since the other party was not party to anything. The last of the three is next, and it is the one the set is named for.

g_sam_40c.name: Stormguard

objective.label: Kill the Glassed Stag in the glassed orchard of the Burned Land

g_sam_40c.desc: The Glassed Stag has kept the glassed orchard of the Burned Land since the flash of the Night turned it to glass where it stood. It is the third duel a samurai cannot refuse, and the Stormguard set is named for it.
offer: The third, and the one the set is named for. The Glassed Stag. On the night of the Sealing, when the border shut, one flash went out from the capital and burned the land round it outward; the fire line is where it stopped. A stag was in the orchard west of the Gardens road when the flash came, and it glassed the stag where it stood, mid-stride, facing away from the city. It has been in that orchard ever since, and it goes for anyone who walks the rows.

Here is my reading of it, and the hall's. The stag was caught in the worst storm this continent has seen and it did not go down. It stands in the storm and keeps its feet. That is the whole of what Stormguard means, and the hall names the set for the thing that did it.
Go to the glassed orchard of the Burned Land, west of the Gardens road. Challenge it; it will answer, as it answers everything that comes into the rows. Take Stormguard from the one that earned it.
progress: The Glassed Stag, in the glassed orchard of the Burned Land, west of the Gardens road. It comes at anything in the rows; take your footing on the glass before it does. Report to me at the Duelling Code when it's down.
complete: It's down. Three hundred years standing in the storm, and you walked up to it and ended it. The hall will enter that against your name in the words the code uses for a duel fought to the end: answered, and finished.

The Stormguard set: headguard, coat, legguards, boots. Lotta has worked glass from the Glassworks into the plates. Nothing on the wall or the fire line will cut it. Plenty beyond the fire line will try, and the last work is beyond it.

g_sam_50a.name: The Guard That Would Not Step Aside

objective.label: Kill 8 beacon sentinels on the upper floors of the Beacon Fort

g_sam_50a.desc: For the Duelling Code's last work, Code-Master Rudd says a challenge to the empire's empty chair passes to whatever stands before the Capital's gates, so you fight inward along that line, starting with eight beacon sentinels on the upper floors of the Beacon Fort.
offer: The last work. Read the third page of the code: the challenge goes to the chair. That means when you have a quarrel with a house, you challenge its master, whoever sits in its chair. Our quarrel is with the empire, and the empire's chair is behind the Capital's gates, and the gates don't answer a challenge. So by the code it passes down the line to whoever stands in front of them, from the outermost post inward.

The line starts at the Beacon Fort, on the Melt Ridge at the east side of the Burned Land, the tower whose beacon was lit on the night. The beacon sentinels on the fort's upper floors were set there to keep that beacon lit, and they never got the order to stop. Eight of them.
They won't step aside, so don't ask them to; a request they can't obey only wastes the breath you'll want. Go up through the Guard Hall to the upper floors, put down eight, and come back to me.
progress: Eight beacon sentinels, on the upper floors of the Beacon Fort, off the Burned Land's east road on the melt ridge. Don't ask them to step aside; they can't. Report to me at the Duelling Code when eight are down.
complete: Eight. Three hundred years at a post, keeping a fire lit for people who never looked back at it, and nobody to relieve them. I'd have liked to relieve them; the code has no form for it, so the sword had to do. Next: the one at the top, and it is different from the eight.

g_sam_50b.name: The Keeper's Answer

objective.label: Challenge and kill the Beacon-Keeper at the top of the Beacon Fort

g_sam_50b.desc: The Beacon-Keeper at the top of the Beacon Fort holds the beacon's lamp and its log, and it answers a challenge. Code-Master Rudd wants it challenged and brought down: the next post in the line to the Capital's gates.
offer: The Beacon-Keeper. It keeps the beacon chamber at the top of the fort, up the Beacon Stair past the floors you've cleared, holding the log of the beacon and the lamp that lit it on the night. Everything you've met on this road so far simply did its post. The Keeper is the first one that will actually answer a challenge; it was made to answer whoever comes up the stair to it, and it still does.

It blinds before it strikes: the lamp goes into your eyes and the stroke follows while you're still seeing white. Sabel's commentary has a chapter on fighting what you can't see. It is a short chapter: close the distance before the light, and read the stroke from the sound of its feet.
Climb the stair, stand before the Keeper, and make the challenge in the form, aloud. Then finish it and come back to the hall.
progress: The Beacon-Keeper, in the beacon chamber at the top of the Beacon Fort. Make the challenge aloud; it answers. Close the distance before the lamp comes up, and listen for its feet when it blinds you. Report to me at the Duelling Code.
complete: Answered, and down. Mark the difference: the eight on the floors below were posts; the Keeper was a duel, challenged and answered in the form, and the hall enters it as one.

Now there is nothing between you and the Capital's gates but the one thing the Regent, the keeper of the city, left standing in front of them. I have been waiting a long time to send someone to it. Come back when you've slept.

g_sam_50c.name: Horizon

objective.label: Challenge and kill the Gate-Marshal on the road before the Capital's gates

g_sam_50c.desc: The Gate-Marshal, the Regent's doorman, has stood on the road before the Capital's gates since the Night and has never drawn first. Challenge it, for the Horizon set, the hall's last, and the title Who Was Answered.
offer: The Gate-Marshal. It is the Regent's doorman: a sentinel in marshal's plate that has stood on the road before the Capital's gates since the night of the Sealing, at the foot of the south wall, west of the gates. It let the embassy past, and it let our camp past, because in three hundred years nobody has drawn on it. It has never drawn first. It has never needed to; everything that came up that road came to knock, not to challenge.

Here is the whole code in one line, and the line this hall has waited three centuries to say in earnest. The challenge goes to the chair. The chair is empty. So it passes to the one who stands before it, and the one who stands before the empire's chair is the Gate-Marshal.
Walk up the road before the gates. Draw. It will answer; that is what a doorman is for. The set for it is called Horizon, and you'll understand the name when you've come back from it.
progress: The Gate-Marshal, on the road before the Capital's gates, at the foot of the south wall west of the gates on the Burned Land. Walk up and draw; it will answer. Report to me at the Duelling Code when it's finished.
complete: It answered, and it's down, and for the first time in three hundred years nobody is standing on the road to the gates. The challenge went to the chair, the chair was empty, and the one before it has been answered. The hall enters it so, and gives you the title that goes with it: Who Was Answered.
The Horizon set: headguard, coat, legguards, boots. There is nothing past it; no further work, no further set, no post beyond that road. That is the point of the name.
One more thing, and it isn't the hall's. Duelist-Master Sabel will want to hear this from you, not from me. Go to her at the camp before the gates and tell her she was right about the composure.

g_sam_34.name: The Cat That Does Not Announce Itself

objective.label: Kill 6 snow cats in the drifts along the Border Wall's Rampart Road, west of the Great Watchtower

g_sam_34.desc: At the embassy's camp on the Border Wall, Duelist-Master Sabel holds a Windborne Waymark headguard from the samurai hall for the samurai who kills six snow cats in the drifts along the Rampart Road and stops them eating the honour guard.
offer: Samurai. Snow cats, in the drifts on the Border Wall: along the Rampart Road west of the Great Watchtower, where the embassy's honour guard walks picket. The cats come up over the parapet out of the snow without a sound and take a sentry before he's turned round. They don't announce themselves, which the code considers bad form and the cats consider breakfast.

Six of them. The embassy's kit came up the wall with a Windborne headguard in it, with the hall's waymark on it, the little road-sign the Duelling Code cuts into kit it sends out of the city, so it finds its way to one of its own. It's yours when the cats stop eating the honour guard.
progress: Six snow cats on the Border Wall, in the drifts along the Rampart Road west of the Great Watchtower. Watch the drifts at the parapet; they come over without a sound. Come back to me at the embassy's camp.
complete: Six, and the picket slept last night, which it hasn't since we climbed the stair. The headguard, waymark and all; Rudd's hall sends its regards and no chit, which is how you tell the two halls apart. Wear it. The wall is cold, and the cats were not the last thing on it.

g_sam_37.name: The Ash Stalker

objective.label: Kill 8 ash stalkers on the ash road in from the King's Gardens

g_sam_37.desc: At the courts' Last Camp on the Burned Land, Duelist-Master Sabel holds a pair of Windborne Waymark boots from the samurai hall for the samurai who kills eight ash stalkers on the Ash Road in from the King's Gardens.
offer: Ash stalkers on the Ash Road, the road in from the King's Gardens, where it swings down the west side of the Burned Land between the Glassed Orchard and the Scar, the stretch the supply carts take down to the camp. Grey things the colour of the ground, and they hunt the carts at dusk: they take the lamps off the carts first, so the carters are blind, and then they take the carters. Nobody has seen one coming yet. Several have seen one leaving.

Eight of them off that road, Samurai. The courts' war-chest, opened for the Capital, has in it a pair of Windborne boots with the Duelling Code's waymark cut into them, sent out of the city for one of the hall's own. Quiet soles. You'll see the point of that on the ash.
progress: Eight ash stalkers on the Ash Road in from the King's Gardens, on its west stretch in the Burned Land, between the Glassed Orchard and the Scar. Hunt them at dusk when they come for the carts, and listen before you look. Come back to me at the camp.
complete: Eight, and you heard them first for once; the carters say the lamps stayed on the carts all night, and the camp ate. The boots, waymark and all; Rudd's hall sends them with its regards. Walk quietly to the gates when the time comes. It's the only way anything has ever walked up to them.

g_drk_10.name: Tusk for the Tally

objective.label: Bring Reckoner Thorn 4 Boar Tusks, uncut, from the bramble boars and young boars of the Heartwood Fields

g_drk_10.desc: Reckoner Thorn of the Grudge Hall will take on a new dark knight who brings four uncut boar tusks from the Heartwood Fields: one to notch for each of the four old grudges a recruit inherits.
offer: So you want the job. Dark knight, the courts call it; in this hall it is grudge-keeper, same as Morrow. I am Hale Thorn, the hall's reckoner. Morrow keeps the floor, the record of every grove and every family the empire took from Heartwood. I keep the dates. Every grudge on that floor has a date against it, and a date is an appointment, and a dark knight is the one who keeps it.

Here is how the book works. Every grudge is notched on a boar's tusk, one notch for every ten years it has gone unpaid, and the tusk is filed beside the page. A recruit brings their own blanks, because you inherit four grudges the day you sign, and none of them is small.

Four boar tusks, uncut: let nobody trim or polish them, the notches go on clean ivory. The boars are in the Heartwood Fields, out through the West Gate. The bramble boars in the far west of the Fields carry the best tusks; the young boars in the north will do. Bring me four and I will read you your four, and the hall will pay for your plate: a full set, head to feet, or nothing.
progress: I still need four boar tusks, uncut. The bramble boars in the far west of the Heartwood Fields carry the best; the young boars in the north of the Fields will do. Bring them to me here at the Grudge Hall.
complete: Four, and uncut. I notch them now, while you watch; that is how it is done. The first: the Hollin grove, felled for the Timber Estates, three hundred and one years unpaid. The second: the Reeds' mill, taken the same year. The third: the Ash Lane burying ground, the same. The fourth is this hall's own door, which an imperial clerk once tried to tax; that one is older still.

Those four are yours now, and so is the plate for keeping them. Ashen Vow, the set is called, after the oath you just took by standing still while I notched. Visor, hauberk, chausses, sabatons. Wear it in. The appointments do not keep themselves, and the hall will have more for you once you have grown into it.

g_drk_20a.name: The Tally

objective.label: Break 8 tally sentinels in the Overseer's Lodge

g_drk_20a.desc: Reckoner Thorn wants eight tally sentinels broken inside the Overseer's Lodge, the Timber Estates' office that still counts Heartwood's felled groves as timber stock.
offer: The second set is called Iron Dusk, and before you earn it you should know why. It is named for the year the Estates came: the year the empire felled Heartwood's groves to plant its Timber Estates, and the smoke off the felling turned every evening the colour of a blade. We call it the Felling. Every grudge on this floor that is not older begins there.

Now the Border Gate is open you can walk onto the Estates yourself: west through the Heartwood Fields, through the gate, and you are standing in our groves, replanted in ruler-straight rows. East among those rows is the Overseer's Lodge, the Estates' own office, entered by the Overseer's Door. It keeps the count of every tree they took, and the tally sentinels inside, the empire's clerks in iron, are still adding to it.

They counted our groves as stock. Trees with names, with families living under them, entered as so many board-feet. Go into the Lodge and break eight tally sentinels. The book has a column for that, and I will fill it when you come back.
progress: Eight tally sentinels, inside the Overseer's Lodge: the Estates' office, east among the ranks of the Timber Estates, through the Overseer's Door. Break them and come back to me at the Grudge Hall.
complete: Eight. I have written it: the count of the Timber Estates is short eight counters, and the Lodge may make do. That is the clerks dealt with. Which leaves the one who signed the count, and that is a longer appointment than any clerk's. Stay a moment; I have the page open.

g_drk_20b.name: The Oldest Appointment

objective.label: Defeat the Overseer at the back of the Overseer's Lodge

g_drk_20b.desc: Reckoner Thorn wants the Overseer, who ran the Timber Estates and whose date has stood three hundred years unkept, defeated at the back of the Overseer's Lodge.
offer: The Overseer ran the Timber Estates. It gave the order for every tree in the count you just shortened, and it is still in the Lodge, at the very back, past the rota hall where the shift roster has marked every shift absent for three hundred years. Its date has stood on this floor three hundred years unkept: the oldest appointment in the book.

Nobody has kept it because the Lodge is full of sentinels and the Overseer is behind all of them. You have already broken eight. Go back in, go past the rota hall to the back of the Lodge, and defeat the Overseer. Take company if you want it; it has run that place alone for three centuries and will not be moved easily.
You are the appointment. Bring me nothing back; I will know when it is kept, because the date has been waiting for a hand to draw a line through it, and mine is ready.
progress: The Overseer, at the back of the Overseer's Lodge in the Timber Estates, past the rota hall. Defeat it and come back to the Grudge Hall; you need bring nothing with you.
complete: Kept. Three hundred years on the page, one line through it, and I draw the line myself; that is the reckoner's privilege. Morrow will want to see the page before the ink dries. Let her.

Iron Dusk, all four pieces: visor, hauberk, chausses, sabatons. The hall paid for them out of the Estates' own writ of compensation, the empire's paper promising Heartwood payment for its groves, 'Restitution upon Return'. We have charged your plate against the promise. That is the kind of joke we allow ourselves.

g_drk_30a.name: Pike-Point

objective.label: Break 8 pruning sentinels in the King's Gardens

g_drk_30a.desc: Reckoner Thorn wants eight pruning sentinels broken in the parterres of the King's Gardens: the same sentinels that once carried the pikes that moved Heartwood's families off the land.
offer: The third set, and the third chapter. It starts where Morrow's line starts, and you will have heard her say it on the floor: every family the empire wanted off its land was moved at pike-point to make room for the King's Gardens. Whole lanes of Heartwood, walked off their ground between two rows of pikes so an emperor could have parterres. Our houses stood where its Cleared Row is now.

The pruning sentinels carried those pikes. They prune now: the same arms, the same motion, a shear where the blade was. They work the four parterres round the fountain court of the King's Gardens, the empire's pleasure grounds beyond the Timber Estates, up the Gardens Road. You will hear the shears before you see them.
Break eight pruning sentinels. The book has the name of every family that walked between those pikes. It is about to have the pikes' names too, in the same column.
progress: Eight pruning sentinels, in the four parterres round the fountain court of the King's Gardens. Listen for the shears. Then back to me at the Grudge Hall in Heartwood.
complete: Eight pikes, entered against eight names. The parterres will grow a little wilder for it, which Heartwood will count as an improvement. That is the hands that held the pikes. Which leaves the hand that pointed them, and I have its name on the next page. Stay; the chapter is not closed.

g_drk_30b.name: The First Name

objective.label: Defeat the Head Gardener in the south-east parterre of the King's Gardens

g_drk_30b.desc: Reckoner Thorn wants the Head Gardener defeated in the south-east parterre of the King's Gardens: it drew the Gardens' plan and wrote 'cleared' across every one of Heartwood's plots.
offer: The Head Gardener drew the plan of the King's Gardens, and the plan survives; this hall holds a copy. Our families' plots are on it, every house, every lane, and across each one the Gardener wrote one word: 'cleared'. One word, across every household we had there. The first name in the Gardens chapter of the book is the Head Gardener's, and it is underlined, which in this hall means overdue even by our standards.

It still walks the paths it drew, checking the hedges against its plan; it works the south-east parterre now, off the Fountain Court's south walk. Go to the King's Gardens, find it there, and defeat it. It is a large thing and it does not work alone; take company. Keep the appointment, and come back to me.
progress: The Head Gardener, in the south-east parterre of the King's Gardens, off the Fountain Court's south walk. Defeat it; take company. Then back to the Grudge Hall in Heartwood.
complete: The first name, struck through. 'Cleared', it wrote; cleared, I have written back, against its own name, and the ink took. There is a second name in this chapter, under the glass. The Nurseryman, in the cellars beneath the glasshouse: it raised the seedlings that were planted where our houses stood. I will tell you about it when you are ready to go under.

g_drk_30c.name: Nightward

objective.label: Defeat the Nurseryman in the Propagating Cellars beneath the King's Gardens

g_drk_30c.desc: Reckoner Thorn wants the Nurseryman defeated in the Propagating Cellars beneath the King's Gardens' glasshouse, where the Gardens' stock was grafted onto roots cut from Heartwood's groves.
offer: The Nurseryman. It keeps the Propagating Cellars, the dungeon beneath the glasshouse in the south-east of the King's Gardens; the way down is through the glasshouse itself. Every plant the Gardens ever grew came out of those cellars, and every one was grafted onto rootstock lifted from our groves when they were felled. Our trees, cut, to grow theirs. The roses an emperor walked among stood on Heartwood roots, and the Nurseryman did the cutting.

That is the second name in the Gardens chapter. Go under the glass, through the potting hall and the grafting room to the Nurseryman's own office, and defeat it. Take company; the cellars are not kind to anyone alone. Come back, and the hall will dress you for the dark.
Nightward, the set is called: the direction our families went when they were walked out, which was wherever the Gardens' lamps did not reach.
progress: The Nurseryman, in the Propagating Cellars beneath the glasshouse of the King's Gardens. Defeat it, with company, and come back to the Grudge Hall in Heartwood.
complete: Two names, struck. The Gardens chapter is closed, and Morrow has already asked for the page to be read aloud under the elders at the Grove Ring. I told her: after you have had it in your hands. You have. She may read it tonight.
Nightward, all four pieces: visor, hauberk, chausses, sabatons. Dark plate for dark appointments. You keep them better than most who have stood where you are standing.

g_drk_40a.name: Hides for the Ledger

objective.label: Bring Reckoner Thorn 6 ash beast pelts from the beasts of the Burned Land

g_drk_40a.desc: The Grudge Hall's book is coming apart at its Burned Land chapter. Reckoner Thorn needs six ash beast pelts, taken inside the fire line of the Burned Land and not bought, for a cover that will not burn.
offer: Before the fourth chapter, a plain errand, because the book itself needs it. Three hundred years of hands turning the same pages, and the binding has given at the Burned Land chapter, which is the heaviest: the ring of ash round the Capital, where one flash out of the Capital, on the Night the household left, scorched everything inside the fire line. Every grudge in that chapter weighs more than the ones before it.

The new cover will be ash beast pelt. It does not burn; the beasts walk that ash and come out of it unsinged, and for the cover of this particular chapter, that is the point. Bring me six ash beast pelts, from the ash beasts and the ash giants inside the fire line, north toward the Capital's gates.
Nothing off the courts' stalls. I will know a bought hide, because a bought hide has never been near a fire. Take them yourself.
progress: Six ash beast pelts, from the ash beasts and ash giants inside the fire line of the Burned Land, north toward the Capital's gates. Taken yourself, not bought. Back to the Grudge Hall when you have them.
complete: Six, and not one of them bought; I can smell the ash on them. The binder is a Reed, of the Reeds' mill, one of your four; she will have the book whole again by the week's end, and the Burned Land chapter will sit in a cover that cannot burn. Now the chapter itself. Stay; I have it open.

g_drk_40b.name: Blackthorn

objective.label: Break 8 scorch sentinels in the Burned Land

g_drk_40b.desc: Reckoner Thorn wants eight scorch sentinels broken in the Burned Land: the sentinels that walked the fire line with oil and torches on the Night so the burn faced outward exactly as ordered.
offer: The scorch sentinels walked the fire line on the Night. Not the fire; the line. The flash came out of the Capital, but the edge of the burn, the ring Junn read with her survey glass, was walked by sentinels with oil and torches so the fire would face outward exactly as far as it was told to and not one yard back toward the walls. A fire with instructions. The book has a column for instructions, and it is the column I least like filling.

Break eight scorch sentinels. They still camp on the line they drew: one camp south-west of the Capital's gates, one east of them on the road to the Beacon Fort's door. Eight between the two camps will do.

The set you earn is Blackthorn, after the hedge round the Hollin grove, your first tusk, which burned in the Felling and grew back black. Things that burn here do not always stay down. Remember that in the ash.
progress: Eight scorch sentinels, in the Burned Land: one camp south-west of the Capital's gates, one east of them on the road to the Beacon Fort. Then back to the Grudge Hall in Heartwood.
complete: Eight. The line is a little less drawn than it was; the ash will blow across it now with nobody to tidy the edge. That is the torches. One more name in this chapter, and this one signed its own entry: the Reply the Regent sent down to our embassy went out under its seal. Stay; the page is open.

g_drk_40c.name: In Writing, In Person

objective.label: Defeat the Wall-Warden at the top of the Great Watchtower

g_drk_40c.desc: The Regent's Reply, telling the free cities to 'prepare to yield custody', went out under the Wall-Warden's seal. Reckoner Thorn wants the Wall-Warden defeated at the top of the Great Watchtower on the Border Wall.
offer: The Regent's Reply. You know it: the courts sent their embassy up the Border Wall to the Great Watchtower with letters for whoever commands inside, and the answer the Herald Sentinel read back had been written in advance, three hundred years before anyone asked. It calls the free cities 'caretaker governments'. It thanks us for keeping the land warm. It tells us to 'prepare to yield custody'. Morrow has written under it: the bill now has a cover letter.

The Reply went out under the Wall-Warden's seal. It is the Great Watchtower's officer of the watch; every dispatch down from that wall carries its mark, and it put its mark on that one and sent it down to us like a clerk sending out a fine. The hall has the Reply in writing. The hall would like it in person.
The Wall-Warden is at the top of the Great Watchtower, on the Border Wall, beside the Embassy's Camp. Take company; the tower is garrisoned to the roof. Defeat it. Keep the appointment.
progress: The Wall-Warden, at the top of the Great Watchtower on the Border Wall, beside the Embassy's Camp. Defeat it with company, then back to the Grudge Hall in Heartwood.
complete: In person. The entry is closed, and the Reply goes back into the book not as a letter but as a receipt, which is what we always meant it for: proof that they know what they owe, in their own hand, under their own seal.

Blackthorn, all four pieces: visor, hauberk, chausses, sabatons. The chapter is rebound in a cover that will not burn, and the plate is paid for. Wear it on the Burned Land; that is where it was earned, and that is where the last chapter waits.

g_drk_50a.name: What the Fire Left Standing

objective.label: Defeat the Glassed Stag in the glassed orchard in the west of the Burned Land

g_drk_50a.desc: Reckoner Thorn wants the Glassed Stag defeated in the glassed orchard in the west of the Burned Land, to settle the one open question in the Grudge Hall's book: whether the stag is a debt the fire owes or a creditor like Heartwood.
offer: The last chapter, and the last set: Eclipse. It is named for the one lamp on the Night that did not lean. On the Night every lamp in the Capital leaned all one way, the way the household went. Ours did not lean, because it was ours and it was outside, and nobody in the Capital looked back to see it was still burning. That is the whole of Heartwood's grievance in one lamp, and you will wear it.

First, the stag. It was in the orchard in the west of the Burned Land on the Night, and the flash caught it mid-stride and glassed it where it stood, facing away from the city; every trunk around it leans the same way. The way I read it, it has been running outward ever since and never got anywhere. It is not ours; it is nobody's. The book has carried it three hundred years as its one open question: a debt the fire owes, or a creditor like us.

Settle it. The glassed orchard is in the west of the Burned Land, west of the Ash Road Crystal. Defeat the Glassed Stag; take company, it is heavy and fast and glass does not tire. Then come back and tell me which it was.
progress: The Glassed Stag, in the glassed orchard in the west of the Burned Land, west of the Ash Road Crystal. Defeat it with company, then back to the Grudge Hall in Heartwood.
complete: Settled. Creditor, I have written: it was owed something by that fire and never paid, the same as us, and now it is paid the only way the book has for a thing that cannot be given back. Paid, and the question closed after three hundred years. Now the beacon. Stay; the page is open.

g_drk_50b.name: Who Lit the Beacons

objective.label: Defeat the Beacon-Keeper at the top of the Beacon Fort

g_drk_50b.desc: The Beacon-Keeper lit the Beacon Fort's fire on the Night, at the free cities. Reckoner Thorn wants it defeated in the beacon chamber at the top of the Beacon Fort and its lamp put out.
offer: The Beacon-Keeper lit the beacon on the Night. The Beacon Fort stands on the Melt Ridge, east of the Capital's gates, and its log is still in the Keeper's hand; Morrow copied the entry for the hall, and the hall has her copy. It reads: 'Lit at the signal. The fire faced outward, as instructed.' In the calm hand, the same hand that wrote 'Seal it behind us' in the Bell Tower.

Think about what a beacon is. It is a lamp you light for people far away, so that they can see it. It was not lit for the household; the household was leaving. The only people far away were us. They lit it at us, and the fire it signalled faced our way.

It still keeps its lamp burning, three hundred years on, waiting for a signal to answer. Go to the Beacon Fort, climb to the beacon chamber at the top, and defeat the Beacon-Keeper. Take company; the fort is held to the roof. Put the lamp out.
progress: The Beacon-Keeper, in the beacon chamber at the top of the Beacon Fort, on the Melt Ridge east of the Capital's gates in the Burned Land. Defeat it with company; then back to the Grudge Hall.
complete: Out. The lamp they lit at us is dark, the entry is drawn through, and I have added under it what the log did not say: who it was lit at. That leaves the gate itself, and the thing that has stood in front of it since the Night, reading. One appointment left in the book. Stay.

g_drk_50c.name: Eclipse

objective.label: Defeat the Proclaimer before the Capital's gate in the Burned Land

g_drk_50c.desc: The last appointment in the Grudge Hall's book: the Proclaimer, the sentinel that read the ban on Heartwood's songs from the Capital's gate, and with it the orders behind every grudge in the hall's book, still reads every dawn before the gates in the Burned Land. Reckoner Thorn wants it defeated.
offer: The last appointment in the book, and the one every dark knight who ever wiped their feet on this floor is sworn to. The Proclaimer is the sentinel that stood at the Capital's gate and read out the empire's proclamations. It read the ban on the chanters' war-songs from that gate, the ban Heartwood still sings under.

And beneath the ban, in the same voice, it read out the rest of the orders: the groves to be felled, the mill to be taken, the families to be moved. Every grudge on this floor was a line in that reading first, and the hall has entered each one as a debt. Morrow has the wording on the floor; I have the date, and it has waited long enough.

It reads them still. Every dawn, before the Capital's gates, in a fair clear voice, to nobody, because nobody ever told it the reading was done. Sabel's camp has heard it every morning since the courts arrived.
Go to the Burned Land, to the ground before the Capital's gates, and defeat the Proclaimer. Take company; it was built to outlast a city, and it has. Keep the appointment, and come home.
progress: The Proclaimer, on the ground before the Capital's gates in the Burned Land. Defeat it with company, then come home to the Grudge Hall in Heartwood.
complete: The last line, drawn. The book is still three hundred years thick and will stay so; the floor does not forget because a line is drawn through it. But the Capital chapter ends on your name, and Morrow has the page already. The ring will hear it read under the elders tonight.

Eclipse, all four pieces: visor, hauberk, chausses, sabatons. The one lamp that did not lean. The hall's floor stays where it is, and the dates stay mine. But you are the first to walk off this floor owed nothing, and the book has a column for that too. I have never filled it before.

g_drk_34.name: The Watch's Own Record

objective.label: Bring Warden Morrow 5 watch ledgers from the rampart and watch sentinels of the Border Wall and the Great Watchtower

g_drk_34.desc: Warden Morrow, at the Embassy's Camp on the Border Wall, wants five watch ledgers from the wall's rampart and watch sentinels, to set the wall's own record of the families marched out past it beside the Grudge Hall's. The reward is a Nightward Waymark visor sent up by Reckoner Thorn.
offer: Thorn sent word up with the embassy's kit that a dark knight of the hall would be on the wall, and here you are. Good. The hall's book says the Border Wall logged every family the empire marched out past it, off the land that became the Estates and the Gardens, and nothing that ever came back in. That is our record. I would like theirs.

The wall's own ledgers would show it; the wall logs everything, it is what a wall is for. The sentinels still carry them: the rampart sentinels on the rampart road, and the watch sentinels inside the Great Watchtower. Bring me five watch ledgers.

Thorn has a visor for you, Nightward Waymark pattern, the little road-sign the hall cuts into kit it sends out of the city, with your name written against it. It came up with the embassy's kit. The price is five ledgers, and I am holding it until they are on this table.
progress: Five watch ledgers, from the rampart sentinels on the rampart road of the Border Wall and the watch sentinels inside the Great Watchtower. Bring them to me at the Embassy's Camp.
complete: Five, and I have read every one. They say what ours says: so many out, by name and by lane, and nothing back. Two books kept three hundred years apart, agreeing to the family. Here is the Nightward Waymark visor; the hall sent it up with the embassy's kit. Accurate, you will notice, when you wear it. Not bitter.

g_drk_37.name: Vultures on the Line

objective.label: Drive 8 pyre vultures from the Glassed Orchard in the west of the Burned Land

g_drk_37.desc: Warden Morrow, at Emmer's Farm in the Burned Land, wants eight pyre vultures driven off the fire line at the Glassed Orchard in the west of the Burned Land, beside the road toward the King's Gardens, where they dig up what the burn left in the ground. Reckoner Thorn has sent Nightward Waymark sabatons for the dark knight who does it.
offer: Pyre vultures. You will have seen them on the way in, working the fire line. They dig the line for whatever the burn left in the ground, and what the burn left in the ground is the people who were inside it and did not go with the household, and did not live either. Nobody is dead, by the rolls; the empire's register has never recorded one death that night, and the hall does not argue with a register. But what lies in that ground is not living either, and the vultures dig for it.

The hall takes in the unclaimed. It is the oldest rule on the floor. The barrow diggers in the Heartwood Fields dig up our families' grave-goods; this is the same work, a long way deeper in, and the hall's answer is the same.

Drive off eight pyre vultures. They are thickest at the Glassed Orchard, on the west side of the Burned Land where the road toward the King's Gardens swings past it; the fire line is oldest there and the ground is softest. Thorn sent sabatons up for the dark knight who stops them. That is not the kind of entry the hall usually makes, so make it worth the ink.
progress: Eight pyre vultures, at the Glassed Orchard on the west side of the Burned Land, beside the road toward the King's Gardens. Then come back to me at Emmer's Farm.
complete: Eight. The ground along that stretch is quiet, and whatever is in it stays in it, unclaimed but undisturbed, which is all the hall can give them from here. Sabatons, Nightward Waymark pattern; Thorn had them sent up and I have kept them dry in my pack, which in this land is a kindness. Wear them home.

g_mnk_10.name: Feathers for the Breath

objective.label: Bring Refrain-Master Larch 6 hen feathers from the wood hens and grove pigeons of the Heartwood Fields

g_mnk_10.desc: Refrain-Master Larch of the Banned Refrain, Heartwood's hall of chanters, will take on a new monk who brings six hen feathers from the Heartwood Fields: a chanter's first lesson is seeing their own breath on a feather.
offer: Shoulders down. Before anything else, shoulders down. I am Ione Larch, refrain-master of this hall, the Banned Refrain, where Heartwood keeps the war-songs the empire forbade us to sing. Chant-Master Wynn teaches the fists. I hand out the refrains, and the first thing I hand a new chanter is not a song. It is a feather.

A chanter's first lesson is seeing your own breath. Hold a feather in front of your mouth and sing a line. If the feather moves, you are breathing and the note is riding on it. If it does not move, you are not breathing, you are shouting, and shouting is what the empire wanted from us.

Bring me six hen feathers from the Heartwood Fields, out through the West Gate. The wood hens scratch about near the charcoal camps; the grove pigeons are out west, if you can catch one. Bring me six and the Breathbound set is yours, head to feet, and you will wear it until it fits you.
progress: Six hen feathers from the Heartwood Fields: wood hens near the charcoal camps, grove pigeons out west. Bring them back to me at the Banned Refrain in Heartwood.
complete: Hold one up. Now sing. It moved. Good; that is breath, and breath is the whole job: the note rides on it and so does the fist. Breathbound: headband, tunic, trousers, footwraps. The feather hangs from the headband; wear it low, in front of your face. It is there to show you your breath, not to be looked at by anyone else.

g_mnk_20a.name: The Work-Song's Watchmen

objective.label: Stop 8 felling sentinels in the Timber Estates

g_mnk_20a.desc: Refrain-Master Larch wants eight felling sentinels stopped in the Timber Estates, and the beat they swing to listened for first: the Estates cut their pace from a Heartwood work-song with the verses the empire disliked taken out.
offer: Now the gate is open, the second set. The Timber Estates, our old groves past the Border Gate west of the Fields, felled and replanted in rows, cut their pace from one of our work-songs: the one Heartwood's fellers sang when the groves were ours and a tree came down with a verse for what it was owed. The empire liked the rhythm. It did not like all the words, so it took out the verses it disliked and set its felling sentinels, the iron axe-hands that still work the Estates, swinging to what was left.

They swing to it still, three hundred years on. Go onto the Estates and stop eight felling sentinels. But listen first: before each one drops, listen to the beat it swings to and count the verses. I want to know which verses the Foreman kept and which it threw away.
progress: Eight felling sentinels, among the ranks of the Timber Estates past the Border Gate. Listen to the beat before each one drops, and come back to the Banned Refrain in Heartwood.
complete: Verses one to four and the chorus; that is what you heard, and that is what they kept. One to four are the cutting verses, how to notch and where to stand. The ones they dropped were the verses about what the trees were owed: the sapling for every trunk, the rest for the ground. That is a receipt, as plain as any in the Grudge Hall. The Foreman that set the pace is next, and you will answer it.

g_mnk_20b.name: Sing It Down

objective.label: Fell the Foreman at the south end of the Timber Estates

g_mnk_20b.desc: Refrain-Master Larch wants the Foreman, which sets the Timber Estates' pace with Heartwood's stolen and shortened work-song, felled at the south end of the Estates below the Felled Block, and the dropped verses sung over it.
offer: The Foreman sets the whole plantation's pace. It stands at the south end of the Timber Estates, below the Felled Block where the last cutting stopped, and it calls the shortened work-song so every sentinel on the Estates swings in time. It stole our song and cut it down to the verses that suited it. A chanter answers a song; that is the job, and this is the first time you will do it for real.

Take a party; it is a big thing and it was built to work all day. It counts in ones and hits in twos: one beat, then two blows, every time. Breathe on the one, move on the two. Fell it, and when it is down, sing the verses it dropped over it, out loud, so the Estates hear the whole song once. Bring the verse back whole.
progress: The Foreman, at the south end of the Timber Estates, below the Felled Block. Take a party. Fell it, then sing the dropped verses over it, and come back to the Banned Refrain in Heartwood.
complete: Down, and the song is ours again at its full length; the Estates heard it whole for the first time since the Felling, and every sentinel still swinging out there is swinging to nothing now. Willowstep: headband, tunic, trousers, footwraps. The trousers are cut for stepping, not for standing. You stand too much. Stop standing.

g_mnk_30a.name: Glass Sung Over

objective.label: Bring Refrain-Master Larch 6 ember glass from the ember wisps of the Furnace Hall

g_mnk_30a.desc: Refrain-Master Larch wants six pieces of ember glass from the ember wisps of the Furnace Hall, the dungeon under the Glassworks, to hear whether the furnace chant's note has drifted in three hundred years.
offer: The third set, and a harder lesson. The Glassworks, the empire's glass desert at the end of the Glassworks Road out of the Timber Estates, has a hall under it, entered by the Kiln Mouth: the Furnace Hall, where the furnaces have burned three hundred years without going out. The Furnace Hall has a chant. The Cinder Abbot leads it, and the ember wisps that drift through its halls are what is left of its choir: embers that remember being singers. Their glass holds the note they went out on.

Every chanter who ever won a fight learned the same thing first: how to hold a note against a louder one. That furnace is the loudest voice left in the world. Go down into the Furnace Hall, take six pieces of ember glass off the ember wisps, and bring them to me.
Before you come back, put one to your ear. I want to know whether the pitch has drifted in three hundred years. Then I will know whether the choir still has the song, or only the noise.
progress: Six ember glass, from the ember wisps in the Furnace Hall, the dungeon under the Glassworks. Put one to your ear before you come back to the Banned Refrain in Heartwood.
complete: Flat. You heard it too; I can see it on your face. Three hundred years at the furnace and the note has gone flat by a quarter tone. The wisps have lost the words, and a chant with no words is only heat. But the amber acolytes down there have not lost them; they still know every word. That is the next thing we deal with.

g_mnk_30b.name: The Furnace Chant

objective.label: Silence 10 amber acolytes in the Furnace Hall

g_mnk_30b.desc: Refrain-Master Larch wants ten amber acolytes silenced in the Furnace Hall under the Glassworks, to thin the furnace chant they sing in shifts until the Cinder Abbot holds it alone.
offer: The amber acolytes still know the words. They sing the furnace chant in shifts, down in the Furnace Hall, so that it never stops: one shift breathes while another sings. That is a discipline, and I would admire it anywhere else. Silence ten of them and the chant thins; there will not be enough voices left to cover the breaths.

Ten amber acolytes, in the Furnace Hall under the Glassworks. Here is the lesson: count your breaths between one kill and the next. Four in, four out, and the count never stops. If you lose the count, you are rushing, and a chanter who rushes in a furnace comes out glass.
progress: Ten amber acolytes, in the Furnace Hall under the Glassworks. Count your breaths between kills. Then back to the Banned Refrain in Heartwood.
complete: Ten fewer voices. The chant thins; it does not stop, because the Cinder Abbot is holding it alone now, with no shift to spell it and no choir to hide behind. One voice against the furnace. That is exactly how I want it, because one voice is something a chanter can answer. Rest, breathe, and then we go for the Abbot.

g_mnk_30c.name: Stillheart

objective.label: Fell the Cinder Abbot in the Furnace Hall

g_mnk_30c.desc: Refrain-Master Larch wants the Cinder Abbot, which keeps the Furnace Hall's time with its own heart, felled in the Furnace Hall under the Glassworks. It blinds, so it needs a party and a steady breath.
offer: A chant with one voice left is a duel. The Cinder Abbot keeps the furnace's time with its own heart: every beat of it is a beat of the chant, and every beat of the chant is a stroke of the furnace. Stop the heart and the hall loses its time. Still it.

It is in the Furnace Hall under the Glassworks, in the Old Flue Chapel, off the far end of the hall past the stoking floor. Take a party; you will not do this alone and I would not ask you to. It blinds: the glare off it takes your eyes for a count of ten at a time. A chanter fights fine blind if the breath is steady, because the breath tells you where your own feet are. Keep it steady, and keep singing between the blows so your party knows where you are.
progress: The Cinder Abbot, in the Furnace Hall under the Glassworks. Take a party. It blinds; keep your breath steady and your feet under you. Then back to the Banned Refrain in Heartwood.
complete: The furnace keeps no time now. It still burns, but it burns like a fire and not like a drum, and the Glassworks will be a quieter place for the courts to work in. Stillheart: headband, tunic, trousers, footwraps. The tunic sits tight across the ribs on purpose. Breathe against it; when it stops feeling tight, you are breathing the way I want.

g_mnk_40a.name: Char at the Door

objective.label: Clear 8 char hounds from the door of the Beacon Fort

g_mnk_40a.desc: Refrain-Master Larch wants eight char hounds cleared from inside the door of the Beacon Fort, on the Melt Ridge in the Burned Land, so the fort's choir, still singing Heartwood's beacon hymn, can be heard.
offer: The fourth set takes you into the Burned Land, the ring of ash round the Capital. On the Melt Ridge, east of the Capital's gates off the east road, stands the Beacon Fort, and its choir is still singing. What it sings is the beacon hymn, the song for lighting a signal fire. Ours, by the way; Heartwood's, from before the empire. Chanter Ives will swear to it, and so will I. The empire took it with the rest.

Nobody has heard the hymn properly in three hundred years, because the char hounds kennelled inside the fort's door go for anyone who stops to listen. Clear eight char hounds off the door. I want to hear a hymn, not a kennel.
progress: Eight char hounds, inside the door of the Beacon Fort on the Melt Ridge, off the Burned Land's east road. Then back to the Banned Refrain in Heartwood.
complete: Eight. You can stand at the door and hear the choir now, and so can anyone else who walks up. What they sing is half the hymn, over and over, from the first line to the middle and back to the first. The half they were singing when they lit the beacon on the Night. They never got to the rest. We have the rest.

g_mnk_40b.name: The Beacon Verse

objective.label: Silence 8 cinder choristers in the Beacon Fort

g_mnk_40b.desc: Refrain-Master Larch wants eight cinder choristers silenced in the Beacon Fort, and the line where each stops listened for: they sing half the beacon hymn, and the Banned Refrain has kept the other half in chests for three hundred years.
offer: The cinder choristers sing half the beacon hymn, and they have been singing that half since the Night. The Banned Refrain kept the other half, the second half, written out and locked in chests in this hall for three hundred years, because the empire had banned it and we were not going to lose it. Two halves of one song, kept by two sides of one wall, and neither has heard the other.

Silence eight cinder choristers in the Beacon Fort; they sing in the Wardens' Cells beside the Beacon Stair. Not for silence's sake: listen hard to the line where each one stops. That is where our half comes in, and I need to know the note it comes in on.
progress: Eight cinder choristers, in the Beacon Fort on the Melt Ridge. Listen to where each one stops singing. Then back to the Banned Refrain in Heartwood.
complete: Eight quiet, and you brought me the note. The half they sang ends on a rising note, unresolved, which means ours comes next, exactly as the chests have it; the two halves fit. One voice is still singing up there. The Beacon-Keeper is holding the last line of their half at the top of the fort, and has been holding it for three hundred years.

g_mnk_40c.name: Cloudstride

objective.label: Fell the Beacon-Keeper in the beacon chamber of the Beacon Fort

g_mnk_40c.desc: Refrain-Master Larch wants the Beacon-Keeper felled in the beacon chamber at the top of the Beacon Fort, and the Banned Refrain's half of the beacon hymn sung over it to finish the song.
offer: The Beacon-Keeper lit the beacon on the Night, and it has stood in the beacon chamber at the top of the fort ever since, with the beacon log in one hand and the last line of their half of the hymn in its mouth, held and never finished. The Grudge Hall wants the log; Thorn can have it. We want the note.

Take a party up the beacon stair to the chamber at the top of the Beacon Fort. It blinds, as the Abbot did; you have trained for blind, and you know your feet now. Fell it, and the moment its line breaks, sing ours: the second half, the half from the chests, over it. Finish the hymn.
progress: The Beacon-Keeper, in the beacon chamber at the top of the Beacon Fort. Take a party. Fell it and sing the second half of the hymn over it. Then back to the Banned Refrain in Heartwood.
complete: Finished. Three hundred years with the hymn stuck on a rising note, and tonight it resolves; I heard it in how you walked in. Thorn can send for the log whenever the Grudge Hall likes; the note is ours. Cloudstride: headband, tunic, trousers, footwraps. Light as the name. You will notice your feet before you notice the fort, which is the right way round.

g_mnk_50a.name: What Comes at the Light

objective.label: Kill 8 ash beasts that come at the light of Sabel's camp before the Capital's gates in the Burned Land

g_mnk_50a.desc: Refrain-Master Larch wants eight ash beasts killed as they come at the light of Sabel's camp before the Capital's gates in the Burned Land, with the war-songs' watch verse sung the whole time.
offer: The last set. Lotus. Three things to do before the hall gives it, and the first is a watch. There is a verse in the war-songs for standing a night watch: you sing it low, all night, so the dark knows it is not welcome at your fire. The empire banned that one too, and we kept it anyway.

Sabel's camp, the courts' last camp, sits on the ash before the Capital's gates, and the ash beasts come at its light every night, all night. Go there and kill eight of them, in sight of the walls, and sing the watch verse the whole time you are doing it. Nobody in that camp will hear you over the fighting, and the Regent on its walls will not care. Do it anyway. The verse is for you.
progress: Eight ash beasts, as they come at the light of Sabel's camp before the Capital's gates in the Burned Land. Sing the watch verse while you do it. Then back to the Banned Refrain in Heartwood.
complete: Eight, and you sang through all of it; I can hear it in your breath, you are still half on the verse. The watch verse holds; it was always going to, that is what it is for. That is one. Now the thing in the orchard, the one that could not hold still.

g_mnk_50b.name: The Stag That Faces Away

objective.label: Fell the Glassed Stag in the glassed orchard of the Burned Land

g_mnk_50b.desc: Refrain-Master Larch wants the Glassed Stag felled in the glassed orchard west of the Ash Road Crystal in the Burned Land. The flash glassed it mid-stride on the Night, and Larch wants that stride finished.
offer: The Glassed Stag. It was in the orchard in the west of the Burned Land when the flash came out of the Capital, and the flash caught it mid-stride and glassed it where it was, facing away from the city. Junn's survey says every trunk in that orchard leans the same way, and so does the stag. The way I hear it, it was running from the flash and it is running still, in glass, and has never finished the stride.

A chanter cannot leave a thing mid-stride. A phrase is finished or it is not sung. Go to the glassed orchard, west of the Ash Road Crystal in the Burned Land, and fell the Glassed Stag. Take a party. It is fast, it is heavy, and it does not stop for a note, so do not waste breath trying to sing it down. Breathe, step, strike. Finish the stride for it.
progress: The Glassed Stag, in the glassed orchard west of the Ash Road Crystal in the Burned Land. Take a party. Then back to the Banned Refrain in Heartwood.
complete: Finished. Glass faces outward, Junn said, and she was right: everything in that land faces away from the centre, the trunks, the ripples, the stag. Everything except one thing, which stands at the Capital's gate and faces out at us on purpose, and reads. That is the third thing, and the last.

g_mnk_50c.name: Lotus

objective.label: Put down the Proclaimer before the Capital's gates in the Burned Land

g_mnk_50c.desc: The Proclaimer, the sentinel that read the ban on Heartwood's war-songs from the Capital's gate, still reads it every dawn before the gates in the Burned Land. Refrain-Master Larch wants it allowed to finish, then the banned refrain sung at it and the Proclaimer put down.
offer: The Proclaimer. It is the sentinel that stood at the Capital's gate and read the empire's proclamations to the land, and three hundred years ago it read the one that banned Heartwood's war-songs: every refrain in this hall, forbidden in a fair clear voice from the top of the gate. It is still at the gate. It reads the proclamation every dawn, to nobody, in the same fair voice, because nobody told it to stop.
