That is the oldest grudge this hall holds. Thorn's hall can keep the rest of them, the groves and the mills; I keep the songs it banned, and I have kept them for exactly this.

Go to the ground before the Capital's gates in the Burned Land, at dawn if you can manage it. Let it finish reading; every word, do not interrupt it. Then sing the banned refrain at it, the whole of it, in the open, and put it down. Take a party; it was built to outlast a city, and so far it has.
progress: The Proclaimer, before the Capital's gates in the Burned Land. Let it finish reading, then sing the banned refrain at it and put it down. Take a party. Then come home to the Banned Refrain in Heartwood.
complete: It has read its last. The refrain was sung at the gate, in the open, in daylight, at the thing that banned it, and the hall will record who sang it; that is what your new title says. Lotus: headband, tunic, trousers, footwraps. The last set this hall gives, because there is nothing left to teach you that a song can. Shoulders down.

g_mnk_34.name: Breath in the Cold

objective.label: Lay 8 frost wights to rest on the snowfields of the Border Wall

g_mnk_34.desc: Warden Morrow, at the Embassy's Camp on the Border Wall, is holding a Stillheart Waymark headband from Refrain-Master Larch for the chanter who lays eight frost wights to rest on the snowfields east of the camp.
offer: Larch sent a headband up with the embassy's kit, Stillheart Waymark pattern, the hall's little road-sign cut into whatever it sends out of the city, with a note: for the chanter who can sing through the snowfields. I am to hold it until you have.

The Snowfields lie east of the Embassy's Camp, past the Great Watchtower. The cold up here takes the breath out of you, and the frost wights take what is left: they are what is left of household people who were on the wall that night and did not go with the household: not dead by any roll, and not alive. Lay eight of them to rest.
Breathe through your wraps, Larch says, and do not stop for the cold. I say come back with all your fingers. Both instructions stand.
progress: Eight frost wights, on the snowfields east of the Embassy's Camp on the Border Wall. Breathe through the wraps. Then back to me at the embassy.
complete: Eight laid to rest, and the snow is quieter for it. Here: the Stillheart Waymark headband, from Larch by way of the embassy's kit. Larch says the breath goes in cold and comes out as a note. I say it comes out as fog, and I have the wall's weather to back me. Take it, and go and stand by the fire.

g_mnk_37.name: Horn and Breath

objective.label: Kill 6 ashhorns east of the fire line in the Burned Land

g_mnk_37.desc: Warden Morrow, at Emmer's Farm in the Burned Land, is holding Stillheart Waymark footwraps from Refrain-Master Larch for the chanter who keeps their feet against six ashhorns east of the fire line, past the Melt Ridge.
offer: Larch sent footwraps for you with the last kit, Stillheart Waymark pattern, and a line I am to read you: for whoever can keep their feet when the boar hits. The boar is the ashhorn. They root the east of the fire line, past the Melt Ridge, turning the ash for whatever grows under it, and they charge at a sound. Any sound. A chanter makes sounds; Larch finds this funny.
Kill six ashhorns, east of the fire line past the Melt Ridge. Sing if you must, but plant your feet before the charge, not after. Keep your feet, and I will hand over the wraps.
progress: Six ashhorns, east of the fire line past the Melt Ridge in the Burned Land. Keep your feet when they charge. Then back to me at Emmer's Farm.
complete: Six, and you are standing, which was the whole of the test. Stillheart Waymark footwraps, from the hall by way of my pack. The ash here gets in everywhere, into the bread and the ink and the boots; these keep it out of the step, and a chanter's step is the one thing Larch will not have spoiled. Go on.

g_whm_10.name: The Antivenin

objective.label: Bring Dean Fairlie 4 venom sacs from the mireback drakelings at the north end of the Moonmere Shores, below the border gate

g_whm_10.desc: Dean Isolde Fairlie of the Mending College wants four venom sacs, whole, from the mireback drakelings at the north end of the Moonmere Shores, below the Border Gate. The college's antivenin is made from the bite itself, and brewing it is a White Mage's first lesson.
offer: I am Dean Isolde Fairlie. I run the Mending College, the academy's college of healing, and I decide who wears its cloth. You want to be a White Mage of this college, so you will start where the college started. The first thing it ever made was the antivenin for mireback bite, and the first thing a White Mage learns is that the antivenin is made from the bite.

So: four venom sacs. The mireback drakelings carry them. They keep to the north end of the Moonmere Shores, across the causeway and then north past the Shore Wood, on the ground just below the Border Gate. Cut the sac out whole; a burst sac is a stain on your sleeve and not a lesson.

Bring the four back to me here at the college and I will show you the press. When the antivenin is on the shelf with your name in the margin, the college dresses you. The cloth is on the shelf behind me, and it has been for some time; see footnote one, which says I do not keep students waiting without a reason.
progress: I still need four venom sacs, whole. The mireback drakelings carry them, at the north end of the Moonmere Shores below the Border Gate, past the Shore Wood. Cut carefully; a burst sac is no use to the press.
complete: Four, and all four whole. Good. The press is in the back room; the antivenin will be on the shelf by evening, and your name will be in the margin beside it, where the college writes the name of whoever brought the bite. That is the first lesson, and you have had it: what mends the wound is taken from the thing that made it.

Mercyweave, the full set: veil, robe, trousers, shoes. The college's own looms, the college's own dye. You will notice the veil does not cover the eyes. That is deliberate; a healer has to see the wound to treat it. See footnote two.

g_whm_20a.name: The Second Column

objective.label: Lay 8 mere wraiths to rest on the east shore of the Summer Lakes

g_whm_20a.desc: Dean Fairlie is opening the second column of the Mending College's infirmary log, the one for what the college could not reach while the Border Gate was shut. She wants eight mere wraiths laid to rest on the east shore of the Summer Lakes, past the villas.
offer: Warden Liss, who keeps this college's infirmary logs, will tell you that on the night the empire vanished the college treated everyone who reached the shore by dawn. Accurate. Incomplete. The log she keeps has a second column, for what the college could not reach on the far side of the border, and for three hundred years that column has been empty, because the Border Gate was shut.
The gate is open. The courts have signed their letters of passage, and a White Mage of this college may walk through it with everyone else. So I am starting the column, and I am starting it with you.

Go through the Border Gate to the Summer Lakes, the old villa lakes of the household, as the sentinels call the empire's people, and follow the east shore past the villas. Mere wraiths rise out of the water there: the lake's dead, never laid down because nobody could reach them. Lay eight of them to rest. A White Mage lays down what cannot be mended; that is the half of the job the academy does not advertise. Then come back to me at the college and tell me the count.
progress: Eight mere wraiths, laid to rest. They rise on the east shore of the Summer Lakes, past the villas. Count them as you go; I am entering each one in the second column of the log.
complete: Eight. I have entered them in the second column of the log, in pencil, because the column is not finished: something keeps putting the dead back into that water. Scout Ilva's forward camp on the Lakes says the pull comes from the Sunken Ballroom, the household's dance hall under the lake. That is the next thing I will ask of you; speak to me again when you are ready to hear it.

g_whm_20b.name: What Drowned Them

objective.label: Put down the Undertow in the Sunken Ballroom

g_whm_20b.desc: The Undertow, in the flooded east wing of the Sunken Ballroom under the Summer Lakes, is what keeps putting the lake's dead back into the water. Dean Fairlie wants it put down so the infirmary log's second column can close. Take a party.
offer: The thing in the water is called the Undertow. It lairs in the flooded wing of the Sunken Ballroom, the household's dance hall under the Summer Lakes, past the Card Salon, and every report Scout Ilva's forward camp on the Lakes has sent me mentions a pull on the swimmers and the dead going back under. I have nine such reports. Nine is a pattern.

Put it down. Take a party; it is not a lesson for one, and it poisons, and I would rather you did not test the antivenin on yourself, however well you brewed it. Go in by the Ballroom Stair on the west mere's shore and down into the Long Portrait Gallery. The grand doors to the ballroom floor have fallen in, so you go round through the salons: take the east wing, through the Card Salon, into the Rose Salon, where the lake has broken the wall and pours in. That flooded wing is where the Undertow is.
When the Undertow is dead, the second column closes, and the college will have earned the right to dress you in Dawnpetal. Come back to me at the college when it is done.
progress: The Undertow, in the flooded east wing of the Sunken Ballroom: through the Card Salon to the Rose Salon, where the lake pours in. Take a party; it poisons. Come back to the college when it is dead.
complete: Done. The lake's dead will stay laid down now, and the second column of the infirmary log is closed; I have initialled it, which is how the college says a thing is finished. Liss will not say anything to you about it. That is how she says thank you.
Dawnpetal, all four pieces. The name is older than the college; we did not choose it, we inherited it with the loom it came off. See footnote three, which I have not written yet.

g_whm_30a.name: Pearl for the Eye-Salve

objective.label: Bring Dean Fairlie 6 mire pearls from the fen lurkers and mire drakes of the Canal Works

g_whm_30a.desc: The Mending College's eye-salve, ground mire pearl in oil, is the only thing that clears the blindness the deep choristers of the Great Sluice leave. The college has four grains left. Dean Fairlie wants six mire pearls from the fen lurkers and mire drakes of the Canal Works.
offer: The bargemen working the Canal Works for the courts' expedition are coming back to me blind. The cause is the deep choristers in the Great Sluice, the empire's old sluice house on the Canal Works fen: anyone who looks at them while they sing loses their sight. The only preparation that clears it is the college's eye-salve, ground mire pearl in oil, and the college has four grains of pearl left.

So, six mire pearls. The fen lurkers carry them, on the west marsh of the Canal Works, and so do the mire drakes to the south of the works; nothing else there does. The mere drakes on the Summer Lakes carry them too, if you are passing. Expect to kill a great many lurkers for six pearls. That is also the lesson: the college does not get its remedies cheaply, and never has.
Bring them to me here at the college. The salve goes in the mortar the day they arrive.
progress: Six mire pearls. The fen lurkers on the west marsh of the Canal Works carry them, and the mire drakes to the south; the mere drakes on the Summer Lakes too. Bring them to me at the college.
complete: Six. That is enough eye-salve for a season of bargemen, and the mortar is already out. Now the reason we needed it: the salve treats the blindness, and I would rather nobody went blind at all. Speak to me again and I will tell you what I want done about the choristers.

g_whm_30b.name: The Deep Choir

objective.label: Silence 8 deep choristers in the Great Sluice

g_whm_30b.desc: The deep choristers in the west gallery of the Great Sluice blind every bargeman who looks at them. Dean Fairlie has treated enough of them; she wants eight choristers silenced.
offer: The deep choristers. They stand in the west gallery of the Great Sluice, the empire's old sluice house on the Canal Works fen, and they sing, and anyone on the water who looks up at them while they sing goes blind and is sent to me. I have treated every one of them for a month. I have the salve now, thanks to you, and I would still rather not need it.

Silence eight of them. Go into the Great Sluice, across the bridge into the wheel hall, and round to the west gallery, where they sing at the great wheel; do not look at them longer than you must, and keep the eye-salve on you. I am aware a healer is supposed to prefer prevention. This is prevention.
Come back to the college when eight are quiet and tell me whether the Canal Works has sent me anyone since.
progress: Eight deep choristers silenced, in the west gallery of the Great Sluice. Keep the eye-salve on you, and look at them as little as you can.
complete: Eight. The Canal Works has sent me no one blind this week, which is the first week since the infirmary log begins. That is what prevention looks like in a ledger: an empty line.

But the choristers were singing to something. It is still down in the sluice, below the galleries, and it is why the sluice does not run. I will tell you about it when you are ready; speak to me again.

g_whm_30c.name: Gracewoven

objective.label: Put down the Thirst in the Great Sluice

g_whm_30c.desc: The Thirst sits in the West Sump of the Great Sluice and drinks the water the sluice should let through; the choristers sang for it. Dean Fairlie wants it put down so the sluice runs. Take a party.
offer: The thing the choristers sang to is called the Thirst. It sits in the West Sump of the Great Sluice, down the Sump Steps below the west gallery, and it drinks what the sluice should be letting through to the canals. The choir was singing for it. A healer gives. The Thirst only takes. I find that offensive on a professional level.
Put it down. Take a party, and take the eye-salve; the sump is where the choir's song ends up, and I want your eyes working when you reach it.
When it is dead the sluice will run, and the college will put you in Gracewoven, which is the cloth we wear when we have stopped pretending the job is gentle. Come back to me at the college.
progress: The Thirst, in the West Sump of the Great Sluice, down the Sump Steps below the west gallery. Take a party and the eye-salve. Come back to the college when it is dead.
complete: Done. The sluice runs; the water is going through to the canals as it was built to. The Canal Works will not thank you, because they do not know what was drinking it, and I am not going to tell them. Some things go in the log and nowhere else.
Gracewoven, all four pieces. The weave is the college's. The name is a reproach to whoever first thought mercy was the whole of the job; it is half, and the other half is this.

g_whm_34.name: Quills for the Case Notes

objective.label: Bring Junn 5 crag feathers from the crag hawks of the Border Wall

g_whm_34.desc: Junn, at the courts' embassy camp on the Border Wall, has a parcel of the Mending College's case notes to copy and no quill to copy them with. The college writes in crag hawk feather. She wants five crag feathers from the hawks on the wall's two stairs.
offer: You wear the Mending College's cloth. Good; that means I can ask you this without explaining the college to you first. Dean Fairlie sent a parcel up to the embassy's camp with the last supply train: a bundle of case notes for me to copy fair, in her own hand, which is illegible, and a note telling me to use a crag hawk quill, because the college writes its case notes in crag hawk and nothing else. It is the one quill the damp does not soften.

And the embassy's trunk came without a single one. So: five crag feathers. The crag hawks nest on the wall's two stairs, the West Stair and the East Stair, at either end of the rampart road; the Wall Drake on the storm side carries them too, but I am not asking you to go near that.

There is a veil in the parcel with a note that says 'for whoever brings the quills'. A Gracewoven Waymark piece, the college's own cut, the little road-sign the college puts on kit it sends out of the city. I think she meant you. I think she means most things.
progress: Five crag feathers, from the crag hawks that nest on the West Stair and the East Stair of the Border Wall. Bring them to me at the embassy's camp.
complete: Five. I can cut these into quills; the Dean's note has a diagram. The veil is yours, by her note, so put it on. The case notes are mine, by her handwriting, which I will be reading until spring. Thank you; the college's record of the wall is going to be legible because of you, which the college will never say.

g_whm_37.name: Bark for the Salve

objective.label: Bring Junn 5 glassed bark from the ash wights, pyre vultures and glass drakes of the Burned Land

g_whm_37.desc: At the fire line in the Burned Land, Junn has found the tree the Mending College's three-hundred-year-old burn salve recipe calls for: the glassed orchard. She wants five pieces of glassed bark from the ash wights, pyre vultures and glass drakes of the Burned Land.
offer: The Mending College has a recipe for a burn salve that calls for glassed bark. I looked it up on the barge, on the way here. The recipe is three hundred years old and has never once been made, because the only tree it could come from stood on the wrong side of the border, and nobody at the college had ever seen one. Well. Here is the fire line, the ring where the flash from the capital stopped, and there is the orchard, and every trunk in it is glass.

Five pieces of glassed bark. You will not get it off the trees with your hands; the creatures here carry it. The ash wights along the fire line, the pyre vultures past the camps, and the glass drakes out to the east all carry shards of it. Bring me five.
The Dean sent a pair of shoes with the recipe, Gracewoven Waymark, made for walking on ash. I assume she assumed somebody from the college would be out here, and I assume she assumed it would be you.
progress: Five glassed bark. The ash wights along the fire line carry it, the pyre vultures past the camps, the glass drakes to the east. Bring them to me at the fire line.
complete: Five. I will send the bark back to Moonmere on the next barge, with a note saying what the tree looked like, since the recipe never says. Bent away from the city. Every trunk in the orchard, bent the same way, as if the whole wood had turned its back on the walls in one moment. The shoes are yours; they are made for this ground.

g_whm_40a.name: Wolves Round the Camp

objective.label: Drive 8 cinder wolves from the ground around the Last Camp in the Burned Land

g_whm_40a.desc: Dean Fairlie is opening a Mending College field hospital at the Last Camp, the courts' camp before the Capital's gates in the Burned Land. The cinder wolves hold the ground east of the camp and come at the lamps; she wants eight driven off before she sends students.
offer: The college is putting a field hospital at the Last Camp: the courts' camp in the Burned Land, the last one before the Capital's gates. I am doing it because the courts' wounded come to me here in Moonmere from the Burned Land a week after they are hurt, and a week is the difference between a burn and a funeral. I have had enough funerals that were a week late.

The trouble is the cinder wolves. They hold the ground east of the camp and they come at the lamps every night, so the tents cannot go up. Drive eight of them off that ground. I will not send students onto it until it is quiet.
I am sending you because you are not a student any more; see the cloth you are wearing. Come back to me at the college when the eight are dead and I will tell you what the hospital needs next.
progress: Eight cinder wolves, driven off the ground east of the Last Camp in the Burned Land, so the hospital's tents can go up. Come back to the college when it is done.
complete: Eight. The tents are up and the lamps stayed lit through the night; the first students are on the barge. Now the hospital needs a burn salve, the old one, and the old one needs an ingredient nobody has ever asked a giant for politely. Speak to me again and I will explain.

g_whm_40b.name: The Old Remedy

objective.label: Bring Dean Fairlie 5 ash giant's teeth from the ash giants south-west of the Last Camp in the Burned Land

g_whm_40b.desc: The Mending College's old burn remedy is ground ash giant's tooth, written in its first formulary in a hand nobody can identify. Dean Fairlie wants five teeth from the ash giants that walk the south-west of the Burned Land, past the Last Camp, so the field hospital can make it.
offer: The old burn remedy, the one the college actually makes rather than the one it only has a recipe for, is ground giant's tooth. It is in the college's first formulary, the book the college was founded on, in a hand I cannot identify, and it works. I do not know what the ash giants were before the night the empire vanished, and I do not know how the first formulary knew about them, and I have decided not to know.

Five teeth. The ash giants walk the south-west of the Burned Land, past the Last Camp and out beyond the road to the gates. A giant drops a tooth perhaps one time in three. Do the arithmetic before you go; I did, and I am still sending you, because the hospital is full and the courts' wounded cannot wait for me to find a gentler source.
Bring the five to me at the college and the mortar will be out before you have finished speaking.
progress: Five ash giant's teeth, from the ash giants that walk the south-west of the Burned Land past the Last Camp. About one giant in three drops one. Bring them to the college.
complete: Five. The mortar is already out. The Last Camp will have the old remedy by the week's end, and the courts' wounded will stop arriving here a week late, because they will be treated there, the same day. That is the hospital doing what it is for.
One thing is still filling its beds, and it is walking the glassed orchard. Speak to me again when you are ready.

g_whm_40c.name: Sanctuary

objective.label: Fell the Glassed Stag in the glassed orchard of the Burned Land

g_whm_40c.desc: The Glassed Stag in the Glassed Orchard, in the north-west of the Burned Land, is filling the field hospital's beds with survey teams. Dean Fairlie wants it felled so the orchard is quiet. Take a party.
offer: Half the beds at the Last Camp are survey teams, and every one of them was in the Glassed Orchard, in the north-west of the Burned Land, and every one of them says the same word: stag. The Glassed Stag. It was in the orchard when the one flash came out of the capital as the empire vanished, and the flash turned it to glass where it was, mid-stride, facing away from the city. It is still walking. Nothing I have mends glass.

Fell it. Take a party; it hits like a fall from the college roof, and I have treated a fall from the college roof. Find it among the glass trees of the Glassed Orchard, in the north-west of the Burned Land, and keep it off the survey teams while you work.

When the orchard is quiet, the hospital earns its name, and so do you. The cloth for this rung is called Sanctuary. That is not a boast; it is a job description. Come back to the college when it is done.
progress: The Glassed Stag, in the Glassed Orchard in the north-west of the Burned Land. Take a party; it hits hard. Come back to the college when it is felled.
complete: Felled. The orchard is quiet, the survey teams are going out again, and the Last Camp has empty beds, which is the only measure of a hospital I accept.

Sanctuary, all four pieces. Wear the veil. Junn's report on the fire line says that everything in that land faces away from the centre, every trunk, every ripple in the melt. A White Mage is the one who turns round and faces it. That is what the veil leaves your eyes free for.

g_whm_50a.name: The Drakes at the Gate

objective.label: Clear 8 glass drakes from the ground before the Capital's gate in the Burned Land

g_whm_50a.desc: The courts have camped in sight of the Capital's gates, and the glass drakes hold the ground between the camp and the walls. Dean Fairlie wants eight cleared so a stretcher can cross. This is the last rung of the Mending College's ladder.
offer: The courts have camped in sight of the Capital's gates, and every banner in the free cities is marching to join them. The glass drakes have the ground between the camp and the walls, and I am treating drake-bite at the Last Camp that was got within sight of its own tents. That cannot stand while the hospital is there.
Clear eight of them from the ground before the gate. A drake's bite is a burn and a poison together; you have both salves now, so use them.

This is the last rung of the college's ladder, and it goes to the gates. I have known for some time where the ladder ended; I did not know when. That is the college's usual relationship with dates, as you will have noticed. Come back to me here when the eight are dead.
progress: Eight glass drakes, cleared from the ground before the Capital's gate in the Burned Land, between the Last Camp and the walls. Come back to the college when it is done.
complete: Eight. The ground before the gates is clear enough to carry a stretcher across without the bearers being bitten, which is the whole of what I asked. Now the fort: the thing that has been burning people on that ridge for three hundred years. Speak to me again.

g_whm_50b.name: Three Centuries of Burns

objective.label: Put down the Beacon-Keeper at the top of the Beacon Fort

g_whm_50b.desc: The Beacon-Keeper at the top of the Beacon Fort, on the melt ridge in the east of the Burned Land, has kept the beacon lit since the night the empire vanished, and every burn it gives is three hundred years old. Dean Fairlie wants it put down and the fort dark. Take a party.
offer: Warden Liss, who keeps our infirmary logs, has asked for the wisps in the Beacon Fort put out; I am asking for the thing that lit them. The Beacon Fort is the empire's signal fort on the melt ridge, in the east of the Burned Land. At the top of it is the Beacon-Keeper, the thing that lit the beacon on the night the empire vanished and has kept it burning ever since, and every burn it gives is three hundred years old. I have treated every one of them.
Put it down. Take a party up the Beacon Stair to the Beacon Chamber; the Keeper blinds, as the choristers did, and you have the eye-salve, so keep it in your hand.

I want that fort dark. The courts' wounded have been coming to me from that ridge since before I took the Dean's chair, and I would like to retire the column in the log that is headed with its name. Come back to the college when the beacon is out.
progress: The Beacon-Keeper, in the Beacon Chamber at the top of the Beacon Fort on the melt ridge. Take a party and the eye-salve; it blinds. Come back to the college when the fort is dark.
complete: Dark. The fort is dark for the first time in three hundred years, and the column headed with its name is closed. I have written today's date in the log beside it, which you will appreciate is not something this college does lightly; we have a history with dates.
One thing is left. It stands before the Capital's gates, and it has been waiting for us, for Moonmere, by name. Speak to me again and I will tell you what it is.

g_whm_50c.name: Daybreak

objective.label: Put down the Sealing Clerk before the Capital's gate in the Burned Land

g_whm_50c.desc: A household sentinel, the Sealing Clerk, has stood before the Capital's gates since the night the empire vanished, holding Moonmere's copy of the sealing order and waiting for someone from the academy to sign for it. For three hundred years nobody could come; the gate has been open for weeks. Dean Fairlie wants it put down and the order brought to her to sign. Take a party.
offer: There is a clerk before the gates. A household sentinel, the Sealing Clerk, holding a sealed order with the academy's name on the cover. It is Moonmere's copy of the empire's sealing order, the same instruction the courts found in the Bell Tower, 'Seal it behind us', written the night before the household left. It has stood there since that night waiting for someone from Moonmere to come and sign for it.
For three hundred years nobody could; the border was shut. That excuse ran out the morning the gate opened, and the college has gone on using it for weeks. Observe who I am sending.
Take a party to the ground before the Capital's gates in the Burned Land and put the Clerk down. It will not let go of the order while it stands. When it falls, bring the order to me.

I will read the order, every line of it. Liss has told half a sentence about that night for as long as I have known her, and stopped; when I have read it, the college will have told the whole sentence at last. The cloth for this rung is called Daybreak. I had it woven the year I took the chair, and I did not expect to give it away.
progress: The Sealing Clerk, before the Capital's gates in the Burned Land. Take a party; put it down and bring the sealed order it holds back to me at the college.
complete: It let go. I have the order. The date on it is the date the college keeps in my desk, the night before the household left; and the signature line, where someone from Moonmere was meant to sign that the academy had received its instruction, is blank. I have signed it. Three hundred years late, in ink.

Daybreak: all four pieces, and the college's title with them. You are the one who mended the night. Liss has always said that what they needed mending that night was elsewhere, and stopped there. Here is the rest of the sentence: it was here. It was us. Go and wear it where someone can see.

g_blm_10.name: Keep the Shelf's Fire

objective.label: Bring Reader Thrale 3 dim embers from the mist sprites on the Moonmere Shores

g_blm_10.desc: Reader Corin Thrale of the Burned Shelf, the academy's college of fire, keeps a lamp that has burned since the fire the college is named for. It burns dim embers, which the mist sprites on the Moonmere Shores carry. Bring three before the wick runs down.
offer: I am Reader Corin Thrale. This is the Burned Shelf, the academy's college of fire, named for the week after the empire vanished, three hundred years ago, when the academy burned its own astronomy section in this room and then began teaching fire in the ashes. Master Corvo teaches the fire. I teach what it was for. You want to be a Black Mage of this shelf, so you start with the lamp.

The lamp on this shelf was lit the week of the fire and has not gone out since. That is not a miracle; it is a rota, and first-years are on it, and you are now a first-year. It burns dim embers, the kind the mist sprites carry about with them on the Moonmere Shores, across the causeway, for reasons nobody has published. Bring me three, before the wick notices it is low.
There is a set of robes in it. Emberstudy black, first-year issue. The pockets are for embers; do not put anything else in them.
progress: Three dim embers, from the mist sprites on the Moonmere Shores across the causeway. Bring them back to the shelf; the wick is noticing.
complete: Three. Into the lamp; watch it take. There: a fire fed by something that was carrying fire without knowing it. That is the first lesson, and most people never notice they have had it.

The Emberstudy set: hat, robe, trousers, shoes. Black for soot, not for drama. You are a Black Mage of the Burned Shelf now, which means the fire is your job and the reading is your homework. The homework is on this shelf. Most of it is burned.

g_blm_20a.name: The Dance Goes On

objective.label: Burn 10 ballroom guests in the Sunken Ballroom under the Summer Lakes

g_blm_20a.desc: In the Sunken Ballroom under the Summer Lakes, the household's guests are still dancing, three hundred years after the night the lamps all leaned one way. Reader Thrale wants ten of them burned, and the lamps noted.
offer: The Border Gate is open and the shelf has a reading list for the other side. First: the Sunken Ballroom, the dance hall of the household, as the sentinels call the empire's people, under the Summer Lakes. Go in by the Ballroom Stair on the west mere's shore. On the night the empire vanished, every lamp in that room leaned one way, all at once, and the music did not stop. The guests are still dancing. That is a footnote I would rather were not true, and it is.

Burn ten of the guests. Fire is what the shelf teaches and what they will answer to. And mind the lamps while you work: they lean the way the household went, and so will you, if you watch them too long. Note which way they lean. That is the homework.
Come back to the shelf with the count.
progress: Ten ballroom guests burned, in the Sunken Ballroom under the Summer Lakes; in by the Ballroom Stair on the west shore. Do not watch the lamps. Come back to the shelf.
complete: Ten. The music went on while you worked, I expect. It always does. Which way did they lean? All of them, the same way, and nobody in three hundred years has set one straight. I have written that down and I will not be publishing what I think it means. There is a second name on the ballroom's dance card, and it belongs to the one who kept those lamps lit. Speak to me again about him.

g_blm_20b.name: The Lamps Leaned

objective.label: Fell the Master of Ceremonies in the Sunken Ballroom

g_blm_20b.desc: The Master of Ceremonies in the Sunken Ballroom kept the lamps lit on the night they all leaned one way, and keeps them still. Reader Thrale wants him felled and the music stopped. Take a party.
offer: The Master of Ceremonies. He ran the ballroom's evening, and when every lamp in the room leaned one way on the night the empire vanished, he kept them lit. He is still keeping them, three hundred years on, on the ballroom floor, announcing each dance for people who are not dancing so much as continuing. I want to know what he was reading by. A lamp kept lit through that night was kept lit for a reason, and the reason is the shelf's subject.

Take a party; he is not a lesson for one, and the guests will keep coming while he announces the dances. Go down by the Ballroom Stair on the west mere's shore, round through the salons and the Mirror Foyer to the ballroom floor, the Interrupted Waltz, and put him down there.
Then come back to the shelf. The Cinderweave set is yours when the music stops.
progress: The Master of Ceremonies, on the floor of the Sunken Ballroom under the Summer Lakes. Take a party. Come back to the shelf when the music has stopped.
complete: The music stopped. Somewhere under the lakes it is quiet for the first time in three hundred years, and nobody but the shelf will write that down. What he was reading by, he took with him. I have a theory. I will not publish it.
Cinderweave, all four pieces. Second-year black. The ballroom's lamp oil is in the dye, which I was not supposed to tell you.

g_blm_30a.name: The Stokers' Irons

objective.label: Bring Reader Thrale 6 stoker's irons from the furnace stokers in the Furnace Hall

g_blm_30a.desc: The furnaces in the Furnace Hall under the Glassworks have not gone out in three centuries. Reader Thrale wants six stoker's irons from the furnace stokers there: the only tools that have touched that fire and not burned.
offer: The Furnace Hall, under the Glassworks, the glass desert in the interior. The furnaces there were lit before the empire left and have not gone out since; the sentinels are still stoking them, and still turning out window panes for the capital, as you will know if you have walked the racking yard. Corvo calls a fire that old a lesson. I call it the advanced class, and the fee is paid in iron.

The furnace stokers still carry their irons, the long rods they rake the fire with. Bring me six. They are the only tools in the world that have touched that fire for three hundred years and not burned, and I want to know why; the shelf has theories, and theories want evidence on the bench.
Go down into the Furnace Hall, take the irons off the stokers, and bring them back to the shelf.
progress: Six stoker's irons, from the furnace stokers in the Furnace Hall under the Glassworks. Bring them to the shelf.
complete: Six. Warm, still. Three hundred years and warm, every one of them, and not a scorch on the metal. Whatever is in that fire is not only heat. On the shelf they go, beside the books they should have been used on. The Hall is not finished with us; speak to me again.

g_blm_30b.name: Sparks Loose in the Hall

objective.label: Burn 8 ash sprites off the furnace row in the Furnace Hall

g_blm_30b.desc: Ash sprites are coming off the furnace row in the Furnace Hall under the Glassworks, and Reader Thrale says each one is a page of something that got out of the fire. Burn eight of them.
offer: The Furnace Hall is throwing sparks. Ash sprites, coming off the furnace row, and they are not sparks: each one is a page of something that went into that fire and got out again, still burning. The Cinder Abbot, the thing that keeps the furnace's time down there, is reading them as they rise. I would rather the shelf read them first, and the shelf cannot, so burn them.

Eight ash sprites, off the furnace row. Fire against fire. You will find it does not work the way the first-year text says; a thing made of fire does not mind more of it unless you put the heat somewhere it has not been. The second-year text explains that. It is on this shelf, burned, so you will have to learn it on the row.
Come back to the shelf with the count.
progress: Eight ash sprites burned, off the furnace row in the Furnace Hall under the Glassworks. Come back to the shelf.
complete: Eight. The row is quieter; fewer pages getting loose. The Master of the Furnace is not quieter. He is the one who has been stoking for three centuries, and he keeps a room of his own down there where fire happened too, if Corvo will lend the phrase. Speak to me again about him.

g_blm_30c.name: The Room Where It Happened

objective.label: Fell the Master of the Furnace in the Furnace Hall

g_blm_30c.desc: The Master of the Furnace has stoked the fire in the Furnace Hall since the night the empire left and has never stopped. Reader Thrale wants him felled and the fire brought back under a syllabus. Take a party.
offer: The Master of the Furnace. Three centuries at the stoking: he was at the fire the night the household left, and he has not stopped, and the window panes crated for the capital come out of his heat. Corvo teaches fire in the room where it happened, meaning this one. The Master kept a fire in a room of his own, the same night, and kept it, and I want to know what he thinks happened. He will not tell you. His fire will.

Take a party into the Furnace Hall; he keeps the Furnace Master's Chamber at the far end, past the Pane Hall, and the stokers will not leave him. Put him down and bring the fire back under a syllabus.
Then come back to the shelf. The Starfall set is in the drawer; it has been waiting longer than you have been alive.
progress: The Master of the Furnace, in the Furnace Master's Chamber at the far end of the Furnace Hall, past the Pane Hall, under the Glassworks. Take a party. Come back to the shelf when he is down.
complete: Done. The furnace is still lit; I did not expect otherwise, and the sentinels will go on stoking it for whoever is coming. The one who kept it is not, and that is what the shelf is for: to say which fires were kept, and by whom, and why.
Starfall, all four pieces. Third-year black. The old name for the set is on this shelf, burned, with the rest of the astronomy. Wear it and keep reading.

g_blm_40a.name: Three Sightings

objective.label: Sight the burn at the glassed orchard, the melt ridge and the old road cut on the Burned Land

g_blm_40a.desc: Junn has read the fire line round the Capital; Reader Thrale wants the Burned Shelf's own reading. Stand at the three survey posts in the Burned Land, the glassed orchard in the west, the melt ridge in the east and the old road cut in the south, and record which way the melt runs.
offer: The fire line: the ring of burned ground round the Capital, out in the Burned Land, where the one flash from the city stopped. Junn has read it with her survey glass and written her report, and I have read Junn's report, and it is good. Now I want the shelf's own reading. A Black Mage, standing on the ground, with no survey glass between you and the burn.

There are three survey posts. The Orchard Sighting, at the glassed orchard in the west. The Ridge Sighting, at the foot of the melt ridge in the east. The Road Cut Sighting, at the mouth of the old road cut in the south. Stand at each, sight along the burn, and record which way the ripples in the melt run.

They run outward. I am telling you that now so you understand why it matters: I want you to have found it yourself, with your own eyes, so that when the shelf says it, one of us has seen it. Come back to the shelf when all three are recorded.
progress: Three survey posts in the Burned Land: the Orchard Sighting in the west, the Ridge Sighting in the east, the Road Cut Sighting in the south. Sight along the burn at each and record which way the melt runs.
complete: Outward, three times. One flash, from the centre, in a single morning, and the land melted away from it like water from a dropped stone. That is not a fire that burned; a fire that burns wanders, and feeds, and goes where the wind sends it. That is a fire that was used: it went one way, all at once, and stopped where it stopped. The shelf teaches the difference, and now so do you. Speak to me again; the drakes out there have learned it too.

g_blm_40b.name: Glass Breath

objective.label: Burn 8 glass drakes on the Burned Land

g_blm_40b.desc: The glass drakes on the fire line in the Burned Land breathe glass, not fire. Reader Thrale wants eight burned before they breathe.
offer: The drakes on the fire line breathe glass. Not fire; glass, the same melt the ground is made of. A drake breathes what it was raised in, and these were raised in the three hundred years after the flash, on ground that is still hot under the crust. Something taught them, and what taught them is the thing I teach, three hundred years further on.

Burn eight glass drakes. They are all over the Burned Land, thickest along the fire line and out to the east towards the melt ridge. Burn them before they breathe; a drake that has drawn breath is already a problem. And if you do take a lungful of what they make, you will know what the orchard knew the morning it turned to glass. I do not recommend the lesson.
Come back to the shelf with the count.
progress: Eight glass drakes burned, on the Burned Land; they keep to the fire line and the ground east towards the melt ridge. Burn them before they breathe. Come back to the shelf.
complete: Eight. Glass breath, at the end of a fire that left glass behind. The land is still teaching the lesson that was taught to it, to anything that lives on it long enough. The Glassed Stag is next; it was in the room, so to speak, when the lesson was first given. Speak to me again.

g_blm_40c.name: Voidglass

objective.label: Fell the Glassed Stag at the glassed orchard on the Burned Land

g_blm_40c.desc: The Glassed Stag stood in the glassed orchard when the flash came and was turned to glass where it was; it still walks the Glassed Orchard, in the north-west of the Burned Land. Reader Thrale wants it felled where it stands. Take a party.
offer: The Glassed Stag. It was in the Glassed Orchard, in the north-west of the Burned Land, when the flash came out of the capital, and the flash turned it to glass where it was, mid-stride, facing away from the city.

Junn's report says it was running. I read the same stride and say it did not run: it has walked that orchard for three hundred years, glass all through, and it has never once left it. I have a theory about why it stayed. The theory is on this shelf, burned.
Take a party and fell it where it stands, among the glass trees. It hits hard, and it is heavier than it looks; the survey teams in the Last Camp's hospital will tell you so.
The Voidglass set is yours after. It is what the academy wore the week it burned its own section; I have had it cleaned.
progress: The Glassed Stag, in the Glassed Orchard in the north-west of the Burned Land. Take a party. Fell it where it stands and come back to the shelf.
complete: The stag. Glass all through, and whatever it was facing that morning, with its back to the city, it faced for a reason; a thing that is turned to glass keeps its last decision. We will not be publishing the reason.
Voidglass, all four pieces. No, I will not say which void. Put it on. The shelf has one more thing to read, and it is behind a fort door on the melt ridge. Speak to me again when you are ready.

g_blm_50a.name: As Instructed

objective.label: Read the last entry of the beacon log in the Beacon Fort's raised chamber

g_blm_50a.desc: The Beacon Fort on the melt ridge in the east of the Burned Land kept a log, and its last entry says the beacon was lit at the signal and faced outward, as instructed. Reader Thrale wants the Burned Shelf's own Black Mage to read that page on the spot, in the raised chamber at the top of the fort.
offer: The Beacon Fort, the empire's signal fort on the melt ridge in the east of the Burned Land. It kept a log, and the last entry, as it has been reported to the shelf, says this: the household departs at the appointed hour; lit at the signal; the fire faced outward, as instructed. As instructed. Somebody wrote the instruction. That is the whole of the shelf's subject in two words, and I will not have it second-hand.

Go into the Beacon Fort, up through the guard hall, past the cinder choristers and the sentinels on the Beacon Stair, to the raised chamber at the top, the Beacon Chamber. The Beacon Log is on its stand there. Read the last entry yourself and take the page. Do not take the Keeper's word for what it says; a thing that followed an instruction is not a witness to it.
Come back to the shelf and tell me the last entry, word for word.
progress: The Beacon Log, on its stand in the raised chamber at the top of the Beacon Fort on the melt ridge. Read the last entry yourself and take the page. Come back to the shelf.
complete: The household departs at the appointed hour. Lit at the signal. The fire faced outward, as instructed. And under it, a fourth: the fire is ours. The whole of the fire line is in the first three, in a calm hand: a time that was fixed in advance, a signal that was given, and a fire that was aimed away from the city, by order. The fourth only says whose it was. Now go and ask the one who followed the instruction. Speak to me again.

g_blm_50b.name: Lit at the Signal

objective.label: Fell the Beacon-Keeper at the top of the Beacon Fort

g_blm_50b.desc: The Beacon-Keeper lit the beacon at the signal on the night the empire left, and has kept it burning since in case the signal comes again. Reader Thrale wants it felled and the beacon put out. Take a party.
offer: The Beacon-Keeper lit it. At the signal, facing outward, as instructed, on the night the household left; and it has kept the beacon lit for three hundred years since, in case the signal comes again. It will not. That signal was given once, for the leaving, and nobody is left to give it again. The shelf is sure of that, and the shelf is sure of very little.

Take a party up the Beacon Stair to the Beacon Chamber at the top of the fort. Put the Keeper down, and then put the beacon itself out. The second part is the point. A Black Mage who cannot put a fire out has read half the book.
Come back to the shelf when the ridge is dark.
progress: The Beacon-Keeper, in the Beacon Chamber at the top of the Beacon Fort on the melt ridge. Take a party; put it down and put the beacon out. Come back to the shelf.
complete: Out. The beacon dark, for the first time in three hundred years; the melt ridge will be black tonight, and the Provost will want a memorandum explaining why the academy put out an imperial signal fire. She will not get one. The shelf does not write memoranda about its own subject.
One more thing stands between the shelf and the Capital's gates, and it has been holding the instruction all this time, with the academy's name on it. Speak to me again.

g_blm_50c.name: What Stands at the Gates

objective.label: Fell the Sealing Clerk before the Capital's gates on the Burned Land

g_blm_50c.desc: A household sentinel, the Sealing Clerk, has stood before the Capital's gates since the night the empire left, holding Moonmere's copy of the sealing order and waiting for someone from the academy to sign for it. The academy knew the date and never came. Reader Thrale wants it felled. Take a party.
offer: Before the Capital's gates, in the Burned Land, stands a household clerk: the Sealing Clerk, a sentinel, with a sealed order under its arm and the academy's name on the cover. The order is Moonmere's copy of the empire's sealing order: the same instruction the courts found in the Bell Tower, 'Seal it behind us', written the night before the household left. The Clerk has stood there since that night, waiting for someone from Moonmere to come and sign that the academy received it.

The academy knew the date, from the morning after, and did not come. Not when the gate opened; not since. That is the whole of the sealing order as far as the shelf is concerned, and the shelf has read every other page. I will not ask what was on the cover, and I will not read what is under it. The shelf reads fires, not signatures.
Take a party to the ground before the gates and put the Clerk down. The Astral set is yours after, and a name the shelf will keep.
progress: The Sealing Clerk, before the Capital's gates in the Burned Land, on the ground between the Last Camp and the walls. Take a party. Come back to the shelf when it is down.
complete: Quiet, before the gates. The order is on the ground where the Clerk dropped it, unsigned; whether anyone from the academy signs it is not a question for this shelf, and I have left it there for whoever decides it is theirs. You read the instruction, you put out the beacon that followed it, and you put down the thing that held it. The shelf's ladder ends there, at the gates, where the instruction started.

Astral, all four pieces. The master's black; the shelf has not given it out since the fire. The title is yours too: the one who read the instruction. The rest of the academy will pretend not to know what it means. Let them.

g_blm_34.name: Ember-Glass Drakes

objective.label: Burn 6 cragmaw drakes on the Border Wall for Junn at the Embassy

g_blm_34.desc: Junn, at the courts' embassy camp on the Border Wall, is holding a hat the Burned Shelf sent with its last dispatch, to be worn only by a Black Mage who has burned a cragmaw drake. Burn six on the wall.
offer: You are from the Burned Shelf; I can tell by the black. Good; I need a Black Mage, and my collar is crooked, and neither of those is in the report I am supposed to be writing. I am Junn, Moonmere's archivist, if we have not been introduced in the field, and this is the embassy's camp on the Border Wall.
The cragmaw drakes on the wall carry ember-glass in their crops: it sits in them, warm, and makes them bad-tempered. They come at the camp's edges along the rampart road. Burn six of them.

The shelf sent a hat with its last dispatch, a Starfall Waymark piece, with a note saying that only a Black Mage who has burned a drake on this wall gets to wear it. I am the courier, not the author. Come back to me here when the six are done.
progress: Six cragmaw drakes, burned on the Border Wall along the rampart road near the embassy's camp. Come back to Junn at the camp.
complete: Six. Thank you. The hat, as per the shelf's note. I read the note twice, which is my job, and it still says Black Mage, so it is yours. Put it on before the sentinels see you without it; the Herald up at the Great Watchtower reports everything, and I would rather it reported the academy properly dressed.

g_blm_37.name: Ember Shards

objective.label: Bring Junn 6 ember shards from the cinder hounds, ember slimes and glass drakes of the Burned Land

g_blm_37.desc: At the fire line in the Burned Land, Junn is collecting a sample of the melt for the Burned Shelf: six ember shards, carried off the melt ridge by the cinder hounds, ember slimes and glass drakes. A pair of shoes came with the request.
offer: The melt is full of ember shards: pieces of the ground that went to glass in the flash and have not finished cooling, three hundred years on. The cinder hounds and the ember slimes carry them off the melt ridge in the east, and the glass drakes along the fire line carry them too. I want six.

The Burned Shelf wants a sample it did not take itself, with a Black Mage's hands on it, so that the sample is the shelf's and not mine. A pair of shoes came with the request, Starfall Waymark, meant for ash. Bring the shards whole; do not break them.
I am writing down which way each one cooled, from the hot face to the cold, and I will not say why yet, which the shelf will recognise as its own habit. Bring them to me here at the fire line.
progress: Six ember shards, whole. The cinder hounds and ember slimes carry them off the melt ridge in the east of the Burned Land, and the glass drakes along the fire line. Bring them to Junn at the fire line.
complete: Six. All six cooled outward: hot face towards the city, cold face away, every one, the same as the ripples and the trunks. I wrote that down and then I underlined it, which is as far as my feelings go in a report. The shoes are yours; the shelf wrapped them in a page of something I was careful not to read.
